Diagnosis:
Evaluation of this adult with a history of pediatric Tetralogy of Fallot repair reveals severe right ventricular dilation (RVEDVI of 155 mL/m²) and severe, free pulmonary regurgitation with a regurgitant fraction of 46% calculated via phase-contrast flow analysis. The right ventricular ejection fraction is mildly reduced at 44%. The patch closure of the ventricular septal defect (VSD) appears intact with no residual shunt.

Impression: Status post remote repair of Tetralogy of Fallot, now demonstrating severe pulmonary regurgitation and severe right ventricular dilation. This profile is key in determining timing for pulmonary valve replacement.

Cardiac MRI reveals severe bi-ventricular dilation with diffuse, global hypokinesis. The left ventricular end-diastolic volume is significantly increased, and the left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) is severely depressed at 22%. Mid-wall late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) is observed in the basal to mid-interventricular septum, consistent with a non-ischemic etiology. Moderate mitral and tricuspid regurgitation are present, secondary to annular dilation.

Impression: Dilated cardiomyopathy with severe global LV systolic dysfunction and mid-wall fibrosis, highly suggestive of a non-ischemic or idiopathic process.

Brain MRI with susceptibility-weighted imaging (SWI) demonstrates numerous small foci of signal void (microhemorrhages) scattered throughout the cortical and subcortical regions of both cerebral hemispheres, sparing the basal ganglia and brainstem. There is also prominent periventricular leukoaraiosis and generalized cerebral atrophy, appropriate for age. No acute lobar hemorrhage or acute ischemic stroke is noted.

Impression: Extensive cerebral microhemorrhages in a lobar distribution, classic for severe cerebral amyloid angiopathy (CAA). Clinical monitoring for cognitive decline and avoidance of anti-thrombotic therapy where possible is recommended.

MRI of the brain demonstrates a focal, hyperacute-to-acute intraparenchymal hematoma centered within the left basal ganglia/putamen, measuring 2.6 x 2.1 cm. The lesion is surrounded by a moderate rim of vasogenic edema on FLAIR imaging and displays hypointensity on susceptibility-weighted imaging (SWI) consistent with intracellular deoxyhemoglobin. There is mild mass effect on the left lateral ventricle but no herniation or midline shift.

Impression: Acute left basal ganglia intraparenchymal hemorrhage with surrounding vasogenic edema. The anatomical location is highly characteristic of hypertensive hemorrhage.

Multiplanar, multisequence brain MRI was performed. The brain parenchyma is normal in appearance, with no focal areas of signal abnormality, acute ischemia, hemorrhage, or abnormal post-contrast enhancement. The ventricles and basal cisterns are normal in caliber. The cranial nerves and internal acoustic canals are normal.

Impression: Normal magnetic resonance imaging of the brain. No structural correlates identified for the patient's headaches.

Fetal MRI at 34 weeks gestation demonstrates borderline isolated left ventriculomegaly. The left lateral ventricle atrium measures 10.5 mm, whereas the right lateral ventricle atrium measures 8.9 mm. Cortical plate development, gyration, and sulcation are entirely normal for 34 weeks. The midline structures, including the corpus callosum, are intact and without deviation.

Impression: Mild, isolated left lateral ventriculomegaly. No other intracranial anomalies or markers of syndromic pathology are observed.

Magnetic resonance imaging of the brain with multiplanar and multisequence protocols shows normal intracranial architecture. The ventricles and cortical sulci are within normal limits for the patient's age. No focal areas of ischemic stroke, mass effect, or pathological parenchymal enhancement are visualized.

Impression: Unremarkable and normal brain MRI. No evidence of major neurological disease process or acute structural abnormality.

Brain MRI was obtained utilizing standard protocols including DWI, FLAIR, T2, and pre/post-contrast T1 sequences. No areas of restricted diffusion are identified to suggest acute ischemia. The cerebral and cerebellar parenchymal signals are unremarkable, and there is no intracranial mass lesion or midline shift. The ventricles and extra-axial spaces are normal for age.

Impression: Normal brain MRI with no evidence of acute infarction, hemorrhage, mass lesion, or abnormal enhancement.

Multisequence, multiplanar MR imaging of the brain was obtained without intravenous contrast. The cerebral parenchyma, brainstem, and cerebellum show normal signal characteristics throughout. The ventricles, sulci, and cisterns are within normal anatomical limits. No restricted diffusion, acute infarct, or extra-axial collection is demonstrated.

Impression: Unremarkable MRI of the brain with no structural or acute intracranial pathology identified.

Fetal MRI at 21 weeks gestation reveals a bony defect in the midline occipital bone. There is a herniation of a meningeal sac containing a small amount of dysplastic cerebellar tissue, consistent with an occipital encephalocele. The lateral ventricles are dilated, with the atrium measuring 11.2 mm, showing early-stage sulcation appropriate for 21 weeks.

Impression: Occipital encephalocele with associated ventriculomegaly. Recommend high-risk obstetrical and pediatric neurosurgical consultation.

Fetal MRI at 25 weeks gestation demonstrates an occipital encephalocele. A midline bony defect in the occipital bone is identified, with herniation of dysplastic cerebellar tissue and cerebrospinal fluid into a large sac. This has resulted in microcephaly with a compressed posterior fossa. Supratentorial ventriculomegaly is noted, with lateral ventricular atria measuring 11.0 mm. Cortical sulcation is appropriate for 25 weeks.

Impression: Occipital encephalocele containing herniated brain tissue with microcephaly and associated mild ventriculomegaly at 25 weeks gestation.

Cardiac MRI reveals a heavily calcified and thickened aortic valve with restricted leaflet excursion. Planimetry of the aortic valve orifice yields a severe narrowing with a valve area of 0.8 cm². There is concentric left ventricular hypertrophy (septal thickness 15 mm, posterior wall 14 mm) with preserved systolic function (ejection fraction of 65%). Phase-contrast flow quantification demonstrates a peak velocity across the aortic valve of 4.2 m/s, consistent with severe aortic stenosis.

Impression: Severe valvular aortic stenosis with secondary concentric left ventricular hypertrophy and preserved ejection fraction. No evidence of myocardial infarction on late enhancement.

Fetal MRI at 29 weeks gestation demonstrates severe bilateral renal agenesis. No renal parenchymal tissue or renal arteries are identified in either renal fossa or within the pelvis. This is associated with profound oligohydramnios, limiting optimal fetal visualization. The fetal chest is small and bell-shaped, consistent with severe pulmonary hypoplasia secondary to the lack of amniotic fluid.

Fetal brain imaging, though restricted by positioning, shows acceptable ventricular size (6.5 mm) and sulcul pattern for gestational age. Impression: Bilateral renal agenesis with secondary severe oligohydramnios and pulmonary hypoplasia (Potter's sequence). This finding represents a highly lethal prognosis.

Fetal MRI performed at 24 weeks gestation demonstrates normal, age-appropriate intracranial structures. The cerebral hemispheres show expected early opercularization and smooth gyration patterns suitable for this gestational stage. The lateral ventricles are symmetric, with the atrial diameter measuring 6.1 mm. The midline structures, including the corpus callosum and septum pellucidum, are clearly visualized and structurally intact. The posterior fossa shows a normal cerebellar vermis and fourth ventricle.

Impression: Normal fetal brain MRI at 24 weeks gestation with no structural abnormalities or ventriculomegaly identified.

MR evaluation of the brain was performed to assess mild cognitive decline. The scan reveals generalized age-appropriate cerebral cortical volume loss with mild compensatory prominence of the sulci and ventricles. There is no focal lobar atrophy (such as disproportionate hippocampal atrophy), no acute infarcts, and no intracranial mass lesions. The deep white matter shows only minimal, non-specific T2/FLAIR hyperintensities.

Impression: Age-appropriate brain morphology without evidence of focal lobar atrophy, acute ischemia, or other structural abnormalities to explain cognitive decline.

Fetal MRI at 23 weeks gestation demonstrates complete absence of both fetal kidneys in the renal fossae. The adrenal glands are lying flat ("laying down" sign) in the empty renal fossae. There is severe, near-complete oligohydramnios, which limits the resolution of some musculoskeletal structures. Fetal lung volumes are severely reduced, consistent with early pulmonary hypoplasia due to anhydramnios.

Intracranial structures are poorly visualized but lateral ventricles appear normal in size (atrium 6.0 mm). Impression: Bilateral renal agenesis with secondary severe oligohydramnios and early pulmonary hypoplasia, representing Potter sequence.

Cardiac MRI shows completely normal biventricular size, volume, and systolic function. The left ventricular ejection fraction is calculated at 60%, and the right ventricular ejection fraction is 58%. No regional wall motion abnormalities, valvular dysfunction, or abnormal myocardial enhancement on late gadolinium sequences are observed.

Impression: Normal cardiac MRI study. Normal chamber volumes and preserved biventricular systolic function with no myocardial tissue abnormalities.

Cardiac MRI and MR angiography of the thoracic aorta demonstrate a focal, severe narrowing of the proximal descending thoracic aorta just distal to the origin of the left subclavian artery. The minimum lumen diameter at the coarctation site measures 6 mm. Prominent, dilated internal mammary and intercostal collateral arteries are visualized bypassing the obstruction. There is associated concentric left ventricular hypertrophy (septal wall thickness 14 mm) as a response to chronic pressure overload, but LVEF remains preserved at 60%.

Impression: Classic post-ductal coarctation of the aorta with extensive collateral vascular network and moderate concentric left ventricular hypertrophy.

Brain MRI with internal auditory canal (IAC) protocol demonstrates a well-defined, intensely enhancing mass centered within the left cerebellopontine angle, measuring 1.8 x 1.4 cm. The mass extends into and mildly widens the internal auditory canal. There is early compressive effect on the adjacent left cerebellar peduncle, but the fourth ventricle remains patent.

Impression: Left acoustic neuroma (vestibular schwannoma) with extension into the internal auditory canal. Mild adjacent mass effect is identified without secondary hydrocephalus.

MR imaging of the brain demonstrates a large, heterogeneously enhancing intra-axial mass in the right temporal lobe measuring approximately 4.8 x 4.2 x 3.9 cm. The mass exhibits central non-enhancing areas consistent with necrosis, surrounded by a thick, irregular rim of enhancement. There is extensive surrounding vasogenic edema resulting in subtotal compression of the right lateral ventricle and a 7 mm leftward midline shift.

Impression: Large necrotic, ring-enhancing intra-axial right temporal lobe mass, highly suspicious for glioblastoma multiforme (GBM). Given the substantial mass effect and midline shift, urgent neurosurgical consultation and dexamethasone therapy are recommended.

MR imaging of the sella turcica demonstrates a well-defined, enhancing mass arising from the adenohypophysis, measuring 1.4 x 1.2 cm. The lesion extends superiorly into the suprasellar cistern, causing mild upward displacement and compression of the optic chiasm. The cavernous sinuses are bilaterally intact, with no evidence of vascular invasion.

Impression: Pituitary macroadenoma with suprasellar extension and mild compression of the optic chiasm. Recommend visual field testing and endocrine correlation.

Cardiac MRI evaluates a patient with a history of surgically repaired Tetralogy of Fallot. There is severe dilatation of the right ventricle (EDV indexed to BSA is 155 mL/m2) with moderate right ventricular systolic dysfunction (RVEF 38%). Phase-contrast flow analysis of the main pulmonary artery demonstrates a severe pulmonary regurgitant fraction of 44%. Mild residual right ventricular outflow tract obstruction is observed, but no residual ventricular septal defect.

Impression: Late post-repair Tetralogy of Fallot status showing severe pulmonary regurgitation and significant secondary right ventricular dilation with moderate right ventricular dysfunction.

Cardiac MRI was performed to investigate occasional palpitations. Left and right ventricular chamber sizes, wall thicknesses, and systolic parameters are within normal limits. Calculated left ventricular ejection fraction is 58% and right ventricular ejection fraction is 56%. No late gadolinium enhancement or abnormal myocardial signal intensity is observed.

Impression: Normal cardiac MRI study. There is no evidence of structural heart disease, myocardial edema, or fibrotic scar.

Cardiac MRI evaluates myocardial viability in the setting of coronary artery disease. There is a large transmural scar in the apex and apical anterior wall, demonstrating near 100% late gadolinium enhancement thickness. No significant contractile reserve is demonstrated in these regions on low-dose dobutamine stress imaging. Left ventricular volume is increased, and the global ejection fraction is calculated at 35%.

Impression: Apical and apical anterior myocardial infarction with transmural scar and no functional viability. Global left ventricular systolic function is moderately-to-severely reduced.

There is a crescentic, extra-axial fluid collection along the left frontoparietal convexity measuring up to 1.8 cm in maximal thickness. The collection exhibits heterogeneous signal on T1 and T2-weighted sequences with internal septations, indicative of chronic subdural hematoma with areas of subacute rebleeding. It exerts moderate mass effect with effacement of adjacent sulci and 5 mm of rightward midline shift.

Impression: Large, chronic-on-acute left subdural hematoma causing moderate mass effect and mass-induced midline shift. Neurosurgical evaluation is recommended.

MR examination of the brain was completed for a patient reporting persistent subjective tinnitus. The brain parenchyma is symmetric with a normal distribution of gray and white matter. The ventricular system, extra-axial spaces, and vascular flow voids are unremarkable. The internal auditory canals, cochlea, and vestibule are normal bilaterally with no evidence of tumor or vascular loop compression.

Impression: Completely normal brain MRI. No structural abnormality, vascular compression, or cerebellopontine angle mass to explain the patient's tinnitus.

Brain MRI with multiplanar sequences demonstrates normal parenchyma, ventricles, and extra-axial spaces. No pathologic contrast enhancement is identified. Intracranial flow voids of main arteries are normal. Mastoid air cells are well-pneumatized and clear.

Impression: Unremarkable MRI of the brain with no acute or chronic pathological findings.

Fetal MRI at 26 weeks gestation demonstrates a classic Dandy-Walker malformation. There is severe hypoplasia of the cerebellar vermis with a large posterior fossa fluid collection that freely communicates with an enlarged fourth ventricle. The tentorium cerebelli and torcular herophili are significantly elevated. There is accompanying supratentorial ventriculomegaly, with lateral ventricular atria measuring 13.0 mm on the right and 12.8 mm on the left. The cerebral cortex shows normal migration patterns.

Impression: Dandy-Walker malformation with associated bilateral ventriculomegaly at 26 weeks gestation. Pediatric neurology and neurosurgery consultations are recommended.

Cardiac MRI shows a heavily calcified, thickened aortic valve with restricted leaflet mobility. Velocity-encoded phase-contrast imaging over the aortic valve demonstrates a peak velocity of 4.2 m/s, consistent with severe aortic stenosis. There is marked concentric left ventricular hypertrophy with a diastolic septal thickness of 1.7 cm. The left ventricular ejection fraction remains preserved at 55%, though there is mild diastolic dysfunction. No transmural scar is noted on LGE.

Impression: Severe calcific aortic stenosis with compensatory concentric left ventricular hypertrophy. There is no evidence of associated ischemic scar, and overall left ventricular systolic performance is preserved.

Fetal MRI at 23 weeks gestation demonstrates a complete absence of amniotic fluid (anhydramnios). There is non-visualization of both kidneys in the renal fossae; the adrenal glands are present but flattened ('lying-down' adrenal sign). The fetal bladder is not visualized, and there is severe crowding of fetal parts. Intracranial structures demonstrate an atrial width of 6.0 mm with normal early cortical sulcation.

Impression: Bilateral renal agenesis associated with anhydramnios. The finding carries a highly guarded prognosis due to predicted severe pulmonary hypoplasia.

The right ventricle is significantly dilated (RVEDVI of 118 mL/m²) with areas of dyskinesis and microaneurysm formation noted along the RV outflow tract and inferior wall. The right ventricular ejection fraction is depressed at 34%. Multiplanar fat-attenuated imaging demonstrates high signal intensity within the RV free wall, suggesting fibrofatty replacement. The left ventricle appears normal in size and function.

Impression: Morphological and functional features are highly suggestive of Arrhythmogenic Right Ventricular Cardiomyopathy (ARVC) based on major Task Force criteria.

MR examination of the brain reveals normal brain morphology. The grey-white matter differentiation is preserved, and there are no abnormal areas of signal intensity within the cerebral hemispheres, brainstem, or cerebellum. The ventricles are normal in size and position. The paranasal sinuses and mastoid air cells are clear.

Impression: Unremarkable MRI of the brain with no acute, structural, or demyelinating abnormalities identified.

Fetal MRI performed at 22 weeks gestation for further evaluation of suspected central nervous system anomalies on ultrasound. The cerebral hemispheres demonstrate normal signal intensity and morphology. The cerebral sulcation and migration patterns are appropriate for 22 weeks of gestation. The lateral ventricles are symmetric and normal in size, with the atrial width measuring 5.8 mm. The corpus callosum is fully visualized and intact. The cerebellum, brainstem, and posterior fossa fluid spaces are unremarkable.

Impression: Normal fetal MRI at 22 weeks gestation. No structural intracranial anomalies or developmental delays identified.

There is a crescent-shaped extra-axial fluid collection along the left cerebral hemisphere, measuring up to 1.2 cm in maximal thickness. The collection is hyperintense on T1-weighted images and heterogeneous on T2/FLAIR, indicating a subacute subdural hematoma. There is substantial mass effect leading to compression of the left lateral ventricle and a 7 mm midline shift to the right.

Impression: Large subacute left-sided subdural hematoma causing significant mass effect and moderate midline shift.

Fetal MRI at 23 weeks gestation demonstrates a lumbosacral neural tube defect with an associated myelomeningocele sac containing herniated neural elements. There is associated Chiari II malformation, characterized by a small posterior fossa, cerebellar crowding ('banana sign'), and frontal bone scalloping ('lemon sign').

The lateral ventricles are mildly dilated, with the atrium measuring 10.5 mm, reflecting mild ventriculomegaly. The cerebral sulcation pattern is normal for this early gestational age. Impression: Open lumbosacral myelomeningocele with characteristic secondary features of Chiari II malformation and mild ventriculomegaly.

Fetal MRI at 31 weeks gestation demonstrates isolated, asymmetric right-sided lateral ventriculomegaly. The right lateral ventricular atrium measures 12.1 mm, whereas the left lateral ventricular atrium is normal at 7.5 mm. There is no evidence of intraventricular hemorrhage, periventricular nodular heterotopia, or aqueductal stenosis. The sulcation and gyration pattern is normal and appropriate for 31 weeks.

The corpus callosum is fully formed. Normal amniotic fluid is present. Impression: Isolated right-sided mild-to-moderate ventriculomegaly. Serial follow-up is recommended.

Fetal MRI at 22 weeks gestation reveals lobar holoprosencephaly. There is incomplete division of the cerebral hemispheres anteriorly, with fusion of the frontal lobes. The septum pellucidum is absent, and there is a dysgenic, hypoplastic corpus callosum. The single, fused frontal horn of the lateral ventricles is dilated, with the posterior atria measuring 12.5 mm.

Cortical sulcation is markedly delayed, showing a smooth cerebral surface abnormal for 22 weeks. Impression: Lobar holoprosencephaly with corpus callosum dysgenesis, ventriculomegaly, and severely delayed cortical sulcation.

A comprehensive cardiac MRI was performed utilizing multiplanar cine and late gadolinium enhancement imaging. Left and right ventricular chamber dimensions and wall thicknesses are well within physiological limits. Left ventricular end-diastolic volume is 125 mL with a stroke volume of 78 mL. No regional wall motion abnormalities or focal thinning are observed. Late gadolinium enhancement imaging demonstrates no myocardial fibrosis, scarring, or infiltration.

Impression: Completely normal cardiovascular magnetic resonance examination. Normal biventricular size and systolic function, with a left ventricular ejection fraction of 62% and right ventricular ejection fraction of 58%.

An MRI of the brain, focused on the internal auditory canals, reveals a well-defined, intensely enhancing mass centered within the left cerebellopontine angle. The mass measures 1.4 x 1.2 cm and extends into the left internal auditory canal, causing mild widening of the porus acusticus. There is minor mass effect on the adjacent brainstem but no hydrocephalus.

Impression: Small, left-sided intracanalicular and extracanalicular cerebellopontine angle mass, highly consistent with a vestibular schwannoma (acoustic neuroma).

Fetal MRI at 26 weeks gestation demonstrates complete agenesis of the corpus callosum. There is a characteristic 'steer-horn' configuration of the lateral ventricles on coronal views, with parallel orientation of the lateral ventricles and dilatation of the occipital horns (colpocephaly). The atrium of the left lateral ventricle measures 13.5 mm, indicating moderate ventriculomegaly.

The third ventricle is dorsally displaced and moderately dilated. Sulcation and gyration are otherwise normal for this gestational age, and the posterior fossa structures are preserved. Impression: Complete agenesis of the corpus callosum with secondary colpocephaly and moderate ventriculomegaly.

Brain MRI demonstrates a large, heterogeneous, ring-enhancing mass centered within the left temporal lobe, measuring approximately 4.5 x 4.2 x 3.8 cm. There is a central necrotic component and extensive surrounding T2/FLAIR hyperintensity consistent with vasogenic edema. Significant mass effect is noted, with compression of the left lateral ventricle and a 6 mm rightward midline shift.

Impression: Large necrotic, ring-enhancing mass in the left temporal lobe, highly suspicious for high-grade glioma (such as glioblastoma multiforme). There is substantial surrounding vasogenic edema and moderate mass effect.

The brain MRI demonstrates normal anatomical development and signal intensity throughout the cerebrum, cerebellum, and brainstem. There are no foci of restricted diffusion, acute hemorrhage, or mass lesions. The ventricles and subarachnoid spaces are normal. Orbits and paranasal sinuses are unremarkable.

Impression: Normal brain MRI with no structural or acute intracranial pathology.

Cardiac MRI shows severe dilation of the left and right ventricles, with marked thinning of the left ventricular free wall. Left ventricular end-diastolic volume is severely increased at 250 mL, and there is global hypokinesis with a calculated left ventricular ejection fraction of 24%. Delayed enhancement imaging reveals no evidence of subendocardial or transmural scar tissue, ruling out ischemic etiology.

Impression: Severe, non-ischemic dilated cardiomyopathy with critical bi-ventricular dysfunction (LVEF 24%, RVEF 30%). No focal scar tissue is identified on late gadolinium enhancement imaging.

Cardiac MRI shows a discrete, focal narrowing of the descending thoracic aorta immediately distal to the origin of the left subclavian artery. There is significant post-stenotic dilation of the distal aorta. Bright blood imaging reveals marked collateral flow through dilated internal mammary and intercostal arteries. The left ventricle shows mild concentric hypertrophy with an ejection fraction of 61%.

Impression: Discrete coarctation of the aorta with prominent collateral circulation and compensatory mild left ventricular hypertrophy. Left ventricular systolic function is preserved.

Fetal MRI at 29 weeks gestation demonstrates a large left-sided congenital diaphragmatic hernia (CDH). Herniated structures within the left hemithorax include the stomach, several loops of small bowel, and a small portion of the left hepatic lobe (liver-up configuration). There is marked mediastinal shift to the right, with significant compression of the heart and contralateral right lung. The observed total lung volume is reduced, with an estimated lung-to-head ratio (LHR) indicative of moderate pulmonary hypoplasia.

Impression: Left-sided congenital diaphragmatic hernia with liver herniation and secondary pulmonary hypoplasia.

MRI of the brain demonstrates normal gray-white matter differentiation. The ventricles, sulci, and basal cisterns are unremarkable for the patient's age. There are no intra- or extra-axial mass lesions, areas of acute ischemia, or hemorrhage. Cranial nerves are intact, and paranasal sinuses are clear.

Impression: Normal MR brain scan. No pathology identified to explain clinical history of progressive non-specific headaches.

Fetal MRI performed at 28 weeks gestation demonstrates normal structural development of the fetus. Intracranial structures are completely intact, with a normal ventricular atrial measurement of 6.0 mm. Sulcation patterns show normal maturation for 28 weeks, including well-defined parieto-occipital and cingulate sulci. Spine, chest, and abdomen show normal development with no fluid collections or masses.

Impression: Completely normal fetal MRI study demonstrating age-appropriate brain development and normal visceral anatomy at 28 weeks.

A large, intra-axial mass lesion is identified in the left temporal lobe measuring approximately 4.8 x 4.2 x 3.9 cm. The mass exhibits heterogenous peripheral enhancement with a large central necrotic component. Extensive surrounding vasogenic edema is present, resulting in partial compression of the left lateral ventricle and a 6 mm rightward midline shift.

Impression: Large, necrotic left temporal intra-axial mass with substantial mass effect and midline shift. Findings are highly suspicious for a primary high-grade glioma, such as glioblastoma multiforme.

MRI of the brain demonstrates unremarkable brain parenchyma without any acute ischemic change, hemorrhage, or mass lesion. The ventricles, sulci, and cisterns are of normal caliber and morphology for the patient's age. The craniocervical junction is normal, and the orbital structures are unremarkable.

Impression: Normal MRI of the brain. No acute or chronic intracranial pathology noted.

Brain MRI with dedicated sellar cuts demonstrates a well-circumscribed, solid mass arising from the pituitary gland measuring 1.6 x 1.4 x 1.3 cm. The lesion causes enlargement of the sella turcica, demonstrates moderate heterogeneous enhancement, and abuts the optic chiasm, causing mild superior displacement and compression. The cavernous sinuses are not grossly invaded.

Impression: Pituitary macroadenoma with suprasellar extension, causing mild compression and elevation of the optic chiasm. Ophthalmology/endocrinology referral recommended.

A cardiac MRI study was conducted to evaluate ischemic heart disease. The images demonstrate apical thinning and dyskinesis of the left ventricular apex and distal septum. Late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) imaging reveals a dense, transmural hyperenhancement zone in the LAD coronary artery territory, occupying approximately 15% of the total left ventricular myocardium.

Impression: Transmural myocardial infarction of the apex and distal septum with associated regional dyskinesis. Left ventricular systolic function is moderately-to-severely reduced with an ejection fraction of 38%.

MR imaging of the brain and sella turcica demonstrates a well-circumscribed, solid mass arising from the adenohypophysis, measuring 1.8 x 1.5 x 1.4 cm. The lesion exhibits moderate, homogeneous enhancement following contrast administration and demonstrates suprasellar extension with mild upward displacement and compression of the optic chiasm. No invasion into the cavernous sinuses is detected; bilateral internal carotid arteries are patent.

Impression: Pituitary macroadenoma with suprasellar extension causing mild mass effect on the optic chiasm. No cavernous sinus invasion is evident.

Brain MRI performed per headache protocol shows no evidence of acute intracranial hemorrhage, territorial infarction, or mass effect. Ventricular size, configuration, and sulcal patterns are entirely unremarkable and normal for the patient's age. The major intracranial arterial flow voids are intact, and there is no evidence of abnormal extra-axial fluid collections.

Visualized orbits, paranasal sinuses, and mastoid air cells are unremarkable. Impression: Completely normal MR examination of the brain with no structural or vascular abnormalities identified.

Cardiac MRI shows a prominent defect in the mid-atrial septum measuring 24 mm, consistent with a secundum-type atrial septal defect (ASD). Phase-contrast flow quantification indicates a significant left-to-right shunt with a Qp/Qs ratio of 1.9:1. There is associated severe dilation of the right atrium and right ventricle, with mild right ventricular hypertrophy and normal pulmonary artery pressure indices.

Impression: Large secundum atrial septal defect with a hemodynamically significant left-to-right shunt and resulting right-sided chamber overload. Cardiothoracic surgery or interventional cardiology evaluation for closure is indicated.

Cardiac MRI demonstrates marked dilation of the left ventricle with severe global hypokinesis. The left ventricular end-diastolic volume (LVEDV) is indexed at 165 mL/m² (total volume 320 mL), and the left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) is severely reduced at 24%. The right ventricle is also mildly dilated with an ejection fraction of 38%. Late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) sequence is negative for any subendocardial or transmural enhancement, arguing against an ischemic etiology.

Impression: Severe non-ischemic dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM) characterized by marked LV dilation, global systolic dysfunction, and lack of ischemic-pattern late gadolinium enhancement.

Cardiac MRI shows standard age-related changes, including mild left ventricular hypertrophy, but no localized pathological thinning or wall motion abnormalities. Normal left ventricular systolic function is observed with an ejection fraction of 59%. T1/T2 mapping sequences show values within physiological limits, and no delayed enhancement is present.

Impression: Unremarkable cardiac MRI. No evidence of myocardial scar, amyloid infiltration, or active inflammatory process. Normal biventricular systolic function.

Cardiac MRI shows a normal cardiac configuration. Left ventricular cavity size is normal (EDV 140 mL) with normal global and regional systolic function (ejection fraction 61%). The right ventricle is normal in size and function (ejection fraction 55%). Pericardium is thin and there is no effusion. T1 and T2 relaxation times of the myocardium are normal, and late gadolinium enhancement sequences are normal.

Impression: Normal cardiac MRI study. No evidence of ischemia, structural heart disease, or pathological myocardial enhancement.

Cardiac MRI demonstrates a moderately dilated left atrium (volume index 52 mL/m2) and a dilated left ventricle with normal global systolic function (LVEF 57%). Dynamic phase-contrast flow-mapping sequences across the mitral valve reveal a prominent regurgitant jet during systole. Quantitation yields a mitral regurgitant volume of 52 mL and a regurgitant fraction of 46%, consistent with severe mitral regurgitation.

No evidence of late gadolinium enhancement in the left ventricular myocardium. Impression: Severe chronic primary mitral regurgitation with secondary dilatation of the left atrium and left ventricle. Left ventricular systolic function is preserved.

Fetal MRI at 33 weeks gestation reveals a dilated cisterna magna (megacisterna magna), measuring 12.8 mm in anteroposterior diameter. The cerebellar vermis is fully intact and demonstrates normal height, area, and orientation, rule out a classic Dandy-Walker malformation. The cerebellar hemispheres are normal in structure. No ventriculomegaly is seen; both lateral ventricles measure 6.5 mm. Sulcation and gyration are appropriate for 33 weeks.

Impression: Megacisterna magna without cerebellar vermian hypoplasia at 33 weeks gestation. This is generally associated with a normal developmental prognosis when isolated.

Cardiac MRI evaluates valvular heart disease. The aortic valve is severely thickened and demonstrates calcification with restricted systolic excursion. Planimetry of the aortic valve area measures approximately 0.8 cm2, and phase-contrast velocity mapping demonstrates a peak transvalvular velocity of 4.1 m/s. Additionally, a prominent regurgitant jet is observed during diastole with a regurgitant fraction of 25%. Left ventricular concentric hypertrophy is present with a septal wall thickness of 15 mm.

Impression: Severe aortic stenosis associated with moderate aortic regurgitation and secondary left ventricular concentric hypertrophy. Left ventricular ejection fraction is preserved at 54%.

Cardiac MRI demonstrates marked trabeculation of the left ventricular apex, lateral wall, and inferior wall. The ratio of non-compacted to compacted myocardium at end-diastole is measured at 2.6, meeting the Petersen criteria for left ventricular non-compaction (LVNC).

Left ventricular volumes are mildly increased, and global systolic function is mildly impaired with an ejection fraction of 47%. No late gadolinium enhancement is identified within the trabecular or compacted layers. Impression: Morphological features consistent with left ventricular non-compaction (LVNC) accompanied by mild global systolic dysfunction.

Brain MRI demonstrates marked symmetric enlargement of the lateral and third ventricles, which is out of proportion to the degree of cerebral sulcal enlargement. High-resolution coronal FLAIR images reveal flattening of the gyri against the vertex (crowded gyri) and a narrow corpus callosal angle of approximately 65 degrees. Periventricular T2 hyperintensity is noted, consistent with transependymal flow of cerebrospinal fluid. No mass lesion or aqueductal stenosis is visible.

Impression: Ventriculomegaly disproportionate to sulcal enlargement, highly characteristic of Normal Pressure Hydrocephalus (NPH). Correlation with clinical triad of gait disturbance, cognitive decline, and urinary urgency is suggested.

MRI of the brain demonstrates mild, symmetric prominence of the cerebral cortical sulci and ventricular system, consistent with age-related cerebral volume loss. There is no evidence of acute ischemia, hemorrhage, or mass effect. A few scattered, small foci of T2/FLAIR hyperintensity are observed in the periventricular white matter, typical of chronic microvascular ischemic changes of no clinical significance.

Impression: Mild, age-appropriate global cerebral atrophy and minor chronic microvascular ischemic changes. No focal structural, neoplastic, or vascular pathology is identified to account for the patient's mild cognitive changes.

Fetal MRI at 27 weeks gestation reveals a right-sided congenital diaphragmatic hernia (CDH). The right lobe of the liver and portions of the small intestine have herniated into the right hemithorax. This herniation causes a significant mediastinal shift to the left, compressing the fetal heart and contralateral left lung. Fetal lung volumes are reduced, with the observed-to-expected total lung volume (o/e TLV) calculated at 38%.

Intracranial structures are normal. Brain sulcation (sylvian and cingulate fissures) is appropriate for 27 weeks, and the lateral ventricular atria measure 6.2 mm. Impression: Right-sided congenital diaphragmatic hernia with liver herniation and moderate-to-severe pulmonary hypoplasia. Prenatal multidisciplinary counseling is recommended.

MRI of the brain and internal auditory canals (IACs) reveals a well-circumscribed, canalicular mass centered in the left cerebellopontine angle with extension into the left internal auditory canal, producing an 'ice cream cone' appearance. The mass measures approximately 1.8 x 1.2 cm and demonstrates intense, homogeneous enhancement on post-contrast T1-weighted images. There is mild compression of the adjacent pons, but no hydrocephalus is present.

Impression: Well-circumscribed enhancing left cerebellopontine angle mass with extension into the internal auditory canal, highly characteristic of a vestibular schwannoma (acoustic neuroma).

Fetal MRI at 22 weeks gestation evaluates renal structures. The left kidney is enlarged and replaced by multiple, non-communicating cysts of varying sizes, with no identifiable normal renal parenchyma, consistent with unilateral multicystic dysplastic kidney (MCDK). The right kidney is present in the right renal fossa, showing normal size, shape, and signal intensity. Amniotic fluid volume is normal.

Intracranial anatomy is unremarkable, with normal lateral ventricular size (atrium 5.4 mm) and normal sulcation. Impression: Left unilateral multicystic dysplastic kidney with a normal contralateral kidney and adequate amniotic fluid.

Fetal MRI at 24 weeks gestation reveals classic findings of a Dandy-Walker malformation. There is severe hypoplasia and upward rotation of the cerebellar vermis, accompanied by cystic dilation of the posterior fossa (fourth ventricle) communicating with the enlarged retrocerebellar space. Torcular-lambdoid inversion is present. The lateral ventricles are mildly dilated, with the left atrium measuring 9.5 mm and the right measuring 9.2 mm.

Cortical sulcation patterns are appropriate for 24 weeks gestation. Impression: Fetal Dandy-Walker malformation. Notable findings include cerebellar vermian hypoplasia, cystic posterior fossa dilation, and mild ventriculomegaly.

Fetal MRI at 25 weeks gestation reveals severe skeletal anomalies. There is severe shortening of all long bones (micromelia), with the femurs exhibiting a characteristic curved, 'telephone-receiver' appearance. The fetal chest is extremely narrow and bell-shaped with short ribs. Platyspondyly is noted throughout the spinal column.

Intracranial structures are normal with no ventriculomegaly (atrial size 6.0 mm). Cortical sulcation is appropriate for gestational age. Impression: Skeletal dysplasia, highly characteristic of thanatophoric dysplasia type I. Severe thoracic hypoplasia is noted, indicating a poor respiratory prognosis.

Fetal MRI at 28 weeks gestation demonstrates bilateral and symmetric lateral ventriculomegaly. The left lateral ventricle atrium measures 14.5 mm, and the right lateral ventricle atrium measures 13.8 mm, indicating moderate ventriculomegaly. The third and fourth ventricles are normal in size. The cerebral cortex shows mild delay in sulcation and gyration patterns for 28 weeks, but no migration defects are clearly seen.

The corpus callosum is present and intact. The posterior fossa and other extracranial structures appear normal. Impression: Moderate bilateral fetal ventriculomegaly. Recommend serial follow-up and pediatric neurosurgical consultation.

Brain MRI was performed with multiplanar T1, T2, FLAIR, DWI, and post-contrast sequences. There are no focal areas of abnormal contrast enhancement or restricted diffusion within the supratentorial or infratentorial brain parenchyma. The ventricles and extra-axial spaces are normal in caliber. No dural or leptomeningeal enhancement is identified.

Impression: No evidence of intracranial metastatic disease. Unremarkable MRI of the brain.

Brain MR imaging was conducted. Multiplanar imaging demonstrates completely normal appearance of the cerebral hemispheres, brainstem, and cerebellum. There are no cortical lesions, areas of abnormal signal intensity, or signs of acute ischemia or intracranial bleeding. Ventricles are normal in size and position.

Impression: Unremarkable MRI of the brain. No structural abnormalities or parenchymal changes identified to suggest an epileptogenic focus.

MRI study of the brain demonstrates no structural or signal abnormalities within the cerebral hemispheres, cerebellum, or brainstem. The ventricular system, basal cisterns, and cortical sulci are within normal limits for the patient's age. There is no evidence of ischemia, hemorrhage, mass effect, or abnormal enhancement.

Impression: Normal MR imaging of the brain. No structural, neoplastic, or vascular etiology seen to explain the patient's syncopal episode.

Cardiac MRI shows diffuse, symmetric thickening of the left ventricular myocardium (septum measuring 16 mm) and the right ventricular free wall, associated with biatrial enlargement. T1 mapping demonstrates significantly elevated native myocardial T1 values. Late gadolinium enhancement imaging reveals diffuse, subendocardial hyperenhancement with abnormal myocardial nulling patterns during scout sequences.

Impression: Findings are highly consistent with cardiac amyloidosis with advanced infiltrative changes, severe diastolic dysfunction, and preserved left ventricular ejection fraction of 51%.

Cardiac MRI reveals patchy, subepicardial and mid-wall late gadolinium enhancement within the basal and mid-inferolateral walls of the left ventricle. Corresponding areas demonstrate elevated T2 relaxation times and increased signal on T2-weighted triple-inversion recovery imaging, indicating localized myocardial edema. The left ventricular ejection fraction is mild-to-moderately reduced at 47% with localized hypokinesis in the affected lateral segments.

Impression: MRI findings meet Lake Louise Criteria for active myocarditis. Subepicardial and mid-myocardial edema and fibrosis are present, associated with mild global left ventricular systolic dysfunction.

Fetal MRI evaluated at 22 weeks gestation reveals normal development. The intracranial anatomy is normal for gestational age, featuring smooth cerebral hemispheres characteristic of early cortical development. The lateral ventricles are completely symmetric, with an atrial width of 5.2 mm.

The spine is intact throughout its entire course without evidence of dysraphism. No abdominal or thoracic anomalies are demonstrated. Impression: Unremarkable fetal MRI demonstrating completely normal structural development at 22 weeks gestation.

Brain MRI reveals normal cerebral parenchyma, cerebellopontine angles, and internal auditory canals. The ventricular system, basal cisterns, and major vascular flow voids are completely unremarkable. There is no evidence of restricted diffusion or abnormal contrast enhancement.

Impression: Unremarkable MRI of the brain, demonstrating normal intracranial anatomy.

Fetal MRI at 30 weeks gestation demonstrates completely normal structural development. Symmetric lateral ventricles are visualized, measuring 6.3 mm at the atrium. Midline brain structures, cerebral sulcation, and posterior fossa structures are normal. Lung volumes and abdominal organ positions are fully appropriate.

Impression: Completely normal fetal MRI study demonstrating normal developmental anatomy at 30 weeks gestation.

The heart was imaged using standard cine and tissue characterization protocols. Both ventricles demonstrate normal cavity sizes, normal myocardial mass, and normal global systolic function. The left ventricular ejection fraction is 63% and right ventricular ejection fraction is 58% without focal wall motion abnormalities. Late gadolinium enhancement imaging is normal with no focal scarring.

Impression: Normal cardiac MRI with normal ventricular performance and no structural or ischemic heart disease identified.

MRI of the brain was performed without the administration of intravenous contrast. The cerebral and cerebellar hemispheres are normal in signal intensity and architectural structure. The ventricles and basilar cisterns are unremarkable. There is no evidence of intracranial mass, stroke, or hemorrhage. Auditory canals are bilaterally symmetrical and free of pathology.

Impression: Unremarkable MRI of the brain with no structural pathology, intracranial masses, or acute vascular events detected.

Brain MRI demonstrates a large, irregular, peripherally enhancing mass with central necrotic changes centered in the right frontal lobe, measuring 4.5 x 4.2 x 3.8 cm. Extensive surrounding T2/FLAIR hyperintensity is present, consistent with vasogenic edema, causing significant mass effect with a 6 mm leftward midline shift and compression of the right lateral ventricle. No intracranial hemorrhage is observed.

Impression: Large necrotic right frontal lobe mass with extensive surrounding vasogenic edema and mass effect, highly characteristic of a high-grade glioma such as glioblastoma. Urgent neurosurgical consultation is recommended.

Fetal MRI at 28 weeks gestation demonstrates complete agenesis of the corpus callosum. The lateral ventricles exhibit a colpocephalic configuration, with marked enlargement of the occipital horns and parallel alignment of the ventricular bodies; the atrial width is 12.0 mm. The third ventricle is dorsally displaced and moderately dilated. Sulcation pattern is mildly atypical with radial sulci extending from the margins of the third ventricle.

Impression: Complete agenesis of the corpus callosum with characteristic colpocephaly. No further extracranial structural anomalies identified.

Fetal MRI at 32 weeks gestation demonstrates mild, borderline ventriculomegaly. The left lateral ventricle atrium measures 10.8 mm, while the right lateral ventricle atrium measures 10.2 mm. No asymmetry is noted, and the parenchyma shows appropriate signal intensity without evidence of intraventricular hemorrhage.

The sulcation and gyral patterns are appropriate for 32 weeks, with expected secondary sulci development. The corpus callosum and posterior fossa are unremarkable. Impression: Mild, stable bilateral fetal ventriculomegaly with age-appropriate brain development and no other structural anomalies.

Brain MRI with cervical junction evaluation reveals cerebellar tonsillar herniation through the foramen magnum measuring approximately 7.5 mm. The cerebellar tonsils are pointed and peg-like. There is associated effacement of the CSF space at the craniocervical junction. No evidence of a cervical syrinx or spinal cord compression is seen on the localized sag T2 sequences.

Impression: Chiari I malformation with cerebellar tonsillar ectopia of 7.5 mm. Mild crowding at the level of the foramen magnum is noted without focal syrinx formation.

Cardiac MRI demonstrates a non-dilated left ventricle with a mildly reduced ejection fraction of 51%. There is prominent trabeculation of the left ventricular apex and lateral wall, with a marked double-layered appearance of the myocardium. The ratio of non-compacted to compacted myocardium (NC/C ratio) during end-diastole is calculated at 2.4, which satisfies diagnostic criteria.

Impression: Features consistent with left ventricular non-compaction (LVNC) involving the apical and lateral segments, with mild global left ventricular systolic impairment.

Cardiac MRI shows severe enlargement and thinning of the right ventricle, with prominent microaneurysms and dyskinesia of the RV free wall. Calculated right ventricular ejection fraction (RVEF) is severely depressed at 31% with an elevated end-diastolic volume index (130 ml/m2). Late gadolinium enhancement demonstrates extensive fibrofatty infiltration/scarring localized to the RV outflow tract and free wall, extending into the apical segments. LVEF is preserved at 54%.

Impression: Imaging findings are highly characteristic of Arrhythmogenic Right Ventricular Cardiomyopathy (ARVC) meeting multiple major Task Force criteria. Clinical and electrophysiological correlation is strongly advised.

Fetal MRI at 31 weeks gestation demonstrates partial agenesis of the corpus callosum, with absence of the splenium and posterior body. There is mild, localized enlargement of the occipital horns of the lateral ventricles (colpocephaly), with an atrial width of 9.5 mm. Atypical radial orientation of the medial gyri is observed, reflecting altered gyration. 

Impression: Partial agenesis of the corpus callosum with associated mild colpocephaly. Structural and developmental patterns are otherwise normal.

High-resolution MRI of the brain and internal auditory canals demonstrates no intra-axial or extra-axial mass lesions. The vestibulocochlear nerves are normal in course and caliber, and the CP angles are clear. No areas of abnormal enhancement or signal abnormality are detected.

Impression: Normal MRI of the brain and internal auditory canals. No etiology found for bilateral tinnitus.

The study demonstrates severe, asymmetric hypertrophy of the left ventricle, primarily involving the anterior septum and anterior wall. The maximal septal wall thickness is measured at 2.4 cm. Dynamic cine imaging shows systolic anterior motion (SAM) of the anterior mitral valve leaflet, causing severe dynamic left ventricular outflow tract (LVOT) obstruction and moderate mitral regurgitation. Late gadolinium enhancement is present at the RV insertion points and mid-myocardium of the hypertrophied segments.

Impression: Hypertrophic obstructive cardiomyopathy (HOCM) with severe asymmetric septal hypertrophy and dynamic LVOT obstruction. The left ventricular ejection fraction is hyperdynamic at 75%.

MRI of the brain was completed without complication. The cerebral cortex, deep grey matter structures, and brainstem appear within normal limits. There is no evidence of acute infarction, hemorrhage, or mass effect. Mild, age-appropriate prominence of the sulci is noted, with no focal areas of restriction on DWI or abnormal enhancement on post-contrast views.

Impression: Normal age-appropriate brain MRI. No acute intracranial findings or structural causes for the patient's complaints of transient dizziness.

A well-circumscribed, extra-axial mass is noted along the left parietal convexity, measuring 2.8 x 2.5 cm. The mass is broad-based to the dura and shows homogenous avid enhancement with a prominent dural tail sign. There is mild adjacent vasogenic edema but no significant mass effect on the ventricles.

Impression: Left parietal extra-axial dural-based mass, characteristic of a benign meningioma.

Brain MR demonstrates a well-circumscribed, extra-axial mass arising from the left frontal convexity, measuring approximately 2.6 x 2.4 x 2.2 cm. The mass is iso- to hypointense on T1-weighted sequences, hyperintense on T2, and shows homogeneous, intense contrast enhancement with a prominent dural tail sign. There is mild mass effect on the adjacent frontal lobe parenchyma with minimal surrounding vasogenic edema.

No other intracranial abnormalities are identified. Impression: Solitary extra-axial mass at the left frontal convexity, most consistent with a benign dural-based meningioma. Recommend outpatient neurosurgical follow-up.

Cardiac MRI evaluates a patient with a history of repaired Tetralogy of Fallot (TOF). There is severe dilation of the right ventricle, with an end-diastolic volume index of 162 mL/m2. Quantitative phase contrast imaging demonstrates severe pulmonary regurgitation with a calculated regurgitant fraction of 42%. RV systolic function is moderately reduced.

Impression: Post-repair TOF status with severe pulmonary regurgitation and severe right ventricular dilation. Right ventricular ejection fraction is reduced at 40%, while LV function is preserved (LVEF 56%).

Brain MR imaging shows no structural abnormalities in either cerebral hemisphere. High-resolution sequences through the internal auditory canals reveal completely symmetric, normal cranial nerves VII and VIII. There is no evidence of tumor, vascular loops compression, or demyelinating plaque in the cerebellopontine angle. Brainstem and ventricular structures are entirely unremarkable.

Impression: Normal MR of the brain and internal auditory canals. No organic or structural pathology identified to explain the progressive left-sided sensorineural hearing loss.

Multiplanar cine imaging displays normal ventricular anatomy, volumes, and functions. LVEF is 63% and RVEF is 59%. There are no focal wall motion abnormalities. First-pass perfusion sequences show no inducible perfusion defects. Late gadolinium enhancement images are negative for scarring or focal fibrosis. Valvular structures are unremarkable.

Impression: Normal cardiac MRI study. Preserved biventricular function with no findings of ischemia, infarction, or cardiomyopathy.

MR imaging of the brain reveals multiple small, round, well-circumscribed lesions located at the grey-white matter junctions of both the cerebral and cerebellar hemispheres. The largest lesion is in the left frontal lobe, measuring 1.2 cm, and displays ring-like enhancement with disproportionate surrounding vasogenic edema. Several other punctate enhancing lesions are noted.

Impression: Multiple enhancing intracranial lesions with surrounding edema, highly suspicious for metastatic disease. Clinical correlation with the patient's known primary malignancy history is advised.

Cardiac MRI demonstrates a diffuse, circumferential pericardial effusion measuring up to 1.8 cm in maximum depth posterior to the left ventricle, without clear features of acute cardiac tamponade. The pericardium itself is thickened, measuring up to 4 mm, and shows prominent enhancement on late post-contrast sequences. Cine imaging shows a diastolic bounce of the interventricular septum, suggestive of abnormal ventricular coupling.

Impression: Moderate to large circumferential pericardial effusion accompanied by thickened, enhancing pericardium. The septal bounce on cine imaging raises concern for early constrictive-effusive pericarditis.

Brain MRI displays age-appropriate brain volume with mild, diffuse widening of the cerebral sulci and lateral ventricles. There is no focal restricted diffusion to suggest acute ischemia, no intracranial masses, and no evidence of hemorrhage. Major flow voids along the skull base are intact.

Impression: Unremarkable MR exam of the brain showing mild age-appropriate involutional changes. No acute neurological pathology detected.

Cardiac MRI demonstrates a dilated right ventricle with an end-diastolic volume index of 115 mL/m² and regional dyskinesis of the right ventricular free wall, particularly in the outflow tract and apex. The right ventricular ejection fraction is depressed at 34%. There is fatty infiltration of the right ventricular myocardium visible on T1-weighted sequences, along with microaneurysms. The left ventricle has a normal ejection fraction of 58% with no major abnormalities.

Impression: Findings are highly suggestive of Arrhythmogenic Right Ventricular Cardiomyopathy (ARVC), meeting major Task Force criteria including RV dilation, regional dyskinesis, and depressed RV ejection fraction.

Fetal MRI at 26 weeks gestation demonstrates a right-sided congenital diaphragmatic hernia (CDH). Herniation of the liver, gallbladder, and loops of small bowel is seen within the right hemithorax, resulting in leftward mediastinal shift and compression of the left lung. The right lung is severely hypoplastic and barely visible. Fetal brain biometry is normal, and lateral ventricles measure 6.4 mm. Sulcation patterns match gestational age.

Impression: Right-sided congenital diaphragmatic hernia containing liver, gallbladder, and bowel, causing severe mediastinal shift and right pulmonary hypoplasia.

MRI of the brain demonstrates a large, heterogeneously enhancing mass centered in the left temporal lobe, measuring approximately 4.8 x 4.2 cm. The mass exhibits central areas of non-enhancement, consistent with necrosis, and is surrounded by an extensive zone of vasogenic edema that extends into the internal capsule. There is prominent mass effect resulting in compression of the left lateral ventricle and a 7 mm rightward midline shift. Elevated perfusion and restricted diffusion are noted along the peripheral margins.

Impression: Large necrotic, heterogeneously enhancing left temporal lobe mass surrounded by extensive vasogenic edema and mass effect, highly suspicious for glioblastoma multiforme.

Fetal MRI at 36 weeks gestation demonstrates advanced fetal brain maturation. Sulcation and gyration patterns are highly appropriate for 36 weeks, with well-formed secondary and tertiary cortical folds. The ventricles are normal and symmetric, with atrial diameters of 5.5 mm. The brainstem, posterior fossa, and midline structures are completely normal.

The lungs display normal signal intensity and volume. No congenital diaphragmatic or spinal defects are visualized. Impression: Normal fetal MRI at 36 weeks gestation demonstrating excellent cortical development.

There are extensive, multi-segmental subendocardial and transmural late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) defects involving the mid-to-basal inferior and inferolateral walls (consistent with RCA/LCx territories). Regional wall motion analysis shows severe hypokinesis to akinesis in these segments. The left ventricle is moderately dilated, and the overall LVEF is calculated at 31%, reflecting significant ischemic cardiomyopathy.

Impression: Multi-vessel ischemic cardiomyopathy with significant subendocardial and transmural myocardial infarctions of the inferior and inferolateral walls. Severely depressed left ventricular systolic function.

Fetal MRI at 27 weeks gestation reveals borderline ventriculomegaly. The left lateral ventricle atrium measures 10.1 mm, while the right lateral ventricle atrium measures 8.9 mm. There is no shift of midline structures or subependymal hemorrhage. The sulcation and opercularization of the sylvian fissure are appropriate for 27 weeks. The corpus callosum and posterior fossa elements are morphologically normal.

The remainder of the systemic examination of the fetus is within normal limits. Impression: Isolated unilateral borderline left fetal ventriculomegaly. Close interval ultrasound follow-up is recommended to monitor ventricular dimensions.

Cardiac MRI demonstrates normal biventricular volumes and systolic function. The left ventricular ejection fraction is calculated at 62%, and the right ventricular ejection fraction is 58%. Wall thickness, myocardial mass, and chamber dimensions are all within normal limits for age and body surface area. No regional wall motion abnormalities are identified on cine sequencing, and there is no evidence of myocardial edema on T2-weighted imaging.

Evaluation for late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) is negative, with no focal areas of myocardial scar or fibrosis visualized. The cardiac valves exhibit normal morphology and excursion without significant stenosis or regurgitation. Impression: Unremarkable cardiac MRI showing normal cardiac structure and biventricular function with no evidence of scar or active myocarditis.

Fetal MRI at 27 weeks gestation demonstrates severe oligohydramnios, limiting optimal fetal visualization. There is a complete absence of identifiable renal parenchyma bilaterally within the renal fossae. The adrenal glands are present but show a 'lying down' configuration. The fetal urinary bladder is persistently empty and non-visualized.

There is associated severe pulmonary hypoplasia, with severely restricted fetal thoracic space. Intracranial ventricles (atrial width 5.5 mm) and cortical sulcation are within normal limits. Impression: Bilateral renal agenesis associated with severe oligohydramnios, empty urinary bladder, and secondary pulmonary hypoplasia (Potter sequence presentation).

Fetal MRI at 28 weeks gestation demonstrates bilateral, asymmetric enlargement of the lateral ventricles. The left lateral ventricular atrium measures 14.5 mm and the right measures 11.2 mm, indicating moderate to severe ventriculomegaly. There is a corresponding mild delay in the opercularization of the Sylvian fissures and cortical sulcation relative to the gestational age.

Impression: Bilateral fetal ventriculomegaly, left greater than right, with associated mild developmental delay in cortical sulcation. Close follow-up and postnatal clinical evaluation are recommended.

Cardiac MRI shows normal chamber volumes, intact valvular function, and symmetric myocardial thickness. The left ventricular ejection fraction is 62% and the right ventricular ejection fraction is 56%. There is no evidence of regional hypokinesis, late gadolinium enhancement, or tissue edema. Flow dynamics across the outflow tracts are normal.

Impression: Normal cardiac MRI with well-preserved biventricular function and no signs of myocardial scar, inflammation, or structural heart disease.

Cardiac MRI evaluation utilizing T1/T2 mapping and LGE techniques. T2-weighted and mapping sequences demonstrate patchily increased signal intensity in the subepicardial and mid-myocardial regions of the basal to mid-lateral left ventricular wall, indicative of myocardial edema. Left ventricular systolic function is mildly reduced with an EF of 48%. LGE images demonstrate matching patchy subepicardial and mid-wall enhancement in the same segments, sparing the subendocardium.

Impression: Findings meet the modified Lake Louise Criteria for acute myocarditis, characterized by localized myocardial edema and non-ischemic subepicardial late gadolinium enhancement of the lateral wall.

Fetal MRI at 32 weeks gestation reveals partial agenesis of the corpus callosum. The anterior callosal body and genu are present, but the splenium and posterior body are absent. This is associated with mild dilatation of the posterior aspects of the lateral ventricles (colpocephaly), measuring 11.8 mm. Abnormal radiating sulci are noted in the posterior parietal regions.

The anterior structures and posterior fossa are otherwise normal. Fetal abdominal and thoracic anatomy are normal. Impression: Partial agenesis of the corpus callosum with associated mild posterior colpocephaly and localized sulcation abnormality.

Dedicated MR imaging of the pituitary gland reveals a hypoenhancing, well-circumscribed lesion within the left aspect of the adenohypophysis measuring approximately 6 x 5 mm. There is subtle superior deviation of the pituitary stalk, though the optic chiasm is structurally completely clear and uninvolved. The cavernous sinuses are symmetrical without invasion.

Impression: Features consistent with a small left-sided pituitary microadenoma. No mass effect on the optic chiasm or extension into adjacent vascular structures is visualized.

Cardiac MRI shows normal internal cardiac architecture with preserved biventricular systolic parameters. The left ventricular ejection fraction is 65% and the right ventricular ejection fraction is 60%. Myocardial thickness is uniform, and there are no focal hypokinetic or dyskinetic wall segments. Valves show normal excursion.

There is no evidence of myocardial edema on T2 maps, and late gadolinium enhancement is completely absent. Visualized major thoracic vessels, including the pulmonary trunk and aorta, are normal. Impression: Completely normal cardiac MRI study.

Fetal MRI at 27 weeks gestation shows excellent visualization of normal fetal brain structures. The cortical sulcation is appropriate for 27 weeks, demonstrating progressive opercularization of the Sylvian fissures. The ventricles are symmetric and normal, with the atrial diameter measuring 6.1 mm. The midline structures, including the corpus callosum and cerebellar vermis, are entirely normal. Fetal situs is normal, and amniotic fluid is adequate.

Impression: Completely normal fetal MRI study demonstrating appropriate cerebral development and normal systemic fetal anatomy at 27 weeks.

MR imaging reveals a well-circumscribed, extra-axial mass along the right parietal convex dura, measuring 2.8 x 2.5 x 2.3 cm. The mass is dural-based, shows homogeneous intense enhancement, and displays a prominent 'dural tail' sign. There is mild mass effect on the adjacent cerebral cortex and minor surrounding vasogenic edema, but no evidence of parenchymal invasion.

Impression: Dural-based, intensely enhancing extra-axial mass along the right parietal convexity, highly characteristic of a benign meningioma. No significant mass effect or herniation.

Fetal MRI at 28 weeks gestation demonstrates normal fetal anatomy. The cerebral cortex shows appropriate development with emerging sulcation and sylvian fissures suitable for 28 weeks. The ventricular system is normal, with the lateral ventricular atrium measuring 6.0 mm. No hemorrhage or fluid collections are visualized within or around the brain.

The thoracic, abdominal, and skeletal structures are normal. Kidneys and bladder are well-visualized and anatomically normal. Impression: Unremarkable fetal MRI study showing completely normal anatomy and age-appropriate brain development.

MRI of the heart reveals normal cardiac dimensions and anatomy. The left ventricular end-diastolic volume and end-systolic volume are within normal physiologic ranges. The left ventricular ejection fraction is calculated at 60%, and the right ventricular ejection fraction is 57%. No regional wall motion abnormalities or areas of focal myocardial scarring are identified on post-contrast imaging.

Impression: Normal cardiac MRI study. There is no structural or functional abnormality to account for the patient's atypical chest pain.

Magnetic resonance imaging of the brain demonstrates multiple hyperintense lesions on T2/FLAIR sequences distributed within the periventricular, juxtacortical, and infratentorial white matter. Several of these lesions are oriented perpendicular to the lateral ventricles, consistent with Dawson's fingers. Following gadolinium administration, two active lesions in the left frontal lobe demonstrate incomplete ring enhancement, indicative of active demyelinating plaques. No mass effect or significant ventricular distortion is observed.

Impression: Demarcated demyelinating lesions of the brain showing spatial and temporal dissemination, highly suggestive of active multiple sclerosis. Neurology follow-up and correlation with cerebrospinal fluid analysis is recommended.

Brain MRI shows symmetric cerebral hemispheres with unremarkable grey-white matter differentiation. No areas of restricted diffusion or susceptibility abnormalities are observed. The ventricles, cisterns, and major vascular flow voids are normal in appearance. No acoustic neuroma or CPA mass identified.

Impression: Normal brain MRI with no structural or vascular lesions. No etiologic factor for progressive tinnitus identified within the central nervous system.

Sagittal T1- and T2-weighted MRI sequences demonstrate low-lying cerebellar tonsils projecting approximately 8 mm below the level of the foramen magnum. The tonsils are pointed or 'peg-like' in morphology. There is associated crowding at the craniovertebral junction. Assessment of the visualized upper cervical spine demonstrates a small, central syrinx at the C2-C3 level.

Impression: Chiari I malformation, characterized by 8 mm tonsillar ectopia, associated with a small cervical syrinx. Clinical correlation is recommended for symptoms of occipital headache or myelopathy.

MRI shows a crescentic, extra-axial collection of fluid overlying the right cerebral hemisphere, measuring up to 1.4 cm in maximal width. The collection has homogeneous low T1 and high T2 signals with internal septations, typical of a chronic subdural hematoma. There is significant mass effect with compression of the right lateral ventricle and 5 mm leftward midline shift.

Impression: Large, chronic right subdural hematoma with moderate mass effect and midline shift. Evaluation by a neurosurgeon is indicated given the degree of mass effect.

Fetal MRI at 31 weeks gestation demonstrates partial agenesis of the corpus callosum. The anterior aspects of the corpus callosum (genu and body) are present, but the posterior components (splenium and rostrum) are absent. This is associated with mild colpocephaly, with the posterior horns of the lateral ventricles measuring 13.1 mm on the left and 12.8 mm on the right. Midline sulcation is abnormally arranged posteriorly.

The cerebellar vermis and brainstem are morphologically normal. The remainder of the fetal systemic anatomy is unremarkable. Impression: Partial agenesis of the corpus callosum with associated moderate colpocephaly and localized sulcal reorganization.

Cardiac MRI evaluates a young patient for possible congenital heart disease. There is a prominent defect in the superior aspect of the interatrial septum, measuring 18 mm, consistent with a sinus venosus atrial septal defect. Partial anomalous pulmonary venous connection (PAPVC) of the right upper pulmonary vein draining into the superior vena cava is clearly visualized. There is significant right ventricular volume overload with an RV end-diastolic volume index of 115 mL/m² and a Qp:Qs ratio estimated at 1.8.

Impression: Sinus venosus atrial septal defect with partial anomalous pulmonary venous return, causing significant left-to-right shunt and consequent right ventricular volume overload.

Multiple focal, ovoid T2/FLAIR hyperintense lesions are scattered throughout the periventricular and juxtacortical white matter, oriented perpendicular to the lateral ventricles (Dawson's fingers). Several lesions in the cervical medullary junction and corpus callosum are also noted. Two lesions exhibit enhancement post-contrast.

Impression: Demyelinating plaques scattered throughout the brain, highly indicative of multiple sclerosis, with active lesions demonstrating contrast enhancement.

Brain MRI shows a well-circumscribed, extra-axial mass along the right parasagittal parietal convexity measuring approximately 3.2 x 2.8 x 2.5 cm. The mass is dural-based and exhibits intense, homogeneous enhancement post-contrast injection, along with a distinct 'dural tail' sign. There is mild compression of the adjacent cerebral cortex with minimal edema in the underlying brain parenchyma.

Impression: Well-circumscribed, dural-based extra-axial mass along the right parasagittal parietal region, highly consistent with a benign meningioma. Mild compression of the underlying cortex is noted.

Fetal MRI at 36 weeks gestation demonstrates a right-sided congenital diaphragmatic hernia (CDH). The right hemidiaphragm is deficient, with the right liver lobe and gallbladder herniating into the right chest cavity. This causes significant leftward mediastinal shift and compression of the heart and left lung. Calculated total fetal lung volume is severely reduced for gestational age.

The fetal brain shows normal cortical sulcation for 36 weeks. The lateral ventricular atria are within normal limits, measuring 6.2 mm. Impression: Right-sided congenital diaphragmatic hernia with herniation of liver and gallbladder, causing severe mediastinal shift and pulmonary hypoplasia.

Brain MRI with dedicated internal auditory canal (IAC) sequences is performed. The internal auditory canals are symmetric, and the vestibulocochlear-facial nerve complexes are normal and free of lesions bilateral. The cerebellar pontine angles are clear, and there is no evidence of an acoustic neuroma, meningioma, or vascular loop compression.

Impression: Unremarkable MRI of the brain and internal auditory canals. No cerebellopontine angle mass or vestibular schwannoma identified to explain unilateral tinnitus.

Fetal MRI performed at 22 weeks gestation demonstrates an open lumbar myelomeningocele with associated hindbrain herniation consistent with a Chiari II malformation. The posterior fossa is narrow with cerebellar crowding, and the lateral ventricles are dilated, with the atrium measuring 11.5 mm.

The spine shows dysraphism at the L3-L5 levels with an intact overlying CSF-filled sac. Early brain sulcation is normal and smooth as expected. Impression: Open lumbar myelomeningocele with Chiari II malformation and associated moderate ventriculomegaly.

Cardiac MRI shows moderate dilation of the left ventricle and left atrium. There is prominent billowing and prolapse of the posterior mitral valve leaflet (P2 segment) into the left atrium during systole. Cine imaging and flow-vessel quantification demonstrate a large regurgitant volume (48 mL) into the left atrium, consistent with severe mitral regurgitation. The left ventricular ejection fraction is 61%.

Impression: Mitral valve prolapse of the posterior leaflet with hemodynamically severe mitral regurgitation, resulting in moderate left-sided chamber remodeling.

Cardiac MRI reveals a localized area of transmural late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) involving the apex and mid-anteroseptal walls of the left ventricle, encompassing approximately 75% of the wall thickness in these segments. These findings correspond to a territory supplied by the left anterior descending (LAD) coronary artery. Regional wall motion analysis shows severe hypokinesis in the corresponding anterior and apical segments. The left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) is reduced at 42%, with an end-diastolic volume of 178 mL, demonstrating mild left ventricular dilation.

Impression: Findings are consistent with a prior myocardial infarction in the LAD distribution with significant transmural scarring. Mild left ventricular dilation and moderately reduced overall systolic function.

Cardiac MRI shows normal cardiac dimensions, wall thickness, and systolic function of both ventricles. Left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) is 60%, and right ventricular ejection fraction (RVEF) is 57%. No regional wall motion abnormalities or signs of myocardial edema are present. Myocardial tissue characterization is unremarkable, and there is no late gadolinium enhancement (LGE).

Impression: Completely normal cardiac MRI. No structural abnormality, perfusion defect, or areas of chronic myocardial scar detected.

Cardiac MRI demonstrates normal biventricular dimensions and systolic function. Left ventricular ejection fraction is 63% and right ventricular ejection fraction is 58%. The myocardium exhibits normal thickness, with no late gadolinium enhancement to suggest myocardial scar, fibrosis, or infiltrative process. Major cardiac valves are structurally intact.

Impression: Unremarkable cardiac MRI. No diagnostic findings of ischemic heart disease, cardiomyopathy, or pericardial abnormality.

Fetal MRI at 26 weeks gestation reveals a large, multicystic dysplastic left kidney (MCDK). The left kidney is replaced by multiple non-communicating cysts of varying sizes, with no identifiable normal renal parenchyma. The right kidney is normal in size and appearance, and there is a normal volume of amniotic fluid, indicating preserved global renal function. Intracranial structures demonstrate normal sulcation for 26 weeks, and the ventricular atrium measures 6.0 mm.

The fetal chest and gastrointestinal tract are normal. Impression: Unilateral (left-sided) multicystic dysplastic kidney (MCDK) with a normal contralateral right kidney and normal amniotic fluid volume. Brain development is completely normal.

The lateral and third ventricles are disproportionately enlarged relative to the degree of cerebral sulcal enlargement. There is a prominent flow void in the aqueduct of Sylvius on T2-weighted images. No signs of transependymal CSF migration or obstructive mass lesion are noted. Mild periventricular white matter changes consistent with microvascular ischemic disease are present.

Impression: Ventriculomegaly out of proportion to cortical atrophy. Findings are highly consistent with Normal Pressure Hydrocephalus (NPH) in the appropriate clinical context.

Fetal MRI at 24 weeks gestation demonstrates a severe forebrain malformation. There is partial separation of the cerebral hemispheres posteriorly, but the frontal lobes are fused across the midline, associated with a single large monoventricle and partially fused thalami. These findings are diagnostic of semilobar holoprosencephaly. The corpus callosum is absent. Sulcation is highly abnormal.

Cleft lip and palate are also visualized. Impression: Semilobar holoprosencephaly with associated facial clefting. Severe prognosis; maternal-fetal medicine and genetic counseling are recommended.

Brain MRI demonstrates a large, crescentic fluid collection over the right cerebral hemisphere, measuring up to 1.8 cm in maximal width. The collection is predominantly hyperintense on T2-weighted imaging and T1-weighted imaging, consistent with subacute-to-chronic subdural hematoma components. Significant mass effect is present, with compression of the right lateral ventricle and 8 mm of leftward midline shift.

Impression: Large subacute-to-chronic right-sided subdural hematoma with significant mass effect and midline shift. Neurosurgical evaluation is indicated.

Cardiac MRI reveals a moderate-to-large circumferential pericardial effusion, measuring up to 1.8 cm in thickness adjacent to the right ventricle and apex. There is diffuse, intense enhancement of both the visceral and parietal pericardial layers on late gadolinium enhancement imaging, indicating acute active pericarditis. No clear signs of diastolic chamber collapse (tamponade physiology) are seen at this time.

Impression: Moderate-to-large circumferential pericardial effusion with significant, diffuse pericardial enhancement consistent with acute active pericarditis.

Fetal MRI at 23 weeks gestation demonstrates a low lumbar myelomeningocele with herniation of the placode and CSF space through a posterior dysraphic defect of the L4-L5 spine. Associated intracranial features of Chiari II malformation are present, including a lemon-shaped skull, banana sign of the cerebellum, and effacement of the cisterna magna. Bilateral lateral ventricles are moderately dilated with an atrial width of 12.0 mm.

Impression: Open lumbar neural tube defect (myelomeningocele) with secondary Chiari II malformation and moderate ventriculomegaly. Early neurosurgical consultation for in-utero vs. postnatal repair planning is advised.
