Cardiac MRI shows normal cardiac anatomy and chamber dimensions. Left ventricular systolic function is normal, with an ejection fraction of 59% and normal stroke volume. Right ventricular dimensions and systolic function are also within normal parameters (RVEF 55%). No valvular abnormalities or flow disturbances are visualized. T1 and T2 mapping parameters are normal, and there is no evidence of myocardial scar or fibrosis on late gadolinium enhancement imaging.

Impression: Normal cardiac MRI. No structural, functional, or tissue characterization abnormalities are identified.

Three-dimensional magnetic resonance angiography (MRA) of the thoracic aorta demonstrates a focal narrowing of the descending thoracic aorta just distal to the origin of the left subclavian artery. Prominent intercostal and internal mammary collateral vessels are visualized bypassing the obstruction. Concentric hypertrophy of the left ventricle is present (mass index 112 g/m²) with an EF of 66%.

Impression: Classic post-ductal coarctation of the aorta with extensive collateral circulation and secondary concentric left ventricular hypertrophy.

MRI of the brain with and without contrast reveals a large, heterogeneously enhancing, necrotic intra-axial mass in the right temporal lobe measuring approximately 4.8 x 4.2 x 3.9 cm. There is extensive surrounding vasogenic edema causing a 10 mm leftward midline shift and partial compression of the right lateral ventricle and temporal horn. Mild subfalcine herniation is noted.

Impression: Large, enhancing, necrotic right temporal lobe mass with significant mass effect and midline shift, highly suggestive of high-grade glioma (e.g., glioblastoma multiforme). Urgent neurosurgical intervention is warranted.

MR of the brain reveals multiple oval-shaped T2/FLAIR hyperintense lesions oriented perpendicular to the lateral ventricles (Dawson's fingers), predominantly in the periventricular and juxtacortical white matter. At least two of these lesions, located in the right frontal subcortical white matter, demonstrate nodular enhancement post-gadolinium administration, indicating active demyelination.

Impression: Demylinating disease of the central nervous system, demonstrating spatial and temporal dissemination, highly consistent with active Multiple Sclerosis (MS).

Fetal MRI at 21 weeks gestation demonstrates a cranial neural tube defect. There is an occipital skull defect measuring 7 mm with herniation of a meningeal sac containing cerebrospinal fluid, consistent with an occipital meningocele. The intracranial structures are otherwise preserved, and the lateral ventricles are normal, measuring 6.5 mm.

Impression: Occipital meningocele without herniation of brain tissue. Recommend pediatric neurosurgical consult for prenatal planning.

Cardiac MRI shows severe, multi-segmental wall motion abnormalities with global hypokinesia and apical dyskinesia of the left ventricle. Left ventricular ejection fraction is severely depressed at 22%, and the ventricle is dilated (EDV 278 mL).

Late gadolinium enhancement imaging demonstrates extensive, confluent transmural scarring (100% thickness) in the mid-to-apical anterior wall, apex, and apical septum, consistent with severe, chronic, non-viable LAD territory myocardial infarction. Subendocardial scar is also noted in the inferior wall. Impression: Severe ischemic cardiomyopathy with marked LV dilation and dysfunction. Large, non-viable transmural anterior/apical myocardial infarction.

Cardiac MRI demonstrates normal biventricular size and systolic function. The left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) is calculated at 62%, with an end-diastolic volume index of 74 mL/m2. The right ventricular ejection fraction (RVEF) is 58%. Wall thickness is normal throughout both chambers without evidence of regional wall motion abnormalities or hypertrophy. Late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) imaging shows no areas of myocardial scar, fibrosis, or focal enhancement.

Impression: Normal cardiac MRI study. No evidence of cardiomyopathy, myocardial scar, or structural heart disease.

Brain MRI reveals a cluster of tightly packed, serpiginous vascular flow voids in the left parietal lobe, measuring approximately 2.5 cm, consistent with a vascular nidus. Prominent feeding arteries arising from the left MCA and dilated draining veins are identified. No acute parenchymal hemorrhage or surrounding edema is seen.

Impression: Left parietal arteriovenous malformation (AVM) without evidence of acute bleeding. Refer to interventional neurorology and neurosurgery for treatment planning.

Fetal MRI at 36 weeks gestation shows appropriate fetal growth and anatomy. The cerebral hemispheres demonstrate mature sulcation and gyration patterns for 36 weeks, with well-formed secondary and tertiary sulci. The lateral ventricles are completely symmetric, measuring 5.2 mm. No intracranial or extra-axial fluid collections are identified.

Fetal lungs display appropriate signal and volume for late gestation. Abdominal organs, musculoskeletal structures, and placental localization are normal. Impression: Completely normal late-gestation fetal MRI demonstrating age-appropriate structural development.

Fetal MRI at 31 weeks gestation demonstrates a large multicystic dysplastic left kidney. The left kidney is enlarged and filled with multiple non-communicating, thin-walled cysts of varying sizes, with no visible normal renal parenchyma. The contralateral right kidney is normal in size and appearance, showing compensatory hypertrophy. Amniotic fluid volume is normal.

The fetal brain is normal, with an atrial ventricular width of 5.7 mm and normal third-trimester sulcation patterns. Impression: Left multicystic dysplastic kidney with a normal right kidney and normal amniotic fluid. Intracranial anatomy is unremarkable.

Fetal MRI at 36 weeks gestation shows fully mature and age-appropriate cerebral cortex morphology. The tertiary sulcation pattern is well-developed across both cerebral hemispheres. The ventricular system is normal, with lateral ventricular atria measuring 5.5 mm on both sides. Posterior fossa and abdominal organs are unremarkable.

Impression: Unremarkable third-trimester fetal MRI demonstrating appropriate brain maturity and normal ventricular size.

Imaging demonstrates a localized region of encephalomalacia and gliosis in the right parietal lobe, with corresponding T2/FLAIR hyperintensity and volume loss. No corresponding restricted diffusion is demonstrated on DWI/ADC, indicating that this is a chronic lesion. There are no acute ischemic changes or intracranial masses.

Impression: Chronic infarct in the right parietal lobe territory. No acute intracranial findings.

Cardiac MRI demonstrates extensive trabeculation of the left ventricular apex and lateral wall, with a non-compacted to compacted myocardial thickness ratio of 2.6:1 in diastole, meeting criteria for left ventricular non-compaction (LVNC). The left ventricular end-diastolic volume is moderately increased, and the left ventricular ejection fraction is mildly reduced at 47%.

No late gadolinium enhancement is identified within either the compacted or non-compacted layers. Impression: Morphological features are diagnostic of left ventricular non-compaction with associated mild left ventricular enlargement and systolic dysfunction.

Fetal MRI at 36 weeks gestation demonstrates advanced sulcation, with well-defined primary and secondary sulci corresponding to third-trimester gestational parameters. Ventricular chambers are of normal caliber, with a maximum atrial diameter of 5.2 mm. Brainstem, cerebellar hemispheres, and vermis are entirely normal. Fetal lungs show homogeneous T2 high signal, representing normal development.

Impression: Normal, late-third-trimester fetal MRI. No intracranial or extracranial anomalies identified.

Cardiac MRI demonstrates normal cardiac architecture. Left ventricular end-diastolic volume index is 74 mL/m² and the ejection fraction is 60%. The right ventricle is of normal size and function (RVEF 56%).

There is no evidence of regional myocardial thinning, wall motion abnormality, or delayed myocardial hyperenhancement to suggest chronic infarction or fibrosis. Valves appear structurally normal. Impression: Completely normal cardiac MRI. No evidence of ischemic heart disease, cardiomyopathy, or structural abnormality.

Dedicated pituitary MR imaging demonstrates a well-circumscribed 1.4 cm hypoenhancing mass within the left side of the sella turcica. The mass extends into the suprasellar cistern, causing mild upward displacement of the optic chiasm. No cavernous sinus invasion is observed.

Impression: Pituitary macroadenoma with suprasellar extension, resulting in mild compression of the optic chiasm. Correlation with endocrine function panel and visual field testing is recommended.

There is a moderate, circumferential pericardial effusion measuring up to 1.8 cm adjacent to the right ventricle and 1.4 cm adjacent to the left ventricular apex. The pericardium is diffusely thickened, measuring up to 4 mm, and demonstrates hyperintensity on T2-weighted imaging and late gadolinium enhancement, indicating active inflammation. No evidence of right atrial or ventricular diastolic collapse is seen.

Impression: Moderate circumferential pericardial effusion associated with active, acute pericarditis. There are no definitive MRI signs of cardiac tamponade at the time of study.

Cardiac MRI shows normal heart anatomy with excellent biventricular systolic performance. The left ventricular ejection fraction is calculated at 65% with an end-diastolic volume of 120 mL. Right ventricular volume and ejection fraction (58%) are within normal physiological ranges.

There is no evidence of septal defects, patent ductus arteriosus, or coarctation of the aorta. Evaluation of late gadolinium enhancement sequences reveals no focal enhancement or myocardial fibrosis. Impression: Unremarkable cardiac MRI. Normal ventricular function and volumes with no structural or valvular abnormalities.

Cardiac MRI evaluates a 28-year-old male with persistent upper-extremity hypertension. There is a focal, discrete narrowing of the proximal descending thoracic aorta, located just distal to the origin of the left subclavian artery, measuring 8 mm in diameter. Phase-contrast imaging demonstrates a significant systolic peak velocity of 3.8 m/s across the stenosis, with holodiastolic flow reversal in the abdominal aorta. Prominent collateral intercostal arteries are noted.

Impression: Severe focal coarctation of the descending thoracic aorta with hemodynamically significant stenosis. Prominent collateral vascular development is visualized.

Cardiac MRI demonstrates a dilated left ventricle with moderate global systolic dysfunction. The left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) is estimated at 38%. Multiplanar cine imaging reveals severe hypokinesis of the mid-to-distal anteroseptal and apical walls. Late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) imaging shows dense, transmural hyperenhancement in these corresponding segments, covering approximately 75% of the wall thickness, consistent with a prior myocardial infarction in the left anterior descending (LAD) coronary artery territory.

Impression: Ischemic cardiomyopathy with severe anteroseptal and apical transmural myocardial infarction and moderately reduced LVEF. No evidence of viable myocardium in the infarcted zones.

Brain MR imaging demonstrates ventriculomegaly disproportionate to the degree of cerebral sulcal atrophy. There is prominent dilation of the lateral and third ventricles, with narrowing of the sulci at the high convexities and parasagittal regions (known as DESH). The callosal angle is acutely narrow at approximately 55 degrees. No significant periventricular transependymal CSF flow is identified, and there is no evidence of aqueductal stenosis.

Impression: Pattern of ventriculomegaly with disproportionate enlargement of the subarachnoid spaces, highly suggestive of normal pressure hydrocephalus (NPH) in this clinical context.

The study reveals significant dilation and dysfunction of the right ventricle, with an end-diastolic volume index of 135 mL/m2. Prominent dyskinesis and localized bulging of the right ventricular free wall are observed during systole. Late gadolinium enhancement imaging confirms focal areas of hyperenhancement along the right ventricular free wall, indicative of fibrofatty replacement.

Impression: Cardiac MRI findings are highly indicative of Arrhythmogenic Right Ventricular Cardiomyopathy (ARVC). Right ventricular ejection fraction is reduced at 34%, while left ventricular function is preserved (EF 55%).

Brain MRI demonstrates an area of encephalomalacia and surrounding gliosis within the left parietal cortex, consistent with a chronic, mature vascular insult. There is compensatory dilation of the adjacent left lateral ventricle atrium. No acute infarcts, hemorrhages, or mass lesions are identified on the current study.

Impression: Chronic left parietal lobe encephalomalacia and gliosis representing a mature territorial cerebral infarction. No evidence of acute ischemic or hemorrhagic events.

Fetal MRI at 25 weeks gestation reveals a right-sided congenital diaphragmatic hernia. The fetal liver is partially herniated into the right hemithorax, along with loops of bowel, causing significant leftward shift of the mediastinum and heart. The right lung is severely compressed and barely visible. The left lung is moderately compressed but demonstrates visible airway structures. Fetal brain anatomy is normal, with ventricles measuring 5.5 mm.

Impression: Right-sided congenital diaphragmatic hernia (CDH) with liver herniated ('liver-up' status) and severe right pulmonary hypoplasia.

Cardiac MRI evaluates cardiac structure, volumes, and function. The left ventricular end-diastolic volume is 140 mL, with a calculated left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) of 64%. The right ventricular end-diastolic volume is 130 mL, with a right ventricular ejection fraction (RVEF) of 59%. There are no regional wall motion abnormalities or areas of focal wall thinning. Myocardial perfusion during first-pass imaging is uniform. Late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) imaging shows no areas of myocardial scar or fibrosis.

Impression: Entirely normal cardiac MRI examination. Preserved biventricular dimensions and systolic function with no evidence of ischemic or non-ischemic myocardial pathology.

MRI demonstrates diffuse, symmetric thickening of the left ventricular myocardium (wall thickness 16 mm) and right ventricular free wall, associated with mild biatrial enlargement. Late gadolinium enhancement imaging reveals a characteristic pattern of diffuse, subendocardial hyperenhancement spanning both ventricles, along with difficulty nulling the myocardial signal. Left ventricular systolic function is moderately depressed with an ejection fraction of 45%.

Impression: Severe cardiac amyloidosis with characteristic diffuse subendocardial late gadolinium enhancement, biventricular wall thickening, and restrictive physiology.

Fetal MRI at 29 weeks gestation demonstrates partial agenesis of the corpus callosum, with the posterior body and splenium not visualized. There is associated colpocephaly, with the posterior horns of the lateral ventricles measuring 11.2 mm on the left and 10.8 mm on the right. The anterior corpus callosum is present but thin.

The brainstem, cerebellum, and fetal abdominal and thoracic organs appear normal. Impression: Partial agenesis of the corpus callosum with mild posterior colpocephaly.

Brain MRI demonstrates extensive, confluent areas of bilateral cerebral white matter hyperintensity on T2/FLAIR images, particularly within the periventricular regions and corona radiata. This is consistent with severe chronic microvascular ischemic white matter disease (Fazekas Grade 3). Symmetrical ventricular enlargement and sulcal prominence reflect moderate generalized cerebral atrophy.

Impression: Severe, chronic microvascular ischemic white matter disease. Moderate generalized cerebral parenchymal volume loss, with no signs of acute infarction or hemorrhage.

Fetal MRI at 32 weeks gestation demonstrates normal intracranial anatomy. The sulcation and gyral patterns are appropriate and well-defined for 32 weeks, showing progressive opercularization of the temporal lobes. The lateral ventricles are symmetric, with the atrium measuring 6.2 mm. The corpus callosum is intact, and the brainstem and posterior fossa structures are normal in size and signal intensity.

Impression: Unremarkable fetal MRI at 32 weeks gestation, showing age-appropriate cortical sulcation and normal ventricles.

Cardiac MRI shows physiological chamber volumes and myocardial mass index. Trace, clinically insignificant mitral and aortic regurgitation are noted, typical for age. Quantitative evaluation of left and right ventricular stroke volumes is symmetric. There is no evidence of ischemic heart disease or infiltrative processes on late gadolinium enhancement imaging.

Impression: Completely normal cardiac MRI for a 72-year-old patient. No evidence of cardiomyopathy, ischemic injury, or clinically significant valvular disease.

MR imaging reveals a large, heterogeneously enhancing intra-axial mass in the right temporal lobe measuring approximately 4.5 x 3.8 x 4.0 cm. The mass is surrounded by extensive vasogenic edema causing a 7 mm leftward midline shift and subfalcine herniation. There are central non-enhancing cystic/necrotic areas and prominent internal vascularity.

Impression: Large, necrotic, enhancing intra-axial mass in the right temporal lobe, highly suspicious for a high-grade glioma (e.g., glioblastoma). Significant mass effect with midline shift and risk of herniation.

Fetal MRI at 24 weeks gestation reveals classic features of Dandy-Walker malformation. There is severe hypoplasia and upward rotation of the cerebellar vermis, accompanied by cystic dilation of the posterior fossa (representing a dilated fourth ventricle) and elevated tentorium cerebelli (torcular-herophili herophili elevation). The supratentorial brain shows mild ventriculomegaly, with the lateral ventricular atria measuring 9.5 mm bilaterally.

Cortical sulcation pattern is appropriate for 24 weeks gestation, with the sylvian and parieto-occipital fissures normally configured. Spinal alignment and spinal cord terminating level are normal. Impression: Dandy-Walker malformation characterized by cerebellar vermis hypoplasia, cystic posterior fossa expansion, and mild bilateral ventriculomegaly.

MR imaging of the brain demonstrates a well-circumscribed, extra-axial mass arising from the left parietal dural convexity, measuring 3.2 x 2.8 x 2.5 cm. The mass is intensely and homogeneously enhancing post-contrast, with a classic 'dural tail' sign. There is mild adjacent parenchymal vasogenic edema and slight compression of the adjacent cerebral sulci, but no midline shift.

Impression: Left parietal extra-axial enhancing mass, highly characteristic of a benign meningioma. Stable appearance is advised for follow-up or neurosurgical consultation depending on symptoms.

Multiplanar brain MRI reveals three distinct, well-circumscribed, ring-enhancing lesions at the gray-white matter junctions: one in the left frontal lobe (1.2 cm), one in the right parietal lobe (0.8 cm), and one in the left cerebellar hemisphere (1.5 cm). Significant surrounding vasogenic edema is associated with each.

Impression: Multiple enhancing intracranial lesions at the gray-white matter junction, consistent with metastatic disease.

Fetal MRI at 26 weeks gestation reveals excellent anatomical development. The cerebral cortex shows typical, age-appropriate gyration with well-defined sylvian fissures. The ventricular system is normal, with both the left and right lateral ventricular atria measuring 6.2 mm. The corpus callosum, cerebellar vermis, and brainstem are completely formed without structural defects.

The fetal spine is intact, and chest/abdominal visceral development is appropriate. No fetal abnormalities are visualized. Impression: Entirely normal fetal MRI study demonstrating age-appropriate structural development at 26 weeks gestation.

Fetal MRI at 28 weeks gestation demonstrates a right-sided congenital diaphragmatic hernia (CDH). Herniation of liver parenchyma and loop of gallbladder are noted within the right hemithorax, with associated leftward deviation of the mediastinum and heart. The right lung is severely hypoplastic, and the left lung is moderately compressed. Total fetal lung volume is reduced for 28 weeks. Intracranial evaluation demonstrates a normal atrial diameter of 5.8 mm and normal, age-appropriate gyration and sulcation.

All other visualized anatomical structures are free of congenital defects. Impression: Right-sided congenital diaphragmatic hernia with liver herniation, leading to moderate pulmonary hypoplasia. The fetal brain is unremarkable.

Fetal MRI at 28 weeks gestation demonstrates normal, age-appropriate intracranial development. The cerebral ventricles are normal and symmetric, with the lateral ventricular atria measuring 6.0 mm. The corpus callosum is fully formed, and the sulcation pattern, including the development of the parieto-occipital and calcarine fissures, is completely normal for 28 weeks. The posterior fossa structures, including the cerebellar vermis and fourth ventricle, are unremarkable. Fetal spine and visceral anatomy are normal.

Impression: Normal fetal MRI at 28 weeks gestation. No structural abnormalities of the brain, spine, or major organs identified.

Cardiac MRI demonstrates marked asymmetric septal hypertrophy, with the maximal septal thickness measuring 22 mm. The left ventricular ejection fraction is hyperdynamic at 75%. Prominent late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) is observed at the anterior and posterior RV-LV insertion points, indicative of myocardial fibrosis.

Impression: Findings are highly consistent with hypertrophic obstructive cardiomyopathy (HCM) with severe asymmetric septal hypertrophy and characteristic insertion point fibrosis.

The left ventricle is severely dilated with a left ventricular end-diastolic volume index (LVEDVI) of 145 mL/m². Global systolic dysfunction is present with a left ventricular ejection fraction of 24%. The right ventricle is also mildly dilated with a reduced ejection fraction of 40%. Late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) imaging demonstrates a thin, mid-wall linear enhancement pattern in the basal-to-mid interventricular septum.

Impression: Severe non-ischemic dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM) with biventricular systolic dysfunction and severe left ventricular dilatation. The mid-wall LGE pattern is characteristic of non-ischemic etiology and is associated with increased arrhythmic risk.

Cardiac MRI demonstrates normal internal cardiac anatomy and biventricular function. Left ventricular ejection fraction is 63% and right ventricular ejection fraction is 57%. There are no regional wall motion abnormalities, wall thickening, or perfusion defects. Late gadolinium enhancement imaging is negative for myocardial fibrosis or scar. The mediastinum and great vessels are unremarkable.

Impression: Unremarkable cardiac MRI examination. No evidence of myocardial ischemia, prior infarction, or structural cardiomyopathy.

Fetal MRI performed at 22 weeks gestation shows age-appropriate cerebral development. The cerebellar hemispheres, vermis, and brainstem appear intact and normal in morphology. The lateral ventricles are symmetric with an atrial width of 5.8 mm. Early primary sulcation, including the sylvian fissure development, is completely appropriate for this stage.

Impression: Unremarkable fetal brain MRI at 22 weeks. No structural brain abnormalities or abnormal fluid collections are identified.

Cardiac MRI evaluates suspected acute myocarditis. Findings demonstrate patchy, non-ischemic subepicardial late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) involving the lateral and inferolateral walls of the left ventricle. T2-weighted and T2-mapping sequences show corresponding areas of elevated T2 relaxation times and hyperintensity in the same distribution, indicating active myocardial edema. The left ventricular dimensions are normal, and global systolic function is mildly reduced with an ejection fraction of 50%.

Impression: Findings are highly characteristic of active acute myocarditis according to the updated Lake Louise Criteria, demonstrating both myocardial edema and non-ischemic injury (LGE) in the lateral left ventricular wall.

MR brain imaging reveals a non-enhancing, infiltrative, hyperintense T2/FLAIR lesion centered in the left frontal lobe cortex and subcortical white matter, measuring approximately 3.5 x 2.9 cm. The lesion does not show restricted diffusion or significant mass effect. Following administration of gadolinium, there is no evidence of nodular or ring-like enhancement, and perfusion sequences show no elevated cerebral blood volume.

Impression: Infiltrative, non-enhancing T2/FLAIR hyperintense left frontal lobe lesion, most consistent with a low-grade diffuse astrocytoma. Serial follow-up or neurosurgical consultation for biopsy is indicated.

Evaluation of the cerebellopontine angles demonstrates an avidly enhancing, ice-cream cone-shaped mass centered within the right internal auditory canal and extending into the CPA cistern, measuring 1.8 x 1.2 cm. There is widening of the IAC and mild compression of the right cerebellar peduncle.

Impression: Right vestibular schwannoma (acoustic neuroma) with mild mass effect on the adjacent brainstem.

MRI demonstrates a dural-based, extra-axial mass along the left frontal convexity measuring approximately 2.8 x 2.4 x 2.2 cm. The mass is isointense to grey matter on T1 and T2 sequences and shows intense, homogeneous enhancement with a prominent dural tail following intravenous contrast administration. Mild compression of the adjacent cerebral cortex and minimal surrounding edema are present.

Impression: Findings are highly suggestive of a benign meningioma. Mass effect on the adjacent brain parenchyma is noted, but there is no midline shift or herniation.

Fetal MRI at 28 weeks gestation demonstrates features of Dandy-Walker malformation. There is mild-to-moderate hypoplasia of the inferior cerebellar vermis and cystic dilation of the fourth ventricle, which freely communicates with an enlarged posterior fossa. The lateral ventricles show moderate dilation, with the atrial width measuring 12.1 mm on the left and 11.8 mm on the right. Sulcation is appropriate for 28 weeks gestation.

The remainder of the brainstem, cerebral hemispheres, and extracranial organs are unremarkable. Impression: Dandy-Walker variant characterized by vermian hypoplasia, a posterior fossa fluid collection, and associated mild-to-moderate ventriculomegaly.

Cardiac MRI was performed to evaluate for a structural cause of arrhythmias. The biventricular dimensions, wall thickness, and ejection fractions are within normal range for age (LVEF 59%, RVEF 54%). No late gadolinium enhancement, edema on T2 STIR, or fatty infiltration is seen in either the left or right ventricles.

Impression: Normal cardiac MRI. No morphologic or tissue characterization features of underlying cardiomyopathy or myocardial scar.

Cardiac MRI reveals significant concentric hypertrophy of both ventricles, with LV septal thickness measuring 17 mm and RV free wall thickness measuring 7 mm. The myocardium demonstrates diffuse, subendocardial late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) involving all walls in a non-coronary distribution, associated with difficulties in nulling the myocardial signal. The left ventricular ejection fraction is mildly reduced at 45%.

Impression: Diffuse, non-coronary subendocardial late gadolinium enhancement with concentric biventricular hypertrophy and abnormal myocardial nulling. These findings are highly characteristic of cardiac amyloidosis.

Fetal MRI at 30 weeks gestation reveals severe skeletal dysplasia. The long bones are extremely short and bowed, with the femur exhibiting a classic 'telephone receiver' shape. The thorax is severely narrow and bell-shaped, causing restriction of the developing lungs. There is also marked platyspondyly of the spine. The head appears relatively large with frontal bossing.

Impression: Severe skeletal dysplasia, most consistent with Thanatophoric Dysplasia Type I. The narrow thorax and resulting pulmonary hypoplasia are indicative of a highly guarded prognosis.

Fetal MRI at 30 weeks gestation demonstrates normal development of the fetal brain. Cortical folding and sulcation are entirely appropriate for 30 weeks, showing normal development of the parieto-occipital and calcarine fissures. The lateral ventricles are small and symmetric, measuring 6.3 mm at the atrium. The corpus callosum and brainstem are completely intact.

Impression: Unremarkable fetal MRI at 30 weeks gestation. No structural fetal anomalies are identified.

Cardiac MRI evaluates cardiac structures and function, demonstrating normal left and right ventricular volumes. Left ventricular ejection fraction is 63%, and right ventricular ejection fraction is 60%. Myocardial wall thickness is symmetric and within normal limits throughout. Multi-slice late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) sequences show no abnormal myocardial enhancement to suggest focal scar or fibrosis.

Impression: Unremarkable cardiac MRI. Normal biventricular size and function with no signs of myocardial injury, scarring, or infiltration.

Cardiac MRI shows asymmetric septal hypertrophy primarily involving the basal and mid-ventricular septum, with a maximum diastolic wall thickness of 21 mm. Left ventricular systolic function is hyperdynamic with an ejection fraction of 72%. Late gadolinium enhancement imaging demonstrates patchy, mid-myocardial enhancement at the RV insertion points and within the hypertrophied septal segments, suggesting myocardial fibrosis.

Impression: Phenotypic findings highly characteristic of hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM). Patchy late gadolinium enhancement noted, indicating focal myocardial fibrosis, a known substrate for arrhythmogenic risk.

MRI reveals a well-circumscribed, extra-axial mass arising along the left parasagittal dura, measuring 2.8 x 2.5 x 2.4 cm. The lesion is broad-based to the dura, demonstrates homogeneous vivid enhancement post-contrast, and shows a classic 'dural tail' sign. There is mild compression of the adjacent cerebral cortex but no significant vasogenic edema in the surrounding brain parenchyma.

Impression: Left parasagittal extra-axial mass, highly consistent with a benign meningioma. Mild mass effect on the adjacent left parietal cortex without significant surrounding edema.

Fetal MRI at 24 weeks gestation demonstrates a defect in the lumbosacral spine with a protruding meningeal sac, consistent with myelomeningocele. Intracranial evaluation reveals downward displacement of the cerebellar vermis into the foramen magnum (Chiari II malformation) and a classic banana-shaped cerebellum. The lateral ventricles show colpocephaly, with the posterior atrial horns measuring 11.8 mm. Cortical sulcation is appropriate for this gestational age.

Impression: Open neural tube defect (lumbosacral myelomeningocele) with secondary features of Chiari II malformation and mild bilateral ventriculomegaly.

The study demonstrates asymmetric septal hypertrophy, with the maximal septal thickness measuring 22 mm at the basal-to-mid septum. There is systolic anterior motion (SAM) of the anterior mitral valve leaflet, resulting in eccentric mitral regurgitation and dynamic left ventricular outflow tract (LVOT) obstruction. The left ventricular ejection fraction is hyperdynamic at 75%. Late gadolinium enhancement imaging reveals patchy hyperenhancement localized to the RV insertion points and within the hypertrophied septal segments.

Impression: Classic asymmetric hypertrophic obstructive cardiomyopathy (HOCM) with dynamic LVOT obstruction. Elevated LVEF with localized myocardial fibrosis at the RV insertion points.

MR imaging of the brain reveals a well-circumscribed, extra-axial mass arising from the right cerebellopontine angle, measuring 2.4 x 2.1 x 1.8 cm. The lesion is broadly based along the petrous bone and demonstrates homogeneous enhancement following contrast administration, with a classic 'dural tail' sign. There is mild mass effect on the adjacent cerebellar hemisphere and pons, without internal brainstem signal changes.

Impression: Right cerebellopontine angle extra-axial mass, classic for a meningioma. Stable appearance without high-risk features; neurosurgical consultation recommended.

High-resolution MRI of the brain, including 3D TOF MR angiography, was performed. The brain parenchyma is entirely normal in appearance, with no structural anomalies, mass lesions, infarcts, or hemorrhages. The 3D TOF MRA shows normal course and caliber of the anterior, middle, and posterior cerebral arteries, with no evidence of focal aneurysm or vascular malformation.

Impression: Completely unremarkable brain MRI and MR angiography. No intracranial aneurysm or vascular malformation identified.

Fetal MRI evaluated at 30 weeks gestation demonstrates complete absence of the corpus callosum. There is characteristic colpocephaly, with prominence and dilation of the occipital horns of the lateral ventricles. The left ventricular atrium measures 11.5 mm and the right measures 11.8 mm, consistent with mild ventriculomegaly. Probst bundles are visualized running parallel along the medial walls of the lateral ventricles. The sulcation pattern and operculization are appropriate for 30 weeks gestation.

Impression: Complete agenesis of the corpus callosum associated with mild bilateral colpocephaly/ventriculomegaly. No other intracranial anomalies or extra-axial fluid collections are identified. Prenatal counseling and postnatal neuroimaging are recommended to evaluate for syndromic associations.

Cardiac MRI was obtained for the assessment of suspected valvular heart disease. Cine and flow-quantification sequences show normal cardiac chamber sizes and symmetrical wall thickness. The left ventricular ejection fraction is 63%, and the right ventricular ejection fraction is 59%. No wall motion abnormalities, regional dyskinesis, or valvular abnormalities are identified.

Late gadolinium enhancement imaging reveals no area of pathologic myocardial enhancement or scarring. Phase-contrast flow analysis shows normal forward and retrograde flow volumes across both the aortic and mitral valves, with no significant regurgitant fraction. Impression: Normal cardiac MRI study showing preserved biventricular function and no evidence of valvular pathology or myocardial scarring.

Cardiac MRI demonstrates moderate dilation and severe dysfunction of the right ventricle, with a right ventricular ejection fraction (RVEF) of 32%. Regional wall motion analysis of the right ventricle shows regional dyskinesia and microaneurysmal outpouchings in the RV outflow tract and inferior wall. High-resolution T1-weighted images reveal focal areas of high signal intensity within the RV free wall, suggesting fatty infiltration. Patchy late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) is observed in the RV free wall. The left ventricular dimensions and ejection fraction (LVEF 55%) are within normal limits.

Impression: Findings are highly suggestive of arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy (ARVC/D), demonstrating classic morphological and functional RV abnormalities including dyskinesia and fatty infiltration.

Brain MRI reveals an ill-defined, non-enhancing T2/FLAIR hyperintense mass within the left temporal lobe, measuring 3.1 x 2.6 cm. The mass involves both cortical and subcortical regions, without significant associated mass effect, midline shift, or vasogenic edema. No diffusion restriction or hemorrhage is observed.

Impression: Left temporal lobe intra-axial mass, appearance most suggestive of a low-grade diffuse astrocytoma. Correlation with MR spectroscopy or surgical biopsy is recommended for definitive grading.

Fetal MRI at 29 weeks gestation demonstrates partial agenesis of the corpus callosum, with absence of the splenium and posterior body. There is mild colpocephaly, with the posterior horns of the lateral ventricles measuring 10.8 mm (right) and 10.5 mm (left). Cortical sulcation is appropriate for 29 weeks, showing normal cingulate gyri where the callosum is present.

No other intracranial or extracranial anomalies are identified. Impression: Partial agenesis of the corpus callosum with mild posterior colpocephaly. Recommend post-natal follow-up.

MRI of the heart demonstrates normal chamber size, volumes, and systolic function of both ventricles. Left ventricular end-diastolic volume is 112 mL and LVEF is 61%. Right ventricular end-diastolic volume is 108 mL and RVEF is 58%. No focal myocardial thinning, regional wall motion abnormalities, or areas of delayed enhancement are observed.

Impression: Unremarkable cardiac MRI. Normal biventricular volumes and function, and no evidence of late gadolinium enhancement to suggest myocardial scar.

Cardiac MRI was conducted as part of an workup for palpitations and lightheadedness. Multiplanar cine imaging shows normal ventricular volumes and wall thickness. Left ventricular ejection fraction is measured at 63% and right ventricular ejection fraction at 55%.

There is no evidence of myocardial edema, fibrosis, or infiltration on T1/T2 mapping or late gadolinium enhancement sequences. Coronary origins are normal and no shunts are identified. Impression: Normal cardiac MRI with well-preserved biventricular function and no signs of focal scar or structural heart disease.

Fetal MRI at 25 weeks gestation reveals classic features of Dandy-Walker malformation. There is severe hypoplasia of the cerebellar vermis with a markedly enlarged posterior fossa. The torcular herophili is elevated, and a large posterior fossa cyst communicates directly with the fourth ventricle. There is secondary mild ventriculomegaly with the lateral ventricles measuring 10.8 mm.

Impression: Dandy-Walker malformation with associated mild ventriculomegaly. Recommend prenatal neurosurgical counseling.

Fetal MRI at 23 weeks gestation demonstrates a dorsal lumbosacral neural tube defect with an open myelomeningocele sac. Associated Arnold-Chiari II malformation is visualized, characterized by a classic 'banana sign' of the compressed cerebellum, pointing caudally, and a 'lemon sign' representing frontal bone scalloping. The lateral ventricles show colpocephalic changes with the posterior horns measuring 11.2 mm.

Impression: Open lumbosacral neural tube defect with classic Chiari II malformation. Fetal surgery evaluation may be considered based on overall clinical criteria.

Fetal MRI at 31 weeks gestation reveals mild asymmetric ventriculomegaly. The right lateral ventricle atrium is dilated and measures 10.5 mm, whereas the left lateral ventricle atrium is within normal limits, measuring 8.4 mm. Parietotemporal opercularization is slightly delayed, though overall cerebral sulcation is appropriate for 31 weeks gestation.

The corpus callosum and posterior fossa structures are normal, and no periventricular cysts or areas of hemorrhage are identified. Impression: Mild, isolated right-sided fetal ventriculomegaly. Recommended follow-up ultrasound to monitor progression.

Fetal MRI at 22 weeks gestation demonstrates a neural tube defect characterized by closed sacral spina bifida and a small lipomyelomeningocele. No cerebellar descent or hindbrain herniation is observed, and the ventricles are normal with an atrial size of 6.0 mm. Sulcation is age-appropriate.

Impression: Closed sacral spina bifida with lipomyelomeningocele. The absence of Chiari II malformation is a favorable prognostic feature.

Fetal MRI at 22 weeks gestation demonstrates bilateral renal agenesis. No identifiable renal tissue or renal arteries are visualized in either renal fossa or within the pelvis. Severe anhydramnios is present, resulting in severe compression of the fetus and limiting fine detail visualization.

The thoracic cavity is small and constricted. The intracranial structures are visible, with the lateral ventricle atrium measuring 5.5 mm and showing normal smooth cortical contours. Impression: Bilateral renal agenesis with secondary severe anhydramnios and classic Potter sequence morphology.

Fetal MRI at 24 weeks gestation demonstrates a dorsal neural tube defect in the lumbosacral region, extending from L4 to S1. There is a visible herniation of the meninges and neural placode through a posterior spinal defect, consistent with a myelomeningocele. Intracranial findings are characteristic of an Arnold-Chiari II malformation, showing downward displacement of the cerebellar vermis and medulla into the cervical canal. The cerebellum appears compressed (banana sign), and there is bifrontal narrowing of the cranium (lemon sign). The lateral ventricles are moderately dilated, with the left atrium measuring 11.2 mm.

Impression: Lumbosacral myelomeningocele at 24 weeks gestation with classic features of Arnold-Chiari II malformation and associated moderate ventriculomegaly.

Brain MRI shows ventriculomegaly out of proportion to the degree of cerebral sulcal enlargement. There is prominent widening of the lateral and third ventricles, with narrowing of the sulci at the high convexities and parasagittal regions. A flow void is visualized within the cerebral aqueduct on T2-weighted imaging, indicative of hyperdynamic cerebrospinal fluid flow.

Impression: Ventriculomegaly out of proportion to sulcal prominence, suggestive of normal pressure hydrocephalus (NPH). Clinical correlation with the triad of gait disturbance, cognitive decline, and urinary urgency is recommended.

Phase-contrast velocity mapping demonstrates a significant regurgitant jet originating from the mitral valve during systole, secondary to posterior leaflet prolapse (P2 segment). The calculated mitral regurgitant volume is 46 mL with a regurgitant fraction of 38%, consistent with severe mitral regurgitation. The left atrium is moderately dilated (volume index of 48 mL/m²), but left ventricular function remains compensated with an EF of 61%.

Impression: Severe mitral regurgitation secondary to posterior leaflet prolapse. The left ventricle is not dilated, and global systolic function is preserved.

MRI of the brain and sella turcica demonstrates a well-circumscribed, soft-tissue mass arising from the pituitary fossa, measuring approximately 2.1 x 1.8 x 1.5 cm. The mass expands the sella, extends suprasellar, and causes mild elevation and compression of the optic chiasm. The lesion is isointense on T1-weighted images and enhances moderately but heterogeneously compared to the normal pituitary gland.

Impression: Pituitary macroadenoma with suprasellar extension and mild compression of the optic chiasm. Clinical correlation for visual field deficits and endocrine workup is advised.

Brain MRI demonstrates a crescent-shaped extra-axial fluid collection along the right frontoparietal convexity, measuring up to 1.4 cm in maximal depth. The collection displays heterogeneous signal on T1 and T2-weighted images, consistent with a chronic subdural hematoma with acute-on-chronic hemorrhage. There is associated mass effect, with compression of the right lateral ventricle and 5 mm of leftward midline shift.

Impression: Right frontoparietal chronic subdural hematoma with evidence of recent re-bleeding (acute-on-chronic subdural hematoma) and moderate mass effect on adjacent structures.

MRI of the brain demonstrates a diffuse, ill-defined T2/FLAIR hyperintense lesion involving the left frontal lobe cortex and subcortical white matter, measuring approximately 5.2 x 4.0 cm. The lesion exhibits no restricted diffusion and no significant enhancement following contrast administration. There is mild mass effect with effacement of the adjacent frontal sulci.

Impression: Diffuse low-grade glioma, such as a low-grade astrocytoma. Follow-up imaging or neurosurgical biopsy is recommended for histological confirmation.

MRI of the brain demonstrates multiple discrete, ovoid T2/FLAIR hyperintense lesions within the periventricular, juxtacortical, and infratentorial white matter. Several of these lesions are oriented perpendicular to the lateral ventricles, demonstrating a classic 'Dawson's fingers' appearance. Following administration of gadolinium, two of the periventricular lesions show active nodular enhancement.

Impression: Demyelinating plaques scattered throughout the cerebrum and cerebellum, with active enhancement indicating areas of blood-brain barrier breakdown. The imaging features and distribution are highly characteristic of active multiple sclerosis.

Cardiac MRI evaluates a patient with suspected aortic pathology. There is a discrete, severe narrowing of the descending thoracic aorta just distal to the origin of the left subclavian artery, with an internal lumen diameter of 7 mm. Marked collateral circulation is observed flowing through dilated internal mammary and intercostal arteries. Moderate concentric left ventricular hypertrophy is present with a preserved EF of 58%.

No other congenital cardiovascular anomalies are visualized. Impression: Classic anatomical and functional evidence of severe coarctation of the aorta with extensive collateral vascularization and secondary left ventricular hypertrophy.

MR imaging of the heart demonstrates a significant zone of subendocardial late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) involving the mid-to-apical anterior and anteroseptal walls, consistent with a prior myocardial infarction in the LAD coronary artery territory. The left ventricle is mildly dilated with an end-diastolic volume of 185 mL and shows regional hypokinesia of the infarcted segments. Left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) is calculated at 38%.

Impression: Prior ischemic injury involving the LAD territory with associated regional wall motion abnormalities and mildly reduced left ventricular systolic function. No evidence of active myocardial edema or microvascular obstruction.

Cardiac MRI shows a large secundum atrial septal defect (ASD) measuring approximately 1.8 cm in diameter, which is associated with a significant left-to-right shunt. This has resulted in marked right ventricular and right atrial dilation. The right ventricular end-diastolic volume index is elevated at 112 mL/m2, although RV systolic function remains preserved with an ejection fraction of 52%.

Impression: Large secundum atrial septal defect with significant left-to-right shunt causing moderate right-sided chamber enlargement. No evidence of pulmonary arterial hypertension on phase-contrast imaging.

Cardiac MR demonstrates marked symmetric thickening of the left ventricular walls, with a septal thickness of 1.9 cm and a posterior wall thickness of 1.7 cm. The left ventricular ejection fraction is moderately reduced at 44% with a restrictive filling pattern. There is diffuse, global subendocardial late gadolinium enhancement that does not conform to any single vascular territory, along with abnormal myocardial and blood pool nulling kinetics.

Impression: Highly characteristic findings of cardiac amyloidosis, including diffuse global subendocardial LGE and significant bi-ventricular wall thickening. Findings correlate strongly with systemic amyloid disease.

Cardiac MRI reveals normal chamber sizes and preserved overall left ventricular ejection fraction at 56%. However, T2-weighted and T1-mapping sequences demonstrate focal area of elevated T2 relaxation times and elevated myocardial native T1 values in the subepicardial lateral wall, indicative of active myocardial edema. Late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) imaging shows patchy, non-ischemic subepicardial hyperenhancement in the same segments of the basal to mid-lateral LV free wall.

Impression: Findings are highly suggestive of acute myocarditis involving the lateral LV free wall, fulfilling the Lake Louise criteria with evidence of both myocardial edema and non-ischemic injury/scar.

There is significant ventriculomegaly involving the lateral, third, and fourth ventricles, which is out of proportion to the degree of cerebral sulcal enlargement. Prominent upward bowing of the corpus callosum is present. There is a visible flow void within the cerebral aqueduct on T2-weighted sequences, with no evidence of mechanical obstruction.

Impression: Ventriculomegaly out of proportion to cortical atrophy, highly suggestive of normal pressure hydrocephalus (NPH) in this clinical context.

Cardiac MRI reveals standard biventricular anatomy and normal systolic function. Left ventricular ejection fraction is calculated at 60% with an end-diastolic volume of 130 mL. The right ventricular ejection fraction is 57%. No abnormal patterns of perfusion or late gadolinium enhancement are present, and the heart valves appear morphologically normal.

Impression: Unremarkable cardiac MRI study. No evidence of myocardial ischemia, structural disease, or focal fibrotic replacement.

Cardiac MRI evaluates a patient with a history of repaired Tetralogy of Fallot. There is severe dilatation of the right ventricle (EDVI 165 mL/m2) and right ventricular outflow tract (RVOT). Phase-contrast flow measurement in the main pulmonary artery reveals severe pulmonary regurgitation with a regurgitant fraction of 48%. The right ventricular ejection fraction is mildly reduced at 43%.

Impression: Severe pulmonary regurgitation with significant right ventricular dilatation and mild right ventricular systolic dysfunction. Findings indicate potential candidacy for pulmonary valve replacement.

MRI of the brain reveals a non-enhancing, well-circumscribed, infiltrative T2/FLAIR hyperintense lesion in the left temporal lobe, measuring approximately 2.5 x 2.2 cm. There is minimal surrounding mass effect and no associated vasogenic edema, hemorrhage, or restricted diffusion. No enhancement is seen on post-contrast sequences.

Impression: Non-enhancing cortical/subcortical left temporal lobe mass, suspicious for a low-grade glial neoplasm, such as a diffuse astrocytoma. Follow-up or biopsy is recommended.

MRI brain demonstrates hyperintense signal within the sulci of the bilateral frontal lobes and the anterior interhemispheric fissure on FLAIR sequences. Corresponding gradient echo (GRE) and susceptibility-weighted imaging (SWI) show marked blooming artifact within the same sulci, indicating acute subarachnoid blood. No underlying mass lesion or vascular malformation is definitively identified on this non-angiographic study.

Impression: Acute subarachnoid hemorrhage localized predominantly in the bilateral frontal and interhemispheric sulci. Emergent CT angiography (CTA) or catheter angiography is recommended to evaluate for a ruptured intracranial aneurysm.

There is a prominent, well-demarcated sellar and suprasellar mass measuring approximately 2.3 x 1.9 x 2.1 cm. The mass expands the sella turcica and abuts the optic chiasm, causing mild superior displacement and compression. The lesion demonstrates heterogeneous enhancement post-contrast with non-enhancing cystic spaces.

Impression: Sellar and suprasellar mass consistent with a pituitary macroadenoma with optic chiasm displacement. Recommend formal visual field testing and endocrine workup.

Cardiac MRI evaluates suspected aortic pathology. There is a discrete narrowing of the proximal descending thoracic aorta, just distal to the origin of the left subclavian artery, with a minimum diameter of 8 mm. Prominent collateral intercostal arteries are visualized. Left ventricular mass is increased (LV mass index 115 g/m2) indicating concentric hypertrophy, but the ejection fraction is preserved at 56%.

Impression: Classical findings of severe post-ductal coarctation of the aorta with significant left ventricular concentric hypertrophy.

MR imaging of the brain demonstrates multiple discrete, ovoid T2/FLAIR hyperintense lesions within the periventricular, juxtacortical, and infratentorial white matter. Several of these lesions are oriented perpendicular to the lateral ventricles, consistent with Dawson's fingers. Post-contrast imaging demonstrates active, nodular enhancement of two periventricular lesions in the left parietal lobe, indicating active demyelination with blood-brain barrier breakdown.

Impression: Multiple demyelinating-type white matter lesions demonstrating spatial dissemination. The presence of both enhancing and non-enhancing lesions indicates dissemination in time, strongly supportive of active relapsing-remitting multiple sclerosis.

Multiple foci of T2* gradient-echo and SWI blooming are noted in the lobar cortices, particularly within the parietal and occipital regions. A small, subacute localized lobar hemorrhage is also identified in the left parietal lobe, with minimal surrounding edema.

Impression: Multiple lobar microhemorrhages and a subacute lobar hemorrhage, highly indicative of cerebral amyloid angiopathy.

MR imaging of the brain was performed. There is diffuse, symmetric prominence of the cerebral sulci, Sylvian fissures, and lateral ventricles, consistent with age-appropriate parenchymal volume loss. No acute territorial ischemia, parenchymal hemorrhage, or mass lesions are identified. Scattered, small, punctate T2/FLAIR hyperintensities are noted in the deep white matter, likely reflecting mild chronic microvascular ischemic changes.

Impression: Normal age-appropriate brain MRI, showing mild cerebral volume loss and chronic microvascular white matter changes, without acute intracranial pathology.

The study demonstrates significant dilation of the right atrium and the right ventricle (RVEDVI 115 ml/m2). A large secundum-type atrial septal defect (ASD) is noted measuring approximately 18 mm. Velocity-encoded phase-contrast imaging reveals a significant left-to-right shunt across the interatrial septum, with an estimated systemic-to-pulmonary shunt ratio (Qp:Qs) of 1.7. Left ventricular parameters remain within the normal range.

Impression: Large secundum atrial septal defect with significant left-to-right shunt and resulting moderate right heart volume overload. Structural repair is recommended based on Qp:Qs measurements.

Fetal MRI at 21 weeks gestation demonstrates a severe holoprosencephaly spectrum. There is a single, large primitive midline ventricle (monoventricle) with absence of the septum pellucidum, corpus callosum, and interhemispheric fissure. The thalami are fused across the midline. Facial structures show hypotelorism and a cleft lip/palate.

The spine, thoracic structures, and abdomen are otherwise normal. Amniotic fluid volume is normal. Impression: Alobar holoprosencephaly with associated facial clefting, representing a severe midline developmental defect.

Multiplanar, multisequence brain MRI is unremarkable. No areas of restricted diffusion are present to suggest acute ischemic stroke. No abnormal enhancement is observed post-contrast. Ventricles and extra-axial spaces are normal in size and configuration for the patient's age.

Impression: Normal brain MRI. No evidence of mass lesion, structural abnormality, or vascular occlusion.

A large, necrotic, ring-enhancing mass is centered in the right temporal lobe, measuring 4.5 x 3.8 x 3.5 cm. Extensive surrounding vasogenic edema is present, causing 8 mm of leftward midline shift and subfalcine herniation. Compression of the right lateral ventricle is noted.

Impression: Aggressive, intra-axial ring-enhancing temporal lobe lesion with significant mass effect, highly suspicious for glioblastoma multiforme.

Cardiac MRI demonstrates localized dilation and dyskinesis of the right ventricular outflow tract (RVOT) and the RV apex. There is regional thinned myocardium of the right ventricle with prominent trabeculations. Fat-water separation sequences suggest focal intramyocardial fat infiltration within the RV free wall. The right ventricular ejection fraction is reduced at 34%, and the left ventricular ejection fraction is preserved at 56%.

Impression: Features are highly suspicious for Arrhythmogenic Right Ventricular Cardiomyopathy (ARVC), meeting major task force criteria. Clinical correlation with ECG findings and family history is highly recommended.

There is a small defect in the membranous portion of the interventricular septum, measuring approximately 6 mm in diameter. Phase-contrast flow measurements demonstrate a small left-to-right shunt with a Qp:Qs ratio of 1.25. The left and right ventricular volumes are within normal limits (LVEDVI 72 mL/m²), and biventricular function is well-preserved.

Impression: Small, membranous ventricular septal defect (VSD) with a hemodynamically insignificant left-to-right shunt. No significant ventricular volume overload or remodeling is visualized at this time.

Fetal MRI at 25 weeks gestation demonstrates classic features of Congenital High Airway Obstruction Syndrome (CHAOS). There is severe, symmetric enlargement and hyperintensity of both fetal lungs, which are herniating out of the thoracic cavity, causing flattening and inversion of the diaphragm. The trachea is markedly dilated distal to a high-grade laryngeal obstruction. Ascites is present within the abdominal cavity, suggesting early non-immune hydrops.

The intracranial structures show normal age-appropriate gyration, and the ventricles measure 7.1 mm. Impression: Congenital High Airway Obstruction Syndrome (CHAOS) with secondary pulmonary hyperinflation, diaphragmatic inversion, and early fetal ascites. Urgent high-risk maternal-fetal medicine consultation is indicated.

Fetal MRI at 24 weeks gestation demonstrates an occipital encephalocele. There is a defect in the midline occipital bone through which a small sac herniates, containing cerebrospinal fluid and a small amount of dysplastic cerebellar tissue. The lateral ventricles are moderately dilated, with atrial measurements of 12.2 mm on the left and 11.8 mm on the right.

The spine is intact. Chest and abdominal organs are within normal limits. Impression: Occipital encephalocele with associated ventriculomegaly. Suggest pediatric neurosurgery and maternal-fetal medicine counseling.

There is significant dilation of the lateral and third ventricles, out of proportion to the degree of cerebral sulcal enlargement. A hyperdynamic CSF flow void is noted through the aqueduct of Sylvius. There is mild periventricular signal hyperintensity, consistent with transependymal CSF migration. The corpus callosum appears stretched and elevated.

Impression: Ventriculomegaly disproportionate to sulcal thinning, indicative of normal pressure hydrocephalus (NPH) given the clinical triad. Correlate with clinical gait evaluation and high-volume lumbar puncture.

The cardiac chambers demonstrate normal dimensions, wall thickness, and contractile function. Left ventricular ejection fraction is 65% and right ventricular ejection fraction is 61%. No areas of delayed enhancement or myocardial edema are identified, and the valvular structures are unremarkable.

Impression: Normal cardiac MRI with excellent biventricular systolic function and no evidence of structural heart disease.

MR imaging of the brain reveals two discrete, well-demarcated ring-enhancing lesions. The larger lesion is located in the right cerebellar hemisphere, measuring 1.8 x 1.5 cm, and is surrounded by extensive vasogenic edema. The smaller lesion is located in the left frontal lobe junction, measuring 0.8 cm. Both lesions demonstrate central necrosis and peripheral enhancement.

Impression: Multiple enhancing intra-axial lesions with surrounding vasogenic edema, highly concerning for metastatic disease. Correlation with systemic imaging is highly recommended.

MRI examination of the heart demonstrates physiological biventricular chamber volumes and preserved systolic function. The left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) is calculated at 60%, and the right ventricular ejection fraction (RVEF) is 55%. There is no evidence of regional wall motion abnormality, focal hypertrophy, or late gadolinium enhancement. The cardiac valves appear thin, mobile, and functionally intact.

Impression: Normal cardiac MRI with normal biventricular volumes and function. No evidence of myocardial scar, active inflammation, or significant valvular pathology.

Fetal MRI at 29 weeks gestation demonstrates entirely normal development of the central nervous system. Symmetric lateral ventricles are noted, measuring 6.1 mm at the level of the atrium. Brainstem, cerebellum, and corpus callosum are fully formed and appropriate in size and signal intensity. Fetal chest and abdomen are unremarkable.

Impression: Normal fetal MRI study demonstrating age-appropriate structural brain and somatic development without anomalies.

Fetal MRI at 30 weeks gestation demonstrates a highly abnormal left kidney. The left renal fossa contains a large kidney replaced by multiple, non-communicating cysts of varying sizes, the largest measuring 1.8 cm. There is no normal renal parenchyma seen on the left. The right kidney is normal in size and appearance with preserved corticomedullary differentiation. Amniotic fluid volume is within normal limits.

Impression: Unilateral left multicystic dysplastic kidney (MCDK). Normal contralateral right kidney and normal amniotic fluid volume.

Fetal MRI at 33 weeks gestation reveals a large right-sided congenital diaphragmatic hernia. The liver and portions of the small and large bowel have herniated into the right hemithorax, resulting in severe compression of the left lung and significant leftward mediastinal shift. The fetal brain exhibits a normal atrial width of 5.9 mm and normal, mature sulcation.

Impression: Right-sided congenital diaphragmatic hernia containing the liver. Severe mediastinal shift is noted. Normal fetal brain development.

Magnetic resonance imaging of the brain shows preserved gray-white matter differentiation and normal signal pathways. There are no acute infarcts, intracranial hemorrhages, or areas of pathologic contrast enhancement. Ventricles and sulci are within normal limits for the patient's age. The mastoid sinuses and paranasal sinuses are clear, and the visualized orbits are unremarkable.

Impression: Unremarkable MR study of the brain with no acute intra-axial or extra-axial abnormalities.

Fetal MRI at 28 weeks gestation reveals bilateral fetal hydronephrosis. The left renal pelvis measures 11.2 mm and the right measures 9.5 mm in the anteroposterior diameter. No ureteral dilation or bladder wall thickening is noted. Intracranial structures, sulcation, and lateral ventricles are completely normal and symmetric.

Impression: Bilateral moderate fetal hydronephrosis without evidence of lower urinary tract obstruction. Recommend postnatal ultrasound tracking.

Fetal MRI at 29 weeks gestation demonstrates partial agenesis of the corpus callosum. The rostrum and splenium are absent, with only a short segment of the body visualized. There is mild colpocephaly with dilation of the posterior horns of the lateral ventricles, with the atrium measuring 13.5 mm. Cortical sulcation is slightly delayed for gestational age, showing fewer secondary sulci than expected.

Extracranial organs and fetal growth are otherwise normal. Impression: Partial agenesis of the corpus callosum with mild ventriculomegaly and delayed sulcation.

Cardiac MRI demonstrates normal left and right ventricular volumes and systolic function. The left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) is estimated at 62%, and the right ventricular ejection fraction (RVEF) is 58%. No regional wall motion abnormalities are present. Myocardial perfusion is normal under resting conditions, and there is no evidence of late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) to suggest myocardial scarring, fibrosis, or infiltration.

Impression: Completely normal cardiac MRI. Normal ventricular dimensions and biventricular systolic function with no evidence of myocardial scar or fibrosis.

Magnetic resonance imaging of the heart was performed with standard cine, perfusion, and late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) sequences. The left ventricle is normal in size and demonstrates normal systolic function, with a calculated ejection fraction of 62% and no regional wall motion abnormalities. Right ventricular size and systolic function are also normal with an ejection fraction of 57%. No myocardial edema is demonstrated on T2-weighted imaging, and there is no evidence of myocardial late gadolinium enhancement to suggest focal scar or fibrosis.

Impression: Normal cardiac MRI study. There is no evidence of myocardial scar, inflammation, or structural heart disease, and global biventricular systolic function is well-preserved.

Cardiac MRI demonstrates normal cardiac chamber dimensions and wall thickness. The left ventricular end-diastolic volume is 135 mL, with a preserved ejection fraction of 64% and no regional wall motion abnormalities. The right ventricle is also normal in size and function, with an ejection fraction of 58%. There is no evidence of myocardial edema on T2-weighted imaging, and perfusion is homogeneous without focal defects.

Impression: Normal cardiac MRI study. No evidence of myocardial infarction, scar tissue, congenital anomaly, or active inflammatory process is identified. Myocardial viability and function are fully preserved.

Cardiac MRI demonstrates severe aortic stenosis with a heavily calcified and thickened trileaflet aortic valve showing restricted mobility. The planimetered aortic valve area is restricted to approximately 0.8 cm². There is moderate concentric left ventricular hypertrophy with a diastolic septal thickness of 15 mm, and the left ventricular end-diastolic volume is preserved. Left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) is calculated at 55%.

Impression: Severe calcific aortic stenosis with associated moderate concentric left ventricular hypertrophy. Systolic function is preserved, and there is no evidence of subendocardial infarction on late enhancement imaging.

Fetal MRI at 33 weeks gestation reveals a well-defined cystic lesion in the posterior fossa measuring 2.5 x 1.8 x 2.0 cm. The cyst is located retrocerebellar and exerts mild mass effect on the cerebellar hemispheres, but the cerebellar vermis is intact and fully formed. The lateral ventricles are mildly prominent, with the atria measuring 8.2 mm.

The cerebral sulcation and operculization are normal for 33 weeks. Visualized spinal cord and skeletal structures are normal. Impression: Retrocerebellar posterior fossa arachnoid cyst with mild mass effect on the cerebellum and mild ventriculomegaly; vermis is normal.

Cardiac MRI demonstrates normal cardiac chamber sizes and symmetrical wall thickness. Left ventricular end-diastolic volume is within normal limits at 148 mL, and the left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) is calculated at 60%. Right ventricular volume and systolic function are also preserved (RVEF of 56%). There are no regional wall motion abnormalities. T1 and T2 mapping parameters are within standard reference ranges, and there is no evidence of late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) to suggest myocardial scarring, infiltrative disease, or active myocarditis.

Impression: Normal cardiac MRI study. Normal biventricular size, thickness, and function with no evidence of myocardial scar or inflammation.

MRI of the brain reveals a ring-enhancing lesion in the left frontal lobe measuring 2.2 cm in diameter. The lesion has a thin, smooth rim that enhances uniformly. The center of the lesion demonstrates marked restricted diffusion (hyperintense on DWI, hypointense on ADC). Moderate surrounding vasogenic edema and sulcal effacement are noted.

Impression: Left frontal ring-enhancing lesion with central restricted diffusion, highly suspicious for an acute cerebral abscess. Clinical correlation with infectious markers is advised.

Cardiac MRI demonstrates patchy, mid-myocardial, and epicardial late gadolinium enhancement involving the basal-to-mid lateral and inferolateral left ventricular wall. T2-weighted STIR images show elevated signal intensity in the same regions, reflecting active myocardial edema. The left ventricular chamber is normal in size with mild hypokinesis of the lateral wall; overall ejection fraction is calculated at 51%.

Impression: Findings are highly consistent with acute myocarditis, satisfying the Lake Louise criteria with matching edema on T2 and subepicardial/mid-wall fibrosis on LGE imaging.

Magnetic resonance imaging of the brain was performed using multiplanar, multisequence techniques. Brain parenchyma demonstrates normal signal intensity and morphology. There is no evidence of acute infarction, hemorrhage, or mass lesion. The ventricles and subarachnoid spaces are normal in size and configuration for the patient's age. The major vascular flow voids are preserved.

Impression: Unremarkable MRI examination of the brain. No intracranial abnormality identified to explain the patient's clinical symptoms of tension-type headache.

MR evaluation of the brain shows unremarkable intracranial anatomy. The brain parenchyma is free from focal lesions, restricted diffusion, or abnormal post-contrast enhancement. Ventricles and sulci are normal in caliber. The visual pathways, internal auditory canals, and craniovertebral junction are within normal limits.

Impression: Normal MR imaging of the brain. No etiology for chronic head pain is demonstrated.

Cardiac MRI demonstrates normal cardiac morphology and function. The left ventricular end-diastolic volume is within the normal range for age and body surface area. Left ventricular ejection fraction is 58%, and right ventricular ejection fraction is 55%. No late gadolinium enhancement is noted, and there is no evidence of valvular dysfunction or pericardial disease.

Impression: Normal cardiac MRI study. Normal biventricular function and size with no signs of myocardial infarction or structural abnormality.

MR imaging of the brain reveals descent of the cerebellar tonsils below the level of the foramen magnum by approximately 7.5 mm. The tonsils appear pointed or peg-like. There is associated crowding at the craniovertebral junction with partial effacement of the cisterna magna. The ventricles are normal in size. A screening sagittal view of the cervical spine reveals no evidence of syrinx.

Impression: Chiari I malformation with 7.5 mm of tonsillar ectopia and crowding at the foramen magnum. No syringomyelia is identified on the visualized upper cervical cord.

MRI of the internal auditory canals and brain demonstrates a well-defined, enhancing mass arising from the left vestibular nerve within the internal auditory canal and extending into the cerebellopontine angle cistern. The lesion measures approximately 1.6 x 1.2 cm, producing a classic 'ice cream cone' configuration. There is mild compression of the adjacent middle cerebellar peduncle, but no significant hydrocephalus.

Impression: Left-sided vestibular schwannoma (acoustic neuroma) with cerebellopontine angle extension. Otolaryngology/neurosurgical consultation is advised for management options.

The study demonstrates severe dilatation of the left ventricle (LVEDV of 230 ml) accompanied by diffuse global hypokinesis. The left ventricular ejection fraction is severely reduced at 28%. Mild right ventricular dilatation is also present with an ejection fraction of 42%. Late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) demonstrates thin, linear mid-myocardial hyperintensity in the basal-to-mid interventricular septum.

Impression: Severe non-ischemic dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM). The presence of mid-wall late gadolinium enhancement is consistent with a non-ischemic etiology and carries prognostic implications for heart failure progression.

Cardiac MRI shows diffuse, concentric hypertrophy of the left ventricle with a septal thickness of 18 mm. The left ventricular ejection fraction is moderately reduced at 42%. Diffuse, circumferential subendocardial late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) is present, along with abnormal myocardial and blood pool gadolinium kinetics, making nulling of the myocardium difficult. Elevated native T1 mapping times and extracellular volume (ECV) of 48% are observed.

Impression: Findings are highly characteristic of cardiac amyloidosis, demonstrating classic diffuse subendocardial LGE and significantly increased extracellular volume.

Brain MRI reveals diffuse cerebral and cerebellar volume loss with corresponding compensatory ventricular enlargement, within limits typical of the patient's age. Confluent and patchy T2/FLAIR hyperintensities are noted within the bilateral periventricular and deep white matter. No acute restricted diffusion or pathologically enhancing focal lesions are demonstrated.

Impression: Moderate chronic microvascular ischemic white matter disease. Diffuse age-appropriate cerebral parenchymal volume loss. No acute intracranial abnormality is observed.

MRI of the brain was obtained for workup of progressive left-sided hearing loss. Assessment of the posterior fossa reveals normal appearance of the brainstem and cerebellum. Thin-slice cranial nerve imaging through the internal auditory canals shows symmetric, normal-caliber vestibulocochlear and facial nerves. There is no evidence of cerebellopontine angle mass or vestibular schwannoma.

Impression: Unremarkable brain MRI. Specifically, no cerebellopontine angle mass or vestibular schwannoma identified.

Fetal MRI at 22 weeks gestation demonstrates normal intracranial and extracranial development. The cerebral ventricles are normal in size, with the atrium of the lateral ventricles measuring 5.4 mm. The corpus callosum is visualized and is structurally intact. Cerebral sulcation and gyration are appropriate for a 22-week gestational age fetus.

Fetal organs including the heart, lungs, stomach, and kidneys are unremarkable in appearance. The spine is intact and there is no evidence of neural tube defects. Impression: Normal fetal MRI study showing expected development for 22 weeks gestation.

Fetal MRI at 24 weeks gestation reveals an open neural tube defect in the lumbosacral region. There is a defect in the posterior element of the lower lumbar and sacral spine with a herniated myelomeningocele sac measuring 2.4 cm. Associated Chiari II malformation is present, characterized by cerebellar tonsillar herniation through the foramen magnum and a banana-shaped cerebellum. Ventricular atrial measurements show bilateral ventriculomegaly, with both atria measuring approximately 12.5 mm.

The remainder of the fetal structures are normal, and the extremities show limited movement. Impression: Open lumbosacral myelomeningocele with classic Chiari II malformation features and moderate bilateral ventriculomegaly.

Fetal MRI at 31 weeks gestation reveals mild asymmetric ventriculomegaly. The left lateral ventricle atrium measures 11.2 mm (mild ventriculomegaly), while the right lateral ventricle atrium measures 8.4 mm (within normal range). The third and fourth ventricles are normal. Sulcation pattern is age-appropriate with normal temporal and parietal operculization.

The remainder of the brain parenchyma, corpus callosum, and posterior fossa are unremarkable. Somatic structures are normal. Impression: Mild, isolated left-sided fetal ventriculomegaly. Suggest follow-up ultrasound to monitor progression.

Fetal MRI at 34 weeks gestation demonstrates a large, rounded, flow-void lesion in the midline posterior fossa, consistent with an aneurysmal dilation of the vein of Galen. There is secondary dilation of the straight sinus and superior sagittal sinus. Fetal echocardiography/chest MRI shows significant cardiomegaly and dilated superior vena cava, consistent with high-output cardiac overload. The lateral ventricles are slightly prominent, measuring 9.5 mm.

Cortical gyration is appropriate for 34 weeks. Impression: Vein of Galen malformation with signs of secondary cardiovascular volume overload and mild ventriculomegaly. Close monitoring and postnatal interventional neuroradiology evaluation planning are recommended.

Cardiac MRI reveals localized subepicardial and mid-myocardial late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) along the lateral and inferolateral walls of the left ventricle. T2-weighted triple IR imaging demonstrates increased signal intensity in the corresponding regions, consistent with localized myocardial edema. The left ventricular cavity size is within normal limits, with a borderline-reduced ejection fraction calculated at 51%.

Impression: Findings are highly characteristic of acute myocarditis involving the lateral left ventricular wall, meeting Lake Louise Criteria. Follow-up imaging is recommended in 3 to 6 months to assess for resolution of active inflammation and scar tissue formation.

Fetal MRI at 20 weeks gestation demonstrates normal development of the fetal central nervous system and viscera. The cerebral mantle shows early, normal lissencephalic appearance with appropriate sylvian fissure indentation for 20 weeks. The lateral ventricles are normal in size, with atrial widths of 5.5 mm. The brainstem, cerebellum, and spine are normal.

The fetal heart, lungs, stomach, kidneys, and bladder are identified in their normal anatomic locations. Amniotic fluid volume is completely normal. Impression: Normal fetal MRI study at 20 weeks gestation showing expected structural anatomy.

Fetal MRI at 35 weeks gestation demonstrates advanced cortical gyration patterns that are highly appropriate for gestational age. The cerebral hemispheres are symmetric, with normal ventricular size (lateral ventricular atria measure 6.4 mm). The corpus callosum, brainstem, and cerebellar structures appear intact and completely unremarkable. The skull and scalp are intact, without any evidence of calvarial defect or cephalocele.

The fetal chest demonstrates symmetrical lung volumes, and the cardiac axis is normal. The intra-abdominal organs, including the stomach and kidneys, are normally positioned. Impression: Unremarkable fetal MRI at 35 weeks gestation, showing no evidence of structural, CNS, or extracranial anomalies.

MR imaging of the brain and craniocervical junction reveals downward herniation of the cerebellar tonsils below the level of the foramen magnum by approximately 7.5 mm. The cerebellar tonsils are peg-like in configuration. There is crowding at the level of the foramen magnum, but the cervical spinal cord demonstrates normal signal with no evidence of syrinx formation.

Impression: Chiari I malformation with 7.5 mm of cerebellar tonsillar ectopia and crowding at the craniocervical junction. No syrinx is noted in the visualized cervical spine.

Fetal MRI at 23 weeks gestation demonstrates complete absence of the left kidney in the renal fossa and pelvis, indicating left renal agenesis. The right kidney is present but is compensatory enlarged, measuring 3.4 cm in length, with mild pelvicalyceal dilation (renal pelvis diameter of 5.5 mm). Amniotic fluid volume is borderline low (mild oligohydramnios). Fetal biometry is otherwise appropriate.

Intracranial anatomy is unremarkable with normal sulcation and lateral ventricular atrial measurements of 6.0 mm. Impression: Left renal agenesis with compensatory hypertrophy and mild hydronephrosis of the solitary right kidney. Close monitoring of amniotic fluid volume is advised.
