Phase-contrast flow analysis demonstrates a small left-to-right shunt with a calculated Qp:Qs ratio of 1.15:1. There is no evidence of left or right ventricular volume overload or hypertrophy. Left ventricular end-diastolic volume is 135 mL, and the left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) is 61%. Right ventricular dimensions and function are completely normal.

Impression: Small, restrictive muscular ventricular septal defect (VSD) with a hemodynamically insignificant left-to-right shunt. No evidence of chamber enlargement or ventricular dysfunction.

Cardiac MRI demonstrates abnormal morphology and function of the right ventricle. The right ventricle is severely dilated (RVEDV index of 122 mL/m²) with areas of dyskinesis and microaneurysmal sacculations in the RV free wall, particularly in the RV outflow tract. The right ventricular ejection fraction (RVEF) is reduced at 34%. Late gadolinium enhancement imaging shows regional mid-wall fibrosis in the RV free wall and apical segments.

Impression: Features are highly characteristic of Arrhythmogenic Right Ventricular Cardiomyopathy (ARVC), meeting major Task Force criteria. Right ventricular dilation, dyskinesis, and regional scar are identified.

Cardiac magnetic resonance imaging demonstrates normal left and right ventricular chamber dimensions and preserved global systolic function. The left ventricular end-diastolic volume is 135 mL, and the ejection fraction is calculated at 62%. The right ventricular ejection fraction is also normal at 58% without regional wall motion abnormalities. Myocardial perfusion sequences show no inducible ischemia, and late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) imaging reveals no myocardial scarring, fibrosis, or past injury.

Impression: Normal cardiac MRI study. No evidence of cardiomyopathy, valvular dysfunction, or myocardial scarring.

Fetal MRI at 26 weeks gestation. Evaluation of the fetal thorax demonstrates a large left-sided congenital diaphragmatic hernia, with herniation of the stomach and multiple loops of small bowel into the left hemithorax. This causes a significant rightward mediastinal shift and compression of the developing fetal lungs. The observed-to-expected total lung volume is severely reduced at 35%. Intracranial anatomy is unremarkable, with appropriate sulcation for 26 weeks and a normal ventricular atrial width measuring 6.0 mm.

Impression: Left-sided congenital diaphragmatic hernia with intrathoracic stomach herniation, severe mediastinal shift, and secondary pulmonary hypoplasia. Prenatal multidisciplinary consultation is indicated.

MR imaging of the brain with and without gadolinium contrast shows a large, irregularly marginated mass in the left temporal lobe measuring 4.2 x 3.8 x 3.5 cm. The mass exhibits thick, heterogeneous ring enhancement, central areas of necrosis, and extensive surrounding T2/FLAIR hyperintensity consistent with vasogenic edema. There is significant mass effect with a 6 mm right-to-left midline shift and partial effacement of the left lateral ventricle.

Impression: Large necrotic ring-enhancing mass in the left temporal lobe with surrounding vasogenic edema and midline shift. These findings are highly characteristic of a high-grade glioma (such as glioblastoma multiforme). Urgent neurosurgical consult is recommended.

Cardiac MRI shows diffuse thickening of the pericardial layers measuring up to 5 mm, demonstrating significant late gadolinium enhancement consistent with active inflammation. There is an associated moderate-to-large circumferential pericardial effusion measuring up to 1.8 cm. Real-time cine imaging during inspiration shows diastolic septal bounce, suggestive of early constrictive physiology. Left ventricular ejection fraction is 55%.

Impression: Active pericarditis with moderate circumferential pericardial effusion and MRI features suggestive of early constrictive pericardial physiology.

Fetal MRI at 32 weeks gestation demonstrates normal intracranial and systemic anatomy. The cerebral hemispheres exhibit highly symmetric sulcation and migration patterns expected for late third trimester. The ventricular system is small, with the atrial width measuring 6.0 mm. Brainstem and posterior fossa structures are unremarkable, and the chest, abdomen, and spine are fully intact.

Impression: Normal fetal MRI study showing age-appropriate brain development, gyration, and structural integrity without evidence of anomaly.

Brain MR imaging demonstrates ventriculomegaly out of proportion to the degree of cerebral sulcal thinning. The lateral and third ventricles are markedly dilated, and there is a prominent flow void within the aqueduct of Sylvius, suggesting hyperdynamic CSF flow. The cortical sulci at the vertex appear compressed or crowded, while the sylvian fissures are paradoxically dilated.

Impression: Ventriculomegaly and imaging features suggestive of normal pressure hydrocephalus (NPH). Clinical correlation with the classic triad of gait disturbance, cognitive decline, and urinary incontinence is recommended.

The study demonstrates severe dilatation of the left ventricle with global hypokinesis. The left ventricular end-diastolic volume is indexed at 145 mL/m² and the ejection fraction is severely depressed at 26%. There is mid-wall linear late gadolinium enhancement in the basal interventricular septum, which is characteristic of non-ischemic dilated cardiomyopathy.

Impression: Non-ischemic dilated cardiomyopathy with severe global left ventricular dysfunction and significant ventricular remodeling. No evidence of obstructive coronary territory infarction.

Cardiac MRI reveals global dilation of both the left and right ventricles, with associated thinning of the ventricular walls. Left ventricular end-diastolic volume index is significantly increased, and the left ventricular ejection fraction is severely depressed at 22%. There are diffuse wall motion abnormalities without a clear vascular distribution. Late gadolinium enhancement imaging demonstrates no subendocardial or transmural scar, though thin mid-wall enhancement is noted in the basal septum, suggestive of non-ischemic etiology.

Impression: Non-ischemic dilated cardiomyopathy with severe biventricular systolic dysfunction and mild mid-myocardial fibrosis of the interventricular septum.

Cardiac MRI demonstrates a severe regional wall motion abnormality involving the apex, anterior, and anteroseptal segments of the left ventricle, which are thinned and akinetic. Late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) imaging shows transmural hyperenhancement (>75% wall thickness) in these same distributions, indicating non-viable myocardium in the left anterior descending artery territory. Left ventricular end-diastolic volume is elevated.

Impression: Large, chronic transmural myocardial infarction in the LAD territory with non-viable myocardium. Overall left ventricular systolic dysfunction with an ejection fraction of 33%.

MRI of the brain reveals moderate, confluent bilateral periventricular and deep white matter T2/FLAIR hyperintensities. No acute territorial infarction or intracranial hemorrhage is observed. There is mild generalized cortical and cerebellar atrophy.

Impression: Moderate chronic microvascular ischemic changes (Fazekas grade 2) and age-appropriate brain atrophy.

MRI of the brain demonstrates mild, age-appropriate diffuse cerebral cortical atrophy and ventricular enlargement. There is no acute territorial infarct, intracranial hemorrhage, or space-occupying lesion. The skull base, orbits, and sinuses are intact.

Impression: Age-appropriate brain MRI without acute intracranial pathology.

Brain MRI shows normal gray-white matter differentiation. No areas of restricted diffusion, acute hemorrhage, or pathological enhancement are observed. The ventricles and subarachnoid spaces are normal in caliber. Cerebellar hemispheres and brainstem structures are entirely within normal limits.

Impression: Unremarkable MRI study of the brain. No structural correlates identified for the patient's tremors.

MR imaging of the brain demonstrates extensive, confluent T2/FLAIR hyperintensities in the bilateral periventricular and deep subcortical white matter. In addition, there are multiple chronic lacunar infarcts involving the basal ganglia and internal capsule bilaterally. Moderate to severe generalized cerebral and cerebellar volume loss is noted, consistent with the patient's age.

Impression: Severe chronic microvascular white matter ischemic disease with multiple chronic lacunar infarcts. Moderate to severe generalized parenchymal volume loss.

Fetal MRI at 35 weeks gestation demonstrates partial agenesis of the corpus callosum. The anterior corpus callosum (rostrum and genu) is present, but the body and splenium are absent. The posterior lateral ventricles show moderate colpocephaly, with the atria measuring 10.8 mm. The brain sulcation is otherwise mature and appropriate for 35 weeks, with no periventricular heterotopias.

Other fetal organs and the musculoskeletal system are normal. Impression: Partial agenesis of the corpus callosum with associated mild colpocephaly.

Cardiac MRI shows a subendocardial perfusion defect during first-pass stress imaging in the inferior and inferolateral segments of the left ventricle. Late gadolinium enhancement reveals a corresponding non-transmural subendocardial scar involving approximately 30% of the wall thickness in the inferior wall. Left ventricular ejection fraction is mildly reduced at 49%.

Impression: Subendocardial myocardial infarction of the inferior wall (RCA territory) with evidence of inducible stress ischemia in the surrounding segments.

Fetal MRI at 23 weeks gestation demonstrates severe skeletal dysplasia, highly suggestive of thanatophoric dysplasia. There is marked micromelia, with all long bones severely shortened and showing a slightly curved ('telephone receiver') morphology. The fetal chest is extremely narrow and bell-shaped, and there is prominent platyspondyly of the spine. The fetal skull demonstrates a mild cloverleaf appearance with a bulging forehead.

The brain parenchymal signal is normal, though temporal lobe gyration appears slightly atypical for 23 weeks. Amniotic fluid volume is increased (polyhydramnios). Impression: Severe skeletal dysplasia with features classic for thanatophoric dysplasia, characterized by severe micromelia, narrow chest cavity, and cloverleaf skull deformity.

Cardiac MRI reveals severe, asymmetric septal hypertrophy of the left ventricle, with maximum wall thickness measuring 24 mm at the basal-to-mid anteroseptal segment. Left ventricular cavity size is small with hyperdynamic systolic function, resulting in an ejection fraction of 74%. Dynamic cine imaging demonstrates systolic anterior motion (SAM) of the mitral valve anterior leaflet, causing moderate mitral regurgitation.

Late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) imaging demonstrates focal patchy enhancement at the right ventricular insertion points and within the hypertrophied septal segment. Impression: Classic findings of hypertrophic obstructive cardiomyopathy (HOCM) with significant asymmetric septal hypertrophy, dynamic LVOT obstruction secondary to SAM, and associated myocardial fibrosis.

Brain MRI shows age-appropriate mild cerebral and cerebellar volume loss with corresponding enlargement of the ventricular system and sulci. There are sparse, scattered T2/FLAIR hyperintensities within the periventricular white matter, typical for mild chronic microvascular ischemic disease. No acute ischemia, hemorrhage, or mass lesions are identified.

Impression: Unremarkable MRI of the brain for age. Chronic white matter changes are mild and likely related to small vessel ischemic disease, without clinical acute findings.

A comprehensive cardiac MRI protocol was performed evaluating cardiac structure and function. Multiplanar steady-state free precession (SSFP) cine imaging demonstrates normal left and right ventricular chamber sizes, wall thicknesses, and systolic function. The calculated left ventricular ejection fraction is 62%, and the right ventricular ejection fraction is 56%. There is no evidence of regional wall motion abnormalities, myocardial edema on T2-weighted imaging, or pathological myocardial fibrosis on late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) sequences.

Impression: Entirely normal cardiac MRI examination showing normal biventricular size and systolic function, and no evidence of focal myocardial scar, edema, or infiltration.

MRI demonstrates multiple small, ring-enhancing lesions located at the gray-white matter junction in both cerebral hemispheres. The largest lesion, measuring 1.2 cm, is situated in the left frontal lobe and is surrounded by a moderate amount of vasogenic edema. There is no significant mass effect on the ventricles.

Impression: Multiple enhancing intra-axial lesions with surrounding edema, highly suggestive of intracranial metastases in this patient with known lung cancer.

Cardiac MRI demonstrates normal biventricular size, wall thickness, and systolic function. The left ventricular end-diastolic volume is 142 mL, with a calculated left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) of 62%. The right ventricular end-diastolic volume is 135 mL, with an ejection fraction of 58%. There is no evidence of myocardial edema, perfusion defects, or late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) to suggest myocardial scarring or fibrosis. Valvular structure and flow dynamics are completely within physiological limits.

Impression: Unremarkable cardiac MRI with normal biventricular volumes and preserved systolic function. No evidence of myocardial infarction, scar, or active inflammation.

MRI of the brain demonstrates a tangled nidus of prominent vascular flow voids in the left parieto-occipital region, measuring approximately 3.2 x 2.4 cm. This lesion is associated with early draining veins into the superior sagittal sinus and dilated arterial feeders arising from branches of the left middle and posterior cerebral arteries. There is mild surrounding T2/FLAIR signal hyperintensity, but no frank hemorrhage.

Impression: Left parieto-occipital arteriovenous malformation (AVM). Intervention-focused neurovascular assessment (digital subtraction angiography or neurosurgical consult) is strongly recommended.

Cardiac MRI reveals a dilated left ventricle with severe hypokinesis and thinning of the apex, apical septum, and apical anterior wall. Left ventricular systolic function is severely depressed with an ejection fraction of 32%. Late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) imaging demonstrates extensive, dense transmural hyperenhancement (>75% thickness) involving the apex and distal anteroseptal walls, consistent with completed transmural myocardial infarction in the LAD distribution. A non-enhancing filling defect is noted in the LV apex, consistent with an apical thrombus.

Impression: Dilated ischemic cardiomyopathy with transmural apical myocardial infarction and associated left ventricular apical thrombus. Severely reduced LVEF of 32%.

MR imaging of the brain shows a well-defined zone of restricted diffusion involving the right middle cerebral artery (MCA) territory, specifically within the right insular cortex and posterior lentiform nucleus. This area corresponds with elevated DWI signal and matched ADC hypointensity, consistent with acute cytotoxic edema. There is no significant mass effect or midline shift, although minor local sulcal effacement is noted. No acute intracranial hemorrhage is detected.

Impression: Acute infarct involving the right insular and right MCA deep territory. No hemorrhagic transformation observed.

Fetal MRI at 30 weeks gestation demonstrates a large multicystic dysplastic kidney (MCDK) on the left side, which is occupied by multiple non-communicating cysts of varying sizes and has no identifiable normal renal parenchyma. In contrast, the right kidney is enlarged and shows compensatory hypertrophy, with normal parenchymal signal and corticomedullary differentiation. Amniotic fluid volume is normal. Brain development and ventricular atrium size (6.1 mm) are appropriate.

Impression: Left multicystic dysplastic kidney with compensatory hypertrophy of the normal right kidney. Normal amniotic fluid level.

Cardiac MRI shows marked asymmetric hypertrophy of the interventricular septum, with a maximum septal thickness of 22 mm at the mid-ventricular level. The posterior wall measures 10 mm. Systolic anterior motion (SAM) of the mitral valve is present, causing moderate dynamic left ventricular outflow tract (LVOT) obstruction with an estimated peak gradient of 45 mmHg. The left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) is hyperdynamic at 72%. Late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) imaging shows patchy, mid-wall enhancement at the right ventricular insertion points, consistent with focal myocardial fibrosis.

Impression: Findings highly characteristic of asymmetric hypertrophic obstructive cardiomyopathy (HCM) with associated dynamic LVOT obstruction and hyperdynamic systolic function. Focal fibrosis at RV insertion points noted.

MR imaging of the brain shows a large area of restricted diffusion with corresponding ADC hypointensity in the right middle cerebral artery (MCA) territory, involving the right insular cortex and frontoparietal lobes. There is associated T2/FLAIR hyperintensity in the cortical and subcortical regions, consistent with subacute ischemic infarction. Mild mass effect is noted on the right lateral ventricle, though there is no significant midline shift. Major flow voids demonstrate a lack of signal in the right M1 segment, suggestive of occlusion.

Impression: Acute-to-subacute ischemic infarction in the right MCA distribution. Mild mass effect without herniation is noted, likely representing cytotoxic edema.

Cardiac MRI was performed to evaluate for possible infiltrative disease. Left and right ventricular dimensions are within normal limits, with a calculated left ventricular ejection fraction of 57% and right ventricular ejection fraction of 54%. No focal or regional myocardial hypokinesis is demonstrated. There is no evidence of abnormal late gadolinium enhancement or signal intensity to suggest myocarditis, amyloidosis, or infarction.

Impression: Structurally and functionally normal cardiac MRI. No evidence of myocardial scarring, edema, or infiltrative cardiac disease.

Fetal MRI at 31 weeks gestation reveals complete agenesis of the corpus callosum. The lateral ventricles show a characteristic parallel orientation and colpocephaly, with the posterior occipital horns dilated to 13.5 mm. There is also atypical radial sulcation extending from the third ventricle. No other intracranial abnormalities or posterior fossa changes are observed.

Impression: Complete agenesis of the corpus callosum with associated colpocephaly. Structural findings appear isolated, but genetic counseling is recommended.

Cardiac MRI was performed to evaluate atypical palpitations. Multiplanar cine sequences demonstrate normal left and right ventricular volumes, wall thickness, and systolic function. The left ventricular ejection fraction is 61% and the right ventricular ejection fraction is 58%. No regional wall motion abnormalities or areas of focal hypertrophy are visualized. Myocardial perfusion and late gadolinium enhancement imaging are completely normal, with no signs of myocardial edema or focal scar.

Impression: Normal cardiac MRI with normal biventricular size and function. No structural, perfusion, or scar-related substrate to explain the patient's symptoms of palpitations.

Brain MR imaging demonstrates an acute intraparenchymal hematoma centered in the left basal ganglia, measuring 3.5 x 2.4 cm. The lesion shows characteristic signal changes of acute intracellular methemoglobin with a surrounding halo of T2 hyperintense vasogenic edema. There is moderate mass effect on the left lateral ventricle and a 3 mm rightward midline shift.

Impression: Acute left basal ganglia hemorrhage with surrounding vasogenic edema and mild mass effect. Features are highly suggestive of hypertensive etiology.

Cardiac MRI shows diffuse, bilateral atrial enlargement and concentric left ventricular hypertrophy. There is an atypical myocardial nulling pattern during late gadolinium enhancement sequences, with diffuse subendocardial and transmural enhancement. Native T1 values are significantly elevated at 1210 ms, and the extracellular volume is calculated at 44%.

Impression: Infiltrative cardiomyopathy, highly characteristic of cardiac amyloidosis. Markedly elevated extracellular volume and characteristic abnormal nulling kinetic properties.

Fetal MRI at 32 weeks gestation reveals a large open neural tube defect in the thoracolumbar region. There is a defect in the posterior vertebral arches extending from T11 through L3, with exposure of the neural placode and an associated myelomeningocele sac. Severe Chiari II malformation is present, with downward displacement of the cerebellar vermis and medulla into the cervical canal. The lateral ventricles are severely dilated, measuring 16.5 mm on the left and 15.8 mm on the right.

Cortical sulcation shows mild delay, likely secondary to severe ventriculomegaly. Impression: Large thoracolumbar myelomeningocele with associated Chiari II malformation and severe bilateral ventriculomegaly.

Fetal MRI at 21 weeks gestation. There is a large, complex, cystic and solid midline mass arising from the occipital region of the fetal skull, communicating with the intracranial space through a midline calvarial defect. Herniation of dysplastic cerebellar tissue into the occipital sac is visualized, confirming an occipital encephalocele. The lateral ventricles are moderately dilated, measuring 11.2 mm. Cortical sulcation is characteristically smooth and appropriate for 21 weeks.

The fetal spine is otherwise intact, and the chest and abdominal viscera are normal. Impression: Large occipital encephalocele containing herniated posterior fossa structures, associated with moderate ventriculomegaly.

Magnetic resonance imaging of the heart shows normal cardiac chamber anatomy and spatial relationships. The left ventricular end-diastolic volume is 128 mL and the right ventricular end-diastolic volume is 135 mL, representing normal sizes. Myocardial perfusion is normal, and there is no late gadolinium enhancement. LVEF is 61% and RVEF is 56%.

Impression: Completely normal cardiac MRI study. There is no evidence of structural, functional, or perfusion abnormalities in either ventricle.

Fetal MRI at 24 weeks gestation demonstrates a normal developmental profile. The cerebral hemispheres are symmetric, and the sulcation is normal with clearly defined parieto-occipital fissures. The lateral ventricles are normal, with an atrial width of 5.5 mm.

The corpus callosum is intact, and the posterior fossa contains normal cerebellar hemispheres and a well-developed vermis. Impression: Normal fetal MRI study demonstrating expected structural development of the brain and spine for 24 weeks gestation.

Fetal MRI obtained at 33 weeks gestation. The left renal fossa contains an enlarged, dysplastic left kidney containing multiple, non-communicating, varying-sized cysts, with no identifiable normal parenchymal signal, typical of a multicystic dysplastic kidney (MCDK). The right kidney is normal in size and signal with normal corticomedullary differentiation. The fetal bladder is visualized and filled. Fetal brain morphology and sulcation are normal, and the lateral ventricular atria measure 6.5 mm.

Amniotic fluid volume is normal. No other anomalies are identified. Impression: Unilateral (left) multicystic dysplastic kidney. Normal right kidney and normal amniotic fluid index suggest preserved overall renal function.

MR study targeted at the sella demonstrates a large, solid-appearing, enhancing sellar mass measuring 2.3 x 1.9 x 1.7 cm. The lesion extends superiorly into the suprasellar cistern, causing remodeling and superior displacement of the optic chiasm. There is mild extension towards the bilateral cavernous sinuses, but no definite internal carotid encasement is seen.

Impression: Enhancing pituitary macroadenoma with suprasellar extension and optic chiasm displacement. Formal neuro-ophthalmologic visual field testing is recommended.

MRI of the brain and sella turcica demonstrates a well-defined, hypoenhancing mass within the anterior pituitary gland measuring approximately 1.2 cm in maximum diameter. The mass causes mild upward bulging of the diaphragmatic sella and slight superior displacement of the optic chiasm. There is no invasion into the bilateral cavernous sinuses.

Impression: Pituitary macroadenoma measuring 1.2 cm. There is mild superior extension with minimal contact but no severe compression of the optic chiasm. Endocrine evaluation and visual field testing are recommended.

Evaluation of the interatrial septum reveals a secundum-type atrial septal defect (ASD) measuring approximately 18 mm in diameter. Flow quantification demonstrates significant left-to-right shunting with an calculated pulmonary-to-systemic blood flow ratio (Qp/Qs) of 1.8. Moderate right ventricular dilation is present, consistent with chronic volume overload, but right ventricular systolic function remains normal.

Impression: Secundum atrial septal defect with significant left-to-right shunt and resulting moderate right ventricular volume overload. No pulmonary hypertension signs detected.

A non-enhancing, ill-defined hyperintense lesion is seen on T2 and FLAIR sequences within the left frontal lobe cortex and subcortical white matter, measuring roughly 3.1 x 2.7 cm. There is minimal mass effect on the surrounding structures, and no associated vasogenic edema, restricted diffusion, or abnormal enhancement on post-contrast imaging.

Impression: Left frontal lobe non-enhancing parenchymal lesion, highly suggestive of a low-grade astrocytoma (glioma) or other low-grade neuroepithelial tumor. Long-term surveillance or biopsy is indicated.

MRI of the brain was acquired with standard headache protocols. There is no evidence of intracranial mass, acute ischemia, hemorrhage, or hydrocephalus. The ventricles, sulci, and cisterns are within normal limits. Orbits and paranasal sinuses are unremarkable.

Impression: Unremarkable MRI of the brain. No structural etiology identified to account for the patient's headache.

Fetal MRI at 35 weeks gestation demonstrates a right-sided congenital diaphragmatic hernia (CDH). Herniation of the liver and gallbladder is observed in the right hemithorax, with significant leftward cardiac displacement. Left lung volume is moderately decreased, but total fetal lung volume is calculated at 48% of predicted for gestational age, representing moderate pulmonary hypoplasia. Brain development shows complex, mature sulcation with lateral ventricles measuring 6.1 mm.

Impression: Right-sided congenital diaphragmatic hernia with liver herniation ("liver up") and moderate pulmonary hypoplasia. Brain development is normal.

MR imaging of the brain was obtained in a young adult presenting with recurrent tension-type headaches. The examination demonstrates normal signal intensity and morphology of the cerebral hemispheres, brainstem, and cerebellum. There is no evidence of intracranial mass, abnormal extra-axial fluid collections, or pathological meningeal enhancement. Ventricles and sulci are entirely normal for age.

Impression: Normal MRI of the brain. No structural, inflammatory, or neoplastic etiology identified.

Cardiac MR reveals marked posterior displacement of both the anterior and posterior leaflets of the mitral valve into the left atrium during systole, consistent with bi-leaflet mitral valve prolapse (Barlow's disease). Phase-contrast imaging demonstrates a large, eccentric, posteriorly-directed regurgitant jet, with a regurgitant fraction calculated at 48%, indicating severe mitral regurgitation. The left atrium is severely dilated (volume 85 mL/m2) and the left ventricle is mildly dilated with preserved systolic function (EF 63%).

Impression: Severe mitral regurgitation secondary to bi-leaflet mitral valve prolapse. The left-sided chambers are dilated, reflecting volume overload, with preserved left ventricular contractile function.

Cardiac MRI reveals severe dilation of the left ventricle with global hypokinesis. The left ventricular ejection fraction is severely reduced at 28% (LVEDV 245 mL, LVESV 176 mL). The right ventricular size and systolic function are at the lower limit of normal with an ejection fraction of 46%. Late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) imaging demonstrates mid-wall linear hyperenhancement within the basal to mid-ventricular septum, characteristic of non-ischemic cardiomyopathy.

Impression: Severe non-ischemic dilated cardiomyopathy with mid-wall septal fibrosis and severely reduced left ventricular systolic function.

T2-weighted turbo spin-echo and T2-mapping sequences show focal hyperintensity in the subepicardium of the lateral and inferolateral left ventricular wall, indicative of myocardial edema. Corresponding late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) imaging demonstrates non-ischemic, subepicardial hyperenhancement in the same segments. The left ventricular ejection fraction is mildly reduced at 50% with mild localized hypokinesia.

No pericardial effusion or thickening is identified. Impression: Findings are consistent with acute myocarditis according to the Lake Louise Criteria, involving the lateral and inferolateral walls with mild left ventricular dysfunction.

Brain MRI reveals a well-circumscribed, extra-axial dural-based mass located along the anterior sagittal sinus, measuring approximately 3.2 x 2.8 x 2.5 cm. The mass is isointense to grey matter on T1 and T2 sequences and demonstrates intense, homogeneous enhancement following gadolinium administration, including a prominent dural tail sign. There is mild compression of the adjacent superior frontal gyrus and a thin rim of surrounding vasogenic edema.

Impression: Well-circumscribed extra-axial dural-based mass along the anterior sagittal sinus, characteristic of a benign meningioma. There is mild mass effect on the adjacent frontal lobe without significant midline shift.

Cardiac MRI shows pronounced global dilation of the left ventricle with severely impaired global systolic function. The left ventricular end-diastolic diameter measures 6.8 cm with diffuse, severe hypokinesis. Late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) imaging reveals focal mid-wall enhancement within the interventricular septum, sparing the subendocardium. This pattern is highly characteristic of a non-ischemic dilated etiology. Right ventricular size is mildly increased with a mildly reduced ejection fraction.

Impression: Dilated cardiomyopathy of non-ischemic origin. Severe global left ventricular dysfunction with an ejection fraction of 24%, accompanied by mid-wall septal scar/fibrosis.

MR imaging of the brain demonstrates a crescent-shaped extra-axial fluid collection overlying the left frontoparietal convexity. The collection measures up to 1.4 cm in maximal width and displays heterogeneous signal intensity, with hyperintense areas on T1 and T2 sequences suggesting subacute-on-chronic blood products. Marked mass effect is present, causing compression of the left cerebral hemisphere and a 7 mm midline shift to the right.

Impression: Subacute-on-chronic left frontoparietal subdural hematoma causing significant mass effect and midline shift. Urgent clinical correlation and neurosurgical evaluation are recommended.

MR imaging of the brain demonstrates a focal area of restricted diffusion in the left middle cerebral artery (MCA) territory, specifically involving the left insular cortex and adjacent temporal lobe, showing high signal on DWI and corresponding low ADC values. Mild sulcal effacement is noted in this region, without evidence of intracranial hemorrhage on susceptibility-weighted imaging (SWI). The ventricular system is normal in size and configuration.

Impression: Acute ischemic infarction within the left MCA territory. No acute intracranial hemorrhage or mass effect.

Fetal MRI at 26 weeks gestation demonstrates a classic Dandy-Walker malformation. There is severe hypoplasia and upward rotation of the cerebellar vermis, communicating with a massively dilated posterior fossa fluid space. The tentorium cerebelli and torcula are elevated. The lateral ventricles are dilated, with the right atrium measuring 12.5 mm and the left measuring 12.1 mm. Sulcation and opercularization are mildly delayed.

The corpus callosum is intact. Fetal spine is normal. Impression: Classic Dandy-Walker malformation with secondary bilateral moderate ventriculomegaly.

Imaging reveals a bicuspid aortic valve with calcified fusion of the left and right coronary cusps. Quantitative velocity-encoded phase-contrast imaging demonstrates a high-velocity jet across the aortic valve with a peak systolic velocity of 4.2 m/s, consistent with severe aortic stenosis. Secondary concentric left ventricular hypertrophy is present with a myocardial mass index of 115 g/m2. Left ventricular ejection fraction is preserved at 51%.

Impression: Bicuspid aortic valve with severe aortic stenosis and secondary concentric left ventricular hypertrophy. Left ventricular systolic function remains overall preserved.

The study demonstrates normal chamber volumes and wall thicknesses. Left and right ventricular contractility is fully preserved. No abnormal tissue enhancement, edema, or perfusion defects are demonstrated. The cardiac valves appear structurally intact with normal forward flow profiles.

Impression: Unremarkable cardiac MRI. Normal biventricular volumes and function with a calculated left ventricular ejection fraction of 61%.

MRI of the brain demonstrates a large, heterogeneously enhancing, thick-walled ring-like lesion within the right temporal lobe measuring 4.2 x 3.8 x 3.5 cm. Extensive surrounding vasogenic edema is present, manifesting as high T2/FLAIR signal extending into the adjacent white matter. There is associated mass effect, with partial compression of the right lateral ventricle and a leftward midline shift of 6 mm.

Impression: Large, necrotic ring-enhancing mass in the right temporal lobe with significant mass effect. The appearance is highly suggestive of a high-grade glioma (glioblastoma) or, less likely, a solitary metastasis.

Fetal MRI at 36 weeks gestation demonstrates advanced sulcation, gyration, and operculization matching late third trimester standards. The lateral ventricles are completely normal, measuring 5.5 mm at the atrium. The posterior fossa, cerebellum, and brainstem are structurally intact, and the corpus callosum is fully formed. Standard evaluation of the thorax and abdomen shows no mass lesions or structural anomalies.

Impression: Unremarkable fetal MRI at 36 weeks showing normal, advanced brain development and completely intact systemic anatomy.

MRI examination of the heart shows normal cardiac chambers with no ventricular hypertrophy or dilatation. The left ventricular ejection fraction is calculated at 63%, and right ventricular ejection fraction is 59%. There is no evidence of myocardial infarction, infiltration, or dynamic perfusion abnormalities.

Impression: Normal cardiac MRI study. Normal biventricular size and function with no signs of myocardial injury.

Fetal MRI at 24 weeks gestation demonstrates a lumbosacral neural tube defect. There is an open myelomeningocele sac containing herniated neural elements at the L4-S2 level. Brain imaging reveals classic Chiari II malformation signs, including herniation of the cerebellar tonsils through the foramen magnum, effacement of the cisterna magna, and a 'banana-shaped' cerebellum. Symmetric ventriculomegaly is present with atrial widths of 12.1 mm.

Impression: Open lumbosacral myelomeningocele with associated Chiari II malformation and moderate ventriculomegaly.

Cardiac MR assessment reveals a dilated left ventricle with severe global systolic dysfunction, manifesting an ejection fraction of 28%. There is prominent thinning and akinesis of the mid-to-apical anterior wall, septum, and apex. Late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) sequences demonstrate subendocardial to transmural enhancement (estimated at >75% wall thickness) in these dysfunctional segments, highly indicative of a prior large myocardial infarction in the left anterior descending (LAD) coronary artery distribution.

Impression: Severe ischemic cardiomyopathy with a large transmural myocardial infarction in the LAD territory, showing minimal viability in the affected anterior and septal segments. Moderate secondary mitral regurgitation is also noted.

The MRI reveals a small defect in the membranous portion of the interventricular septum, measuring 4 mm in diameter, consistent with a perimembranous ventricular septal defect. High-velocity shunting is noted from the left to the right ventricle, with a calculated Qp:Qs shunt ratio of 1.3:1. Ventricular dimensions and volumes are normal, with a left ventricular ejection fraction of 60%.

Impression: Small, hemodynamically stable perimembranous ventricular septal defect (VSD). No significant ventricular volume overload, pulmonary hypertension, or ventricular dysfunction is identified.

Marked, asymmetric septal hypertrophy is observed, with the maximal diastolic septal thickness measuring 22 mm. There is systolic anterior motion (SAM) of the mitral valve anterior leaflet, causing dynamic left ventricular outflow tract (LVOT) obstruction and moderate mitral regurgitation. Patchy, mid-myocardial late gadolinium enhancement is noted at the superior and inferior right ventricular insertion points.

Impression: Hypertrophic obstructive cardiomyopathy (HOCM) with severe asymmetric septal hypertrophy and dynamic LVOT obstruction. Associated focal fibrosis is present at the RV insertion junctions.

Aortic 3D angiographic reconstruction demonstrates a focal narrowing (coarctation) of the descending thoracic aorta just distal to the origin of the left subclavian artery. The narrow segment measures 8 mm in diameter, compared to the normal proximal descending aorta diameter of 18 mm. Prominent internal mammary and intercostal collateral arteries are visualized. Left ventricular hypertrophy is noted, with a preserved ejection fraction of 65%.

Impression: Severe focal coarctation of the descending thoracic aorta with significant collateral vascular development and secondary concentric left ventricular hypertrophy. Global LV systolic function remains preserved.

Fetal MRI at 24 weeks gestation reveals complete absence of the corpus callosum. There is characteristic colpocephaly with parallel alignment of the lateral ventricles and dilatation of the occipital horns. The lateral ventricular atrium measures 11.5 mm bilateral. The third ventricle is superiorly displaced. Sulcation pattern is otherwise normal for gestational age, without signs of polymicrogyria or nodular heterotopia.

Visualized spine and visceral organs are normal. Impression: Complete agenesis of the corpus callosum with associated colpocephaly and mild bilateral ventriculomegaly.

Fetal MRI evaluated at 26 weeks gestation reveals bilateral enlargement of the lateral ventricles. The left ventricular atrium measures 14.2 mm and the right measures 13.8 mm, indicating moderate-to-severe ventriculomegaly. There is associated dangling of the choroid plexus bilaterally, though the third and fourth ventricles are within normal limits. Cerebral sulcation is appropriate for 26 weeks, with no secondary signs of cortical dysplasia.

No other structural malformations are visualized. The corpus callosum appears intact and normal in length. Impression: Moderate bilateral fetal ventriculomegaly. Close prenatal surveillance and postnatal pediatric neurology evaluation are recommended.

Fetal MRI at 23 weeks gestation demonstrates severe oligohydramnios/anhydramnios, limiting resolution of some structures. However, there is clear bilateral renal agenesis; both renal fossae are empty, and no normal renal tissue or renal arteries can be identified. The fetal urinary bladder is not visualized. The adrenal glands are flattened in the renal beds ("lying down" sign). The fetal brain shows normal cortical sulcation for 23 weeks, and the lateral ventricular atrium is 5.5 mm.

Impression: Bilateral renal agenesis associated with severe oligohydramnios (Potter sequence pathology).

Fetal MRI at 20 weeks gestation shows a single fetus in unstable lie. The brain development is entirely normal for this gestational stage. The cerebral hemispheres are symmetric, and early opercularization is proceeding normally. The lateral ventricles are small and symmetric, measuring 5.2 mm in the atrium. The corpus callosum is visible and intact for gestational age.

All extracranial structures, including the spine, diaphragm, and stomach, are normal. Impression: Unremarkable 20-week fetal MRI showing normal development.

MRI evaluation of the heart reveals physiological biventricular structure and function. Left ventricular ejection fraction is 65% with normal stroke volume. Right ventricular volumes are normal with an ejection fraction of 55%. There is no myocardial edema, regional wall motion abnormality, or evidence of late gadolinium enhancement to suggest prior infarction or myocarditis.

Impression: Unremarkable cardiac MRI. Normal ventricular size, function, and myocardial tissue characterization.

Fetal MRI at 29 weeks gestation demonstrates abnormalities suspicious for a skeletal dysplasia. There is generalized shortening of all long bones, particularly the femora and humeri, indicating rhizomelic micromelia. The thoracic cage is severely narrow and bell-shaped, with associated pulmonary hypoplasia. The skull exhibits frontal bossing, but intracranial anatomy, ventricles (7.0 mm), and sulcation are appropriate for age.

There is no evidence of fractures or spinal anomalies. Impression: Skeletal dysplasia characterized by severe rhizomelic micromelia and a narrow thoracic cavity with secondary pulmonary hypoplasia; findings are highly suggestive of thanatophoric dysplasia.

Magnetic resonance imaging of the brain demonstrates a well-defined area of restricted diffusion within the left middle cerebral artery (MCA) territory, specifically involving the posterior limb of the internal capsule and adjacent corona radiata. Corresponding T2/FLAIR hyperintensity is subtle, consistent with hyperacute to acute cerebral infarction. No evidence of mass effect or acute intracranial hemorrhage is visualized.

Impression: Acute ischemic infarct within the left MCA territory. No hemorrhagic transformation is identified. The findings warrant prompt clinical correlation and appropriate stroke management protocol.

Fetal MRI performed at 24 weeks gestation reveals normal development of the intracranial structures. The cerebral hemispheres demonstrate appropriate symmetric morphology, and early sylvian fissure opercularization is visible, consistent with the gestational age. The bilateral lateral ventricular atria are within normal limits, with the left measuring 6.5 mm and the right measuring 6.2 mm.

The posterior fossa is completely intact, displaying normal cerebellar hemispheres and a well-formed vermis. Amniotic fluid volume is subjective within normal limits, and the visualised fetal spine is unremarkable. Impression: Unremarkable fetal brain MRI at 24 weeks gestation with normal ventricular size and age-appropriate sulcation.

Fetal magnetic resonance imaging was performed at 24 weeks gestation. The cerebral hemispheres demonstrate appropriate development, with early sulcation and migration patterns appropriate for gestational age, including visible sylvian fissures. The lateral ventricles are normal in size, with the atrial diameter measuring 5.8 mm. The corpus callosum, brainstem, and posterior fossa structures, including the cerebellar vermis, are intact and morphologically normal.

The fetal chest, abdomen, spine, and extremities are grossly normal, with normal amniotic fluid volume. Impression: Unremarkable fetal MRI demonstrating normal intracranial and extracranial anatomy for 24 weeks of gestation.

The study demonstrates normal parenchymal signal intensity without focal lesions or structural abnormalities. The ventricular system, sulci, and cisterns are completely appropriate for the patient's age. Cranial nerves, extra-axial structures, and major vascular flow voids are unremarkable.

Impression: Unremarkable and normal brain MRI. There are no imaging findings to account for subjective cognitive or memory concerns.

Brain MRI demonstrates a complex cluster of dilated, tortuous vascular structures within the left parieto-occipital region. Multiple serpiginous flow voids are observed on T2-weighted sequences, associated with a prominent feeding artery from the left posterior cerebral artery and early venous drainage into the superior sagittal sinus. There is surrounding gliosis in the adjacent parenchyma, but no evidence of acute hemorrhage.

Impression: Left parieto-occipital arteriovenous malformation (AVM) with prominent feeding vessels and early venous drainage. No evidence of acute intracranial hemorrhage.

A cardiac MRI was performed to evaluate for possible structural disease in the setting of palpitations. Left and right ventricular chambers are of normal dimensions, thickness, and configuration. The left ventricular ejection fraction is 60% and the right ventricular ejection fraction is 55%, both demonstrating excellent systolic function without any segmental wall motion abnormalities. No focal myocardial edema, fatty replacement, or pathological late gadolinium enhancement is visualized.

Impression: Completely normal cardiac MRI. No structural, functional, or tissue-level abnormalities identified to explain the patient's symptoms.

Fetal MRI at 27 weeks gestation demonstrates severe shortening and bowing of all long bones, consistent with micromelia and rhizomelic shortening. The femurs appear severely curved ('telephone receiver' appearance). The thorax is remarkably narrow and bell-shaped, with short ribs wrapping tightly around the heart. Platyspondyly is seen in the spine.

The fetal brain demonstrates normal parenchymal structure and sulcation patterns for 27 weeks gestation. The ventricular atria measure 8.5 mm. Impression: Severe skeletal dysplasia, highly suggestive of thanatophoric dysplasia given the narrow thorax, micromelia, and platyspondyly.

MRI of the brain and IACs reveals a 1.8 x 1.4 cm soft tissue mass centered within the left cerebellopontine angle cistern. The lesion extends into the internal auditory canal, causing focal expansion. It demonstrates intermediate signal intensity on T1-weighted images and intense enhancement after contrast administration, with an 'ice cream cone' morphology.

Impression: Intracanalicular and extracanalicular left cerebellopontine angle mass consistent with a vestibular schwannoma (acoustic neuroma). There is mild mass effect on the adjacent middle cerebellar peduncle.

Fetal MRI at 33 weeks gestation shows normal development. The lateral ventricular atria measure 6.5 mm bilaterally, and the cerebral cortex exhibits progressive sulcation with deep sulci appropriate for early third trimester. The brainstem and cerebellum are completely normal. Fetal stomach, kidneys, and bladder are visualised and normal. No other anomalies are identified.

Impression: Structurally normal third-trimester fetal MRI. Normal intracranial biometry and appropriate sulcation development.

MR imaging of the brain reveals symmetric enlargement of the lateral, third, and fourth ventricles, disproportionate to the mild degree of cerebral sulcal enlargement. There is rounding of the frontal horns and narrowing of the callosal angle (approximately 65 degrees), along with prominent flow void in the aqueduct of Sylvius. Transependymal CSF migration is minimal.

Impression: Ventriculomegaly disproportionate to sulcal enlargement. Features are highly suggestive of normal pressure hydrocephalus (NPH) in the appropriate clinical setting of gait disturbance, cognitive decline, and urinary incontinence.

Fetal MRI performed at 22 weeks gestation. The cerebral hemispheres exhibit normal development with smooth cortical margins appropriate for this early stage of gestation. The lateral ventricles are symmetric, with the atrial diameter measuring 5.5 mm, well within the normal range. The corpus callosum is present and demonstrates early development, and the cerebellum and posterior fossa fluid spaces are normal.

Impression: Normal fetal brain MRI at 22 weeks. No structural anomalies or ventriculomegaly identified.

Brain MR imaging demonstrates normal cortical thickness and sulcal pattern. There are no intra- or extra-axial fluid collections, no areas of focal restricted diffusion to suggest acute ischemia, and no evidence of intracranial microhemorrhage. Ventricles and basal cisterns are unremarkable in size and location.

Impression: Completely normal brain MRI. No structural, traumatic, or vascular changes are seen in this patient presenting with persistent post-concussive symptoms.

Fetal MRI performed at 32 weeks gestation shows age-appropriate development of the fetal brain. Cortical folding and sulcation are well-developed, with deep and well-defined sylvian fissures and parieto-occipital sulci. The cerebral ventricles are normal in size, with a symmetric atrial width of 6.1 mm. The corpus callosum is intact and measures within normal limits for length and thickness. The brainstem and cerebellum are structurally normal with a well-formed vermis.

Impression: Normal fetal MRI at 32 weeks gestation, demonstrating age-appropriate brain maturation and sulcation. No structural anomalies detected.

Cardiac MRI demonstrates normal dimensions of all four cardiac chambers. The left ventricular myocardium shows normal thickness and signal intensity on T1 and T2 weighted sequences. The left ventricular ejection fraction is calculated at 63% and the right ventricular ejection fraction is 58%. No valvular dysfunction or regurgitation is identified. No areas of abnormal late gadolinium enhancement are seen.

Impression: Normal cardiac MRI study. There is no evidence of structural, functional, or infiltrative cardiac pathology.

MRI brain demonstrates prominent, disproportionate dilation of the lateral and third ventricles relative to the degree of cerebral sulcal atrophy. There is rounding of the frontal horns of the lateral ventricles and a prominent flow void ('jet') seen within the aqueduct of Sylvius on T2-weighted images. Periventricular capping, representing transependymal CSF migration, is noted around the frontal horns.

Impression: Ventriculomegaly disproportionate to cortical sulcal thinning, consistent with normal pressure hydrocephalus (NPH) in the appropriate clinical setting. Recommend clinical correlation to assess gait, urinary, and cognitive symptoms.

Brain MRI demonstrates extensive, confluent T2/FLAIR hyperintensity in the periventricular and subcortical white matter, indicating chronic microvascular ischemic disease. Susceptibility-weighted imaging (SWI) demonstrates multiple focal areas of signal loss (blooming artifact) scattered throughout the bilateral lobar cerebral hemispheres, particularly in the temporal and parietal lobes, consistent with microhemorrhages. No acute macrohemorrhage or territorial stroke is seen.

Impression: Chronic microvascular ischemic changes combined with multiple lobar microhemorrhages on SWI, highly characteristic of cerebral amyloid angiopathy (CAA).

Brain MRI demonstrates an ill-defined, non-enhancing expansile T2/FLAIR hyperintense mass within the right frontal lobe cortex and subcortical white matter, measuring approximately 3.1 x 2.7 cm. The lesion shows no restricted diffusion on DWI and no enhancement on post-contrast imaging. Minimal mass effect is noted on the right lateral ventricle frontal horn, with no midline shift.

Impression: Non-enhancing infiltrative intra-axial mass in the right frontal lobe, highly suspicious for a low-grade glioma (e.g., diffuse astrocytoma). Recommend follow-up imaging or stereotactic biopsy.

Fetal MRI at 20 weeks gestation shows unremarkable intracranial and abdominal anatomy. The cerebral hemispheres show initial sylvian fissure invagination, appropriate for early 20-week development. The lateral ventricular atria are symmetric, measuring 5.1 mm. The brainstem, cerebellum, spine, and abdominal viscera are intact and normal in appearance.

Impression: Normal fetal MRI study showing age-appropriate central nervous system development and normal fetal visceral anatomy.

Magnetic resonance imaging of the brain was performed following a mild traumatic head injury. There is no evidence of intracranial hemorrhage, axonal shear injury on susceptibility-weighted imaging, or acute cerebral infarction. The cerebral parenchyma, ventricles, and extra-axial spaces are entirely normal.

Impression: Unremarkable MRI of the brain. No structural sequelae of head trauma or acute intracranial pathology identified.

Fetal MRI performed at 26 weeks gestation reveals bilateral, moderate ventriculomegaly. The left lateral ventricle atrial diameter measures 14.2 mm, and the right measures 13.8 mm. Assessment of the cerebral cortex shows sulcation patterns appropriate for 26 weeks, though there is mild compression of the periventricular white matter. The corpus callosum is present but thin. No germinal matrix or intraventricular hemorrhage is identified. Orbits, posterior fossa, and spine are normal.

Impression: Bilateral moderate fetal ventriculomegaly. Recommend serial follow-up imaging and pediatric neurosurgery consultation to evaluate for potential post-natal hydrocephalus risk.

Brain MRI demonstrates bilateral, symmetric, confluent areas of high T2/FLAIR signal in the periventricular and subcortical white matter. These findings are associated with numerous small chronic lacunar infarcts within the basal ganglia. Prominent widening of the sulci and enlargement of the ventricles are present, indicating moderate global cerebral volume loss.

Impression: Moderate to severe chronic small vessel ischemic white matter disease (Fazekas Grade 3) and diffuse cerebral atrophy. No acute territorial cortical infarct or acute hemorrhage identified.

Brain MRI scan demonstrates symmetric and normal development of the cerebral and cerebellar hemispheres. No abnormal signal intensities or mass lesions are observed. The ventricular system, basal cisterns, and major vascular pathways appear clear and unremarkable. There is no evidence of intracranial pathology or abnormal post-contrast enhancement.

Impression: Completely normal brain MRI. No acute or chronic structural findings are identified to explain the patient's episodic dizziness and vertigo.

Multiplanar, multisequence MRI of the brain demonstrates normal gray and white matter differentiation without abnormal signal intensity. There are no foci of restricted diffusion or intracranial hemorrhage. The ventricular system and sulci are symmetric and normal in caliber. No abnormal enhancement is observed after intravenous contrast administration. Orbits, paranasal sinuses, and mastoid air cells are unremarkable.

Impression: Unremarkable and normal brain MRI. No evidence of central nervous system pathology.

Sagittal T1 and T2 weighted sequences of the brain and craniocervical junction demonstrate herniation of the cerebellar tonsils approximately 7 mm below the level of the foramen magnum. The tonsils appear peg-like and pointed. There is mild crowding of the craniocervical junction, but no evidence of syringomyelia in the cervical spinal cord visualized.

Impression: Chiari I malformation with 7 mm cerebellar tonsillar ectopia. No associated cervical syrinx is visualized on the current study.

Fetal MRI at 32 weeks gestation demonstrating bilateral ventriculomegaly. The atrium of the left lateral ventricle is severely dilated at 14.8 mm, and the right lateral ventricle measures 12.5 mm. There is mild thinning of the overlying cerebral cortex. The sulcation and gyral patterns are within normal limits for gestational age, showing appropriate development of the central and lateral sulci. No intracranial hemorrhage or extra-axial fluid collections are identified.

Impression: Significant bilateral fetal ventriculomegaly, more pronounced on the left. No secondary parenchymal or posterior fossa anomalies are visualized.

MR of the brain shows no focal areas of abnormal parenchymal signal intensity or abnormal enhancement. The ventricles and subarachnoid spaces are symmetric and appropriate for the patient's age. There is no evidence of intracranial mass, mass effect, midline shift, or acute ischemia. Major intracranial arterial structures show intact flow voids.

Impression: Completely normal brain MRI. No significant intracranial pathology or structural abnormalities detected.

Fetal MRI performed at 29 weeks gestation demonstrates findings consistent with Dandy-Walker malformation. There is severe hypoplasia of the cerebellar vermis accompanied by significant enlargement of the posterior fossa cystic space, which communicates with the fourth ventricle. Torcular-lambdoid inversion is noted with elevation of the tentorium.

Bilateral ventriculomegaly is present, with the left and right atrial measurements being 13.1 mm and 12.8 mm respectively. Cerebral sulcation pattern is age-appropriate. Impression: Classic Dandy-Walker malformation with associated moderate bilateral ventriculomegaly.

Cardiac MR demonstrates diffuse, severe thickening of the pericardium, measuring up to 6 mm, with intense late gadolinium enhancement of both the visceral and parietal pericardial layers, indicating active inflammation. A circumferential, moderate pericardial effusion is present, measuring approximately 15 mm in maximal thickness. Real-time cine imaging during free breathing reveals ventricular coupling and septal bounce, suggestive of early constrictive physiology. The myocardium itself exhibits normal signal intensity without evidence of late enhancement.

Impression: Acute-on-chronic pericarditis with moderate circumferential pericardial effusion and MRI features suggestive of early constrictive hemodynamics.

Cardiac MRI demonstrates normal biventricular chamber sizes, wall thickness, and mass. Left ventricular ejection fraction is 61% and right ventricular ejection fraction is 57% without any localized wall motion anomalies. Myocardial tissue characterization is normal with native T1 mapping, T2 mapping, and extracellular volume (ECV) within normal limits. No late gadolinium enhancement is observed.

Impression: Unremarkable cardiac MRI. No evidence of myocardial edema, infiltration, hypertrophy, or late gadolinium enhancement.

Fetal MRI at 21 weeks gestation reveals an open neural tube defect in the lumbosacral region. There is herniation of meninges and neural elements through a posterior spinal defect spanning L4-S2. Cranial secondary signs are noted, including bifrontal indentation of the skull (lemon sign) and herniation of the cerebellar vermis with effacement of the cisterna magna (banana sign), consistent with a Chiari II malformation. Mild ventriculomegaly is present with atria measuring 12.0 mm.

The remaining fetal organs are unremarkable. Impression: Open lumbosacral myelomeningocele with associated Chiari II malformation. Fetal surgery consultation and multidisciplinary care are advised.

MR imaging demonstrates a crescent-shaped extra-axial fluid collection over the left cerebral hemisphere, measuring up to 1.8 cm in maximal depth. This collection exhibits heterogeneous signal intensity, with areas of high T1 signal representing subacute blood products mixed with more chronic hypointense components. There is moderate mass effect, resulting in effacement of the left cortical sulci and a 5 mm shift of midline structures to the right.

Impression: Left-sided chronic to subacute subdural hematoma with significant mass effect and mild midline shift. Urgent neurosurgical consultation is recommended to evaluate for evacuation.

Fetal MRI evaluated at 30 weeks gestation reveals abnormal renal development. The left kidney is significantly enlarged and completely replaced by multiple non-communicating cysts of varying sizes, consistent with a multicystic dysplastic kidney (MCDK). The right kidney is normal in size and appearance.

Amniotic fluid volume is subjectively normal. Intracranial structures show symmetric lateral ventricles with an atrial width of 6.3 mm and appropriate sulcation. Impression: Left multicystic dysplastic kidney (MCDK) with a normal contralateral right kidney and normal amniotic fluid volume.

MRI of the brain demonstrates normal anatomical structure. The cerebral hemispheres exhibit normal cortical thickness and sulcation. No focal signal abnormalities are seen on T2 or FLAIR sequences. The ventricular system and basal cisterns are normal in caliber. No signs of restricted diffusion or pathologic intracranial enhancement.

Impression: Normal brain MRI. No evidence of mass lesion, ischemia, demyelinating disease, or hemorrhage.

MRI of the pituitary gland demonstrates a well-defined hypo-enhancing lesion within the left aspect of the adenohypophysis, measuring 1.2 x 1.0 x 0.9 cm. The lesion causes mild upward bulging of the diaphragmatic sellae and minimal deviation of the pituitary stalk to the right. The optic chiasm is structurally intact with no evidence of compression.

Impression: Left-sided pituitary macroadenoma (measuring >10 mm) without optic chiasm compression or cavernous sinus invasion. Recommend endocrine and clinical follow-up.

The brain parenchyma demonstrates symmetric structure with age-appropriate gyral and sulcal architecture. There are no focal mass lesions, restricted diffusion, or acute hemorrhage. The cerebral ventricles are normal in configuration and caliber. Major intracranial arterial and venous channels show normal flow voids.

Impression: Unremarkable MRI of the brain. No structural, inflammatory, or vascular abnormalities are identified to explain the patient's neurological symptoms or clinical complaints.

Fetal MRI performed at 22 weeks gestation. There is a complete absence of amniotic fluid (anhydramnios), which severely limits fetal motion and compromises image resolution. Both fetal kidneys are not visualized in the renal fossae or within the pelvis. The bladder is not filled. Fetal lung volumes are severely reduced, consistent with secondary pulmonary hypoplasia. Intracranial structures demonstrate normal morphology for 22 weeks, with a smooth cortical mantle and lateral ventricular atria measuring 6.0 mm.

The fetal spine and extremities are poorly visualized due to lack of fluid contrast but appear grossly intact. Impression: Bilateral renal agenesis associated with anhydramnios and severe pulmonary hypoplasia, carrying an extremely guarded prognosis.

Cardiac magnetic resonance imaging demonstrates normal biventricular size and function. The left ventricular ejection fraction is 60%, and the right ventricular ejection fraction is 56%. The myocardium is normal in thickness with no regional wall motion abnormalities. No evidence of myocardial edema is seen on T2-weighted imaging. Late gadolinium enhancement imaging shows no abnormal areas of myocardial enhancement or scarring.

Impression: Normal cardiac MRI study with preserved biventricular systolic function and no evidence of focal myocardial scar or active inflammation.

Magnetic resonance imaging of the heart demonstrates normal cardiac anatomy and function. Left ventricular end-diastolic volume is 142 mL and right ventricular end-diastolic volume is 135 mL, both within standard reference limits. Left ventricular ejection fraction is calculated at 62%, and right ventricular ejection fraction is 56%. The pericardium is of normal thickness and there is no pericardial fluid accumulation. No late gadolinium enhancement is observed.

Impression: Normal cardiac MRI with normal ventricular volumes, preserved systolic function, and no evidence of myocardial fibrosis or structural abnormalities.

Fetal MRI at 24 weeks gestation shows a severely hypoplastic and rotated cerebellar vermis. There is a large cystic dilation of the posterior fossa that freely communicates with an enlarged fourth ventricle. The torcula and transverse sinuses are elevated. The supratentorial brain shows symmetric lateral ventricles with an atrial width of 9.2 mm, with a normal early sulcation pattern.

Impression: Classic Dandy-Walker malformation characterized by cerebellar vermian hypoplasia and posterior fossa expansion. Supratentorial brain anatomy is currently intact.

Fetal MRI evaluated at 21 weeks gestation demonstrates normal intracranial and extracranial development. The cerebral hemispheres exhibit appropriate sulcation and migration patterns for 21 weeks, showing early, well-defined sylvian fissures. The bilateral lateral ventricles are normal in size, with the atrial width measuring 5.4 mm. The corpus callosum, brainstem, and posterior fossa structures are well-formed with no cerebellar abnormalities.

Fetal spine, thorax, and abdominal organs are unremarkable. Impression: Normal fetal MRI study at 21 weeks gestation showing appropriate brain development and normal ventricular measurements.

Fetal MRI performed at 22 weeks gestation demonstrates normal intracranial anatomy. The cerebral hemispheres exhibit appropriate, age-expected sulcation with normal opercularization of the Sylvian fissures. The ventricular system is normal in size, with the lateral ventricular atrium measuring 6.4 mm. The corpus callosum is completely visualized and morphologically normal. Posterior fossa structures, including the cerebellar vermis and brainstem, are unremarkable.

Impression: Normal fetal MRI study at 22 weeks gestation. No structural brain anomalies or developmental deviations identified.

Fetal MRI at 30 weeks gestation demonstrates expected intracranial and visceral development. The cerebral hemispheres exhibit appropriate gyral and sulcal patterns for 30 weeks, with deep and symmetric sylvian fissures. The lateral ventricles are normal, with the atria measuring 5.8 mm. Midline structures are fully formed.

The fetal chest and abdomen reveal normal structures and T2 signal intensities. Spine and extremities are unremarkable. Impression: Normal fetal MRI study at 30 weeks gestation, demonstrating appropriate brain development and normal visceral anatomy.

Fetal magnetic resonance imaging at 32 weeks gestation reveals progressive and age-appropriate brain development. Cortical folding and sulcation are well-advanced, showing defined central and parieto-occipital sulci matching the gestational age. The ventricular atrium measures 6.1 mm bilaterally, without signs of ventriculomegaly or midline shift. The corpus callosum is completely visualized and demonstrates normal thickness throughout its course. The posterior fossa, cerebellar hemispheres, and cisterna magna are normal.

Fetal chest, abdomen, and skeletal structures show normal signal and positioning. The amniotic fluid volume is within normal limits. Impression: Normal fetal MRI showing appropriate cranial maturation and completely unremarkable fetal anatomy at 32 weeks gestation.

Fetal MRI at 25 weeks gestation demonstrates severe micromelia with markedly shortened, curved femurs resembling telephone receivers. The fetal chest is severely narrowed and bell-shaped with short ribs, consistent with pulmonary hypoplasia. The fetal brain exhibits normal ventricles with an atrial width of 6.8 mm, though there is a relative prominence of the temporal lobes with slightly delayed sulcation.

Impression: Skeletal dysplasia, highly suggestive of thanatophoric dysplasia type I, with associated severe narrow chest cavity.

MRI of the heart demonstrates normal biventricular volumes and preserved systolic function (LV EF 61%, RV EF 58%). There are no regional wall motion abnormalities, myocardial hypertrophy, or signs of past or present myocardial injury on late gadolinium enhancement imaging.

Impression: Unremarkable cardiac MRI. Normal biventricular performance and size with no structural abnormalities.

MR imaging of the brain and optic pathways was performed using multiplanar, high-resolution sequences. The optic nerves, optic chiasm, and optic tracts demonstrate normal caliber, path, and signal intensity. The brain parenchyma is normal in appearance, with no mass lesions, abnormal enhancement, or areas of restricted diffusion.

Impression: Completely normal brain and orbital MRI. No structural abnormality or pathology identified along the visual pathways.

Cardiac MRI demonstrates normal ventricular volumes and wall thickness. Calculated left ventricular ejection fraction is 61% (EDV 135 mL, ESV 53 mL) and right ventricular ejection fraction is 56% (EDV 140 mL, ESV 61 mL). Valvular morphology and motion are unremarkable, with no significant stenosis or regurgitation. Late gadolinium enhancement sequences show no focal abnormalities, and native T1 values are within normal physiological limits.

Impression: Unremarkable cardiac MRI. Normal biventricular size and systolic function without signs of myocardial scar, edema, or infiltration.

MR imaging reveals a focus of acute lobar intracerebral hemorrhage within the left occipital lobe, measuring approximately 2.3 x 2.0 cm. The lesion shows acute blood products on susceptibility-weighted imaging (SWI) with surrounding vasogenic edema. Multiple punctate foci of microhemorrhage are also noted at the lobar gray-white junctions globally on SWI.

Impression: Acute left occipital lobar hemorrhage with surrounding edema. The presence of multiple cerebral microbleeds predominantly in lobar locations is highly suggestive of cerebral amyloid angiopathy (CAA).

MRI of the heart shows normal dimensions of all four cardiac chambers. The myocardium is of normal thickness and signal intensity on all sequences. Quantitative analysis of the ventricles yields a left ventricular ejection fraction of 63% and a right ventricular ejection fraction of 59%, with no focal wall motion abnormalities. No late enhancement is seen.

Impression: Normal cardiac MRI study. No evidence of myocardial infarction, active inflammation, cardiomyopathy, or significant valvular dysfunction.

Cardiac MRI reveals a large defect in the mid-interatrial septum measuring 2.4 cm, consistent with a secundum-type atrial septal defect (ASD). There is severe volume overload of the right atrium and right ventricle, with the right ventricular end-diastolic volume index (RVEDVI) elevated at 135 mL/m². Phase-contrast flow quantification indicates a significant left-to-right shunt with a Qp:Qs ratio of 2.1.

Impression: Large secundum atrial septal defect with a hemodynamically significant left-to-right shunt (Qp:Qs = 2.1) and severe right-sided chamber enlargement. Right ventricular systolic function remains preserved.

Cardiac MRI shows marked dilatation of the left ventricle with a left ventricular end-diastolic volume index (LVEDVI) of 135 mL/m². There is global hypokinesia with severely reduced left ventricular systolic function, yielding an ejection fraction of 28%. The right ventricle is also mildly dilated with a depressed ejection fraction of 42%. Diffuse, longitudinal mid-wall late gadolinium enhancement is noted in the interventricular septum.

No subendocardial enhancement is seen, ruling out a primary ischemic etiology. There is no evidence of intracardiac thrombus on early gadolinium sequences. Impression: Non-ischemic dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM) with severe left ventricular dysfunction and characteristic septal mid-wall fibrosis.

Fetal MRI at 21 weeks gestation demonstrates a lumbar myelomeningocele defect with a bulging neural placode and overlying soft tissue defect. Features of Chiari II malformation, including cerebellar herniation and a banana sign, are present. Mild colpocephaly is noted with ventricular atria measuring 12.5 mm. Intracranial sulcation is appropriate for 21 weeks.

Impression: Spina bifida aperta (lumbar myelomeningocele) and associated Chiari II malformation with moderate ventriculomegaly.

Fetal MRI at 23 weeks gestation demonstrates a keyhole fluid communication between the fourth ventricle and the cisterna magna, characteristic of a Dandy-Walker variant. There is mild hypoplasia of the inferior cerebellar vermis, which is slightly rotated upwards. The posterior fossa is not significantly enlarged and the tentorium is in a normal position. The lateral ventricles are normal, measuring 6.2 mm.

Impression: Dandy-Walker variant characterized by mild inferior vermian hypoplasia and keyhole communication with the fourth ventricle. No ventriculomegaly.

Multisequence brain MRI was performed to evaluate persistent lightheadedness. Brain parenchyma exhibits normal morphology and signal intensity. No areas of restricted diffusion or abnormal contrast enhancement are demonstrated. Ventricles, sulci, and cisterns are within normal limits for age. Visualized cranial nerves are symmetric and unremarkable.

Impression: Normal brain MRI. No structural abnormality, extra-axial fluid collections, or signs of elevated intracranial pressure are identified.

Fetal MRI at 23 weeks gestation demonstrates borderline ventriculomegaly. The left lateral ventricle atrium measures 10.5 mm, while the right lateral ventricle atrium is within normal limits at 8.8 mm. Fetal brain sulcation is normal. The remainder of the intracranial structures are structurally intact.

Impression: Borderline isolated left-sided fetal ventriculomegaly. Recommend follow-up imaging in 4 weeks to monitor ventricular size.

Fetal MRI at 29 weeks gestation demonstrates bilateral, enlarged multicystic dysplastic kidneys (MCDK). Multiple large, non-communicating cysts occupy the renal parenchyma bilaterally. Severe oligohydramnios is present. Intracranial evaluation shows appropriate sulcation for 29 weeks and a normal ventricular atrial width of 6.0 mm.

Impression: Bilateral multicystic dysplastic kidneys with severe oligohydramnios, raising concern for secondary pulmonary hypoplasia.

Cardiac MRI demonstrates regional hypokinesis and thinning of the apical and mid-anterior walls of the left ventricle. Left ventricular systolic function is moderately reduced with an ejection fraction of 35%. Late gadolinium enhancement imaging reveals transmural hyperenhancement (>75% wall thickness) involving the apex and mid-anterior wall, corresponding strictly to the left anterior descending (LAD) coronary artery territory.

Impression: Moderately reduced left ventricular systolic function with a transmural anterior and apical myocardial infarction. No viable myocardium is noted in the affected LAD territory.

Fetal MRI at 27 weeks gestation reveals features highly suggestive of skeletal dysplasia, such as thanatophoric dysplasia. There is severe rhizomelic shortening and bowing of all long bones. The thorax is significantly narrowed and bell-shaped, with very short ribs. Macrocephaly is noted, with frontal bossing.

The intracranial structures show age-appropriate sulcation patterns and normal ventricular atrial measurements of 6.8 mm. Impression: Severe skeletal dysplasia characterized by severe rhizomelic limb shortening, narrow thorax, and macrocephaly, highly suggestive of thanatophoric dysplasia.

MRI of the brain reveals an ill-defined, non-enhancing expansile mass within the left frontal lobe cortex and subcortical white matter, measuring approximately 3.8 x 3.5 cm. The lesion is hyperintense on T2/FLAIR sequences and does not exhibit any restricted diffusion or significant enhancement on post-contrast sequences. There is mild localized mass effect with partial effacement of the adjacent frontal horn of the left lateral ventricle.

Impression: Non-enhancing expansile left frontal lobe mass, highly suggestive of a low-grade diffuse astrocytoma (WHO Grade II). Neurosurgical consultation and MR spectroscopy or perfusion studies may be helpful for further characterization.

Cardiac MRI was performed to exclude structural pathology in the setting of frequent palpitations. Cine sequences demonstrate normal chamber morphology and dimensions. The left ventricular ejection fraction is 63% and the right ventricular ejection fraction is 57%. No late gadolinium enhancement or areas of elevated T2 signal are seen. The heart valves are structurally sound.

Impression: Unremarkable cardiac MRI. No structural, myocardial, or valvular substrate found to explain the palpitations.

A small, restrictive perimembranous ventricular septal defect (VSD) is identified, measuring 6 mm in diameter. Phase-contrast imaging demonstrates a left-to-right shunt with a Qp/Qs ratio of 1.3:1. The left and right ventricular volumes are normal, and global systolic function is preserved (LV EF 64%).

Impression: Small perimembranous ventricular septal defect with a hemodynamically minor left-to-right shunt and no evidence of pulmonary overcirculation or chamber enlargement.

Cardiac MRI evaluates a young adult with hypertension. There is focal, discrete narrowing of the proximal descending thoracic aorta just distal to the origin of the left subclavian artery, measuring 9 mm in diameter compared to 19 mm at the diaphragmatic level. Prominent internal mammary and intercostal collateral arteries are visualized. Left ventricular mass index is mildly elevated, and LVEF is 60%.

Impression: Classic anatomical features of discrete coarctation of the aorta with prominent collateral circulation and mild secondary left ventricular concentric remodeling.

MRI of the internal auditory canals and brain demonstrates a well-circumscribed, intensely enhancing mass centered within the left cerebellopontine angle, measuring 1.8 x 1.4 cm. The mass extends into the left internal auditory canal, causing mild widening. There is mild mass effect on the left cerebellar hemisphere and brainstem.

Impression: Left cerebellopontine angle mass with internal auditory canal extension, highly characteristic of a vestibular schwannoma (acoustic neuroma). Recommend ENT/neurosurgery consultation.

MR examination of the brain reveals a well-defined zone of restricted diffusion involving the left middle cerebral artery (MCA) territory, specifically the posterior limb of the internal capsule and adjacent corona radiata. Corresponding low signal on ADC maps confirms acute ischemic stroke. Mild local mass effect with effacement of the adjacent left lateral ventricle body is observed, but no midline shift or herniation is present.

Impression: Acute ischemic infarction in the left MCA territory (posterior limb of the internal capsule and corona radiata). Mild localized mass effect is noted. Recommend urgent clinical correlation and stroke team evaluation.

Fetal MRI at 25 weeks gestation demonstrates an enlarged posterior fossa with a cystic fluid collection that freely communicates with the fourth ventricle. There is severe hypoplasia and upward rotation of the cerebellar vermis. The torcular herophili and transverse sinuses are superiorly displaced. The lateral ventricles are mildly dilated, with the right atrium measuring 8.5 mm and the left atrium measuring 8.2 mm. Supratentorial brain parenchyma and sulcation patterns are otherwise normal for 25 weeks.

Impression: Classical Dandy-Walker malformation at 25 weeks gestation, characterized by vermian hypoplasia, cystic dilation of the posterior fossa, and torcular elevation.
