Cardiac MRI demonstrates diffuse, concentric left ventricular hypertrophy with a wall thickness of up to 18 mm. There is also thickening of the right ventricular free wall (6 mm) and interatrial septum. Left ventricular ejection fraction is mildly reduced at 48%. T1 mapping values are severely elevated at 1390 ms, and extracellular volume (ECV) is highly elevated at 48%.

Post-contrast imaging shows a characteristic pattern of diffuse, subendocardial late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) across both ventricles, accompanied by rapid pool clearance of gadolinium. Impression: Cardiac MRI findings are highly characteristic of cardiac amyloidosis (restrictive cardiomyopathy pattern) with severe diffuse interstitial infiltration.

Fetal MRI at 26 weeks gestation demonstrates normal anatomy. The cerebral hemispheres exhibit appropriate gyral patterns and Sylvian fissure operculization for 26 weeks. The lateral ventricles are symmetric with an atrial width of 6.5 mm. The corpus callosum is intact and appropriate in length. The chest, abdomen, spine, and bladder are all normal, with adequate amniotic fluid and standard fetal biometry.

Impression: Normal fetal MRI study at 26 weeks gestation showing age-appropriate structural development and no evidence of anomalies.

MRI of the brain demonstrates an ill-defined, non-enhancing T2/FLAIR hyperintense infiltrative mass within the left frontal lobe, measuring approximately 3.1 x 2.7 cm. The lesion is primarily localized within the subcortical white matter and does not cause significant surrounding vasogenic edema or mass effect. There is no focal restricted diffusion or necrotic core.

Impression: Infiltrative, non-enhancing intra-axial lesion in the left frontal lobe, highly concerning for a low-grade diffuse glioma or astrocytoma. Close neuro-oncological clinical follow-up or biopsy is indicated.

Cardiac MRI evaluates for possible arrhythmogenic cardiomyopathy. The right ventricle is severely dilated (RVEDVI 130 mL/m²) with localized dyskinesis and micro-aneurysm formation within the right ventricular outflow tract (RVOT) and apical free wall. Right ventricular ejection fraction is significantly reduced at 34%.

High-resolution T1-weighted sequences demonstrate intramyocardial fatty infiltration of the right ventricular free wall, confirmed on fat-saturated sequences. Focal late gadolinium enhancement is noted in the RV free wall. Left ventricular size and systolic function are normal (LVEF 59%). Impression: Right ventricular structural and functional abnormalities characteristic of Arrhythmogenic Right Ventricular Cardiomyopathy (ARVC).

Brain MRI reveals a large, infiltrating, heterogeneously enhancing mass centered in the right temporal lobe, measuring approximately 4.5 x 4.2 x 3.8 cm. The lesion exhibits central necrotic changes, peripheral ring-like enhancement, and substantial surrounding vasogenic edema. There is moderate mass effect causing partial compression of the right lateral ventricle and a 6 mm leftward midline shift.

Impression: Highly aggressive intra-axial neoplasm within the right temporal lobe, highly suspicious for Glioblastoma (GBM). Recommend urgent neurosurgical review and tissue biopsy for histopathological confirmation.

MRI of the brain demonstrates normal ventricular size and preserved cortical sulcation. Hippocampal volumes are symmetric and normal for the patient's age. There are no signs of intracranial space-occupying lesion, major territorial ischemia, or abnormal enhancement.

Impression: Unremarkable MRI of the brain. No structural, ischemic, or atrophic changes are visualized to account for reported transient memory lapses.

Multiplanar steady-state free precession (SSFP) cine sequences reveal normal cardiac anatomy. Left and right ventricular end-diastolic and end-systolic volumes are within established physiological ranges. There are no regional wall motion abnormalities or evidence of pathological tissue enhancement. Myocardial native T1 and T2 values are normal.

Impression: Unremarkable cardiac MRI. Preserved biventricular systolic function with an LVEF of 60% and RVEF of 56%.

MRI of the brain was completed without contrast. All sequences show normal cerebral and cerebellar anatomy with clear differentiation of grey and white matter. The ventricular system, subarachnoid spaces, and basal cisterns are completely unremarkable. No focal signal abnormalities or structural abnormalities are found.

Impression: Completely normal non-contrast brain MRI. No organic cause identified for the patient's syncopal episode.

Fetal MRI at 26 weeks gestation demonstrates a large left-sided congenital diaphragmatic hernia. There is herniation of the stomach, multiple loops of small bowel, and a portion of the left lobe of the liver into the left hemithorax. This has resulted in a severe mediastinal shift to the right and compression of both the left and right lungs. The observed-to-expected total fetal lung volume (O/E TLV) is calculated at approximately 38%, which indicates significant pulmonary hypoplasia.

Intracranial anatomy is unremarkable, with appropriate sulcation for 26 weeks and lateral ventricular atrial measurements of 6.0 mm. Impression: Left-sided congenital diaphragmatic hernia with liver herniation and severe pulmonary hypoplasia. High risk for neonatal respiratory distress.

Fetal MRI at 21 weeks gestation demonstrates complete absence of bilateral kidneys in the renal fossae. Normal renal arterial vessels are not identified, and there is no visualization of the urinary bladder. Severe anhydramnios (lack of amniotic fluid) is present, resulting in severe compression of the fetus. Consequently, there is marked compression of the fetal thorax with significant pulmonary hypoplasia.

Fetal intracranial anatomy shows normal sulcation for 21 weeks, and the lateral ventricles are normal in size, measuring 5.4 mm. Impression: Bilateral renal agenesis associated with anhydramnios, consistent with Potter sequence and severe secondary pulmonary hypoplasia.

MRI of the brain demonstrates marked dilatation of the lateral and third ventricles with relatively normal fourth ventricle, highly suggestive of aqueductal stenosis. There is prominent transependymal flow of cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) manifested as periventricular T2/FLAIR hyperintensity. Significant thinning and elevation of the corpus callosum are also observed.

Impression: Obstructive hydrocephalus, likely secondary to aqueductal stenosis, with active transependymal CSF migration. Prompt neurosurgical consultation is recommended.

Patient underwent cardiac MRI for pre-chemotherapy baseline assessment. The left ventricle is normal in size and demonstrates normal global and regional systolic function with an ejection fraction of 64%. The right ventricle is also normal with an ejection fraction of 57%. No late gadolinium enhancement is identified, and native T1 values are within normal limits, suggesting no pre-existing myocardial fibrosis.

Impression: Normal cardiac MRI with preserved biventricular systolic function and no evidence of myocardial scar, providing a reassuring baseline prior to cardiotoxic oncological therapy.

Fetal MRI at 30 weeks gestation demonstrates asymmetric ventriculomegaly. The right lateral ventricular atrium is dilated, measuring 12.8 mm (moderate ventriculomegaly), while the left lateral ventricular atrium measures 8.5 mm (within normal limits). No intraventricular hemorrhage, periventricular nodular heterotopia, or other brain anomalies are identified. Sulcation patterns match the expected 30-week developmental timeline.

The chest, abdomen, and spine are normal. Impression: Isolated right-sided moderate fetal ventriculomegaly. Follow-up imaging is recommended to evaluate for progression or resolution.

Magnetic resonance imaging of the fetus at 32 weeks gestation shows completely normal intracranial anatomy. The cortical gyration is highly appropriate for 32 weeks, displaying well-developed central, precentral, and superior temporal sulci. The lateral ventricles are symmetrical and measure 5.8 mm. The corpus callosum is intact, and the posterior fossa demonstrates a normal cerebellar vermis.

The fetal chest shows symmetric lungs of normal volume, and the abdominal viscera are unremarkable. Impression: Normal fetal brain and somatic MRI at 32 weeks gestation with expected cortical maturation.

MRI of the brain demonstrates herniation of the cerebellar tonsils approximately 7.5 mm below the level of the foramen magnum. The tonsils appear peg-like and pointed. There is crowding of the craniocervical junction, but the fourth ventricle remains normally positioned. Evaluation of the cervical spinal cord (partially visualized) reveals no evidence of syrinx formation.

Impression: Chiari I malformation, with 7.5 mm of cerebellar tonsillar ectopia and crowding of the foramen magnum. No evidence of cervical syringomyelia on the visualized spinal sequences.

Cardiac MRI demonstrates normal chamber dimensions, valvular function, and myocardial tissue characteristics. The calculated left ventricular ejection fraction is 63% and the right ventricular ejection fraction is 61%. Late gadolinium enhancement imaging shows no evidence of focal myocardial scar or fibrosis.

Impression: Normal cardiac MRI study. No evidence of cardiomyopathy, ischemic injury, or valvular pathology.

Fetal MRI at 28 weeks gestation reveals complete agenesis of the corpus callosum. The lateral ventricles show a classic teardrop configuration (colpocephaly) with parallel orientation of the lateral ventricles. The left atrium measures 11.2 mm and the right atrium measures 10.8 mm. The third ventricle is elevated and moderately dilated. The posterior fossa and brainstem appear otherwise intact.

Impression: Complete agenesis of the fetal corpus callosum with associated mild colpocephaly. Pediatric neurosurgical consultation and postnatal follow-up are recommended.

Fetal MRI at 22 weeks gestation reveals a low lumbar neural tube defect with an overlying herniated cerebrospinal fluid sac containing neural elements, consistent with a myelomeningocele. Intracranial evaluation demonstrates a Chiari II malformation, characterized by a small posterior fossa, downward displacement of the cerebellar vermis ('banana sign'), and bifrontal narrowing ('lemon sign'). There is mild ventriculomegaly with a lateral ventricular atrial width of 10.8 mm and normal early sulcation.

Impression: Lumbosacral myelomeningocele with secondary Chiari II malformation. Mild ventriculomegaly is present.

Fetal MRI at 36 weeks gestation demonstrates advanced fetal development. The cerebral cortex shows deep, complex sulcation and secondary gyral patterns that are highly appropriate for a near-term infant. The lateral ventricles are completely normal with a symmetric atrial diameter of 6.5 mm. The brainstem, cerebellum, and corpus callosum are fully formed and unremarkable.

Impression: Normal, mature fetal brain MRI at 36 weeks gestation showing excellent cortical development.

A cardiac magnetic resonance examination was performed utilizing comprehensive cine, perfusion, and late gadolinium enhancement sequences. The left ventricle is normal in size and volume with concentric geometry. Left ventricular systolic function is well-preserved, with a calculated ejection fraction of 62% and no regional wall motion abnormalities. The right ventricle is also normal in size and function, with an ejection fraction of 56%. No late gadolinium enhancement is visualized to suggest myocardial scar or focal fibrosis.

Impression: Normal cardiac MRI study. There is no evidence of myocardial infarction, infiltrative disease, or cardiomyopathy, with completely normal biventricular size and systolic performance.

Brain MRI demonstrates unremarkable intra- and extra-axial structures. No acute infarct, acute intracranial hemorrhage, or pathologically enhancing mass lesion is identified. The cerebral ventricles, sulci, and cisterns are within normal limits for age. Visualized paranasal sinuses are clear.

Impression: Normal magnetic resonance imaging of the brain with no acute abnormalities seen.

Fetal MRI at 27 weeks gestation demonstrates normal anatomical development. Symmetrical gyration and sulcation patterns are observed, suitable for the gestational age. The ventricular system is normal, with atria measuring 6.1 mm bilaterally. The corpus callosum and posterior fossa elements are well-preserved and intact. Visualized visceral structures show normal development.

Impression: Unremarkable fetal MRI at 27 weeks gestation showing normal neurological and visceral organ development.

Fetal MRI evaluated at 34 weeks gestation demonstrates a well-developed fetus with appropriate intracranial and visceral structures. The cerebral cortex shows advanced secondary and tertiary sulcation appropriate for 34 weeks. The lateral ventricles are completely symmetric, with atrial diameters measuring 6.0 mm. Midline structures, including the corpus callosum and optic chiasm, are normal. Fetal lungs show normal T2 signal intensity and volume relative to fetal weight, indicating no diaphragmatic hernia or masses.

Impression: Unremarkable fetal MRI at 34 weeks gestation demonstrating age-appropriate neural and visceral development. No anatomical abnormalities noted.

The study demonstrates excessive trabeculation of the left ventricular apical and mid-lateral walls. In end-diastole, the ratio of non-compacted to compacted myocardium is calculated at 2.6, which meets criteria for non-compaction. Mild dilatation of the left ventricle is observed, with a mildly reduced ejection fraction of 47%.

Impression: Left ventricular non-compaction (LVNC) cardiomyopathy with mild global systolic dysfunction. No evidence of myocardial infarction or gross fibrosis on late gadolinium enhancement.

Fetal MRI at 26 weeks gestation demonstrates cerebellar vermian hypoplasia consistent with a Dandy-Walker variant. The cerebellar vermis is small and abnormally rotated upward, and the fourth ventricle is mildly dilated. There is also mild enlargement of the cisterna magna. The lateral ventricles are borderline normal, with the atrium measuring 8.8 mm.

The cerebral hemispheres exhibit appropriate sulcation and migration patterns for 26 weeks, with well-formed primary sulci. Impression: Fetal cerebellar vermian hypoplasia (Dandy-Walker variant) with mild posterior fossa fluid space enlargement.

Fetal MRI at 31 weeks gestation shows normal intracranial development. The ventricular system is normal, with symmetric lateral ventricular atria measuring 5.9 mm. Cortical folding and sulcation are normal, demonstrating well-defined central and cingulate sulci appropriate for 31 weeks. Visceral anatomy of the fetal chest and abdomen is normal with normal stomach bubble and renal architecture.

Impression: Normal fetal MRI study showing age-appropriate brain development, normal ventricular size, and unremarkable fetal organ morphology.

Cardiac MRI demonstrates normal left and right ventricular chambers. The left ventricular end-diastolic volume is 125 mL, and the wall thickness is normal. No regional wall motion abnormalities or focal contractile deficits are identified. Delayed enhancement imaging shows no evidence of myocardial necrosis or fibrosis, with an LVEF of 57%.

Impression: Normal cardiac MRI study. No evidence of myocardial infarction, structural heart disease, or non-ischemic cardiomyopathy.

Brain MRI demonstrates advanced cerebral involution and prominent ventricles consistent with senescent changes. There are extensive, confluent T2/FLAIR hyperintensities in the periventricular and deep subcortical white matter, representing severe microvascular ischemic disease. No areas of acute infarction or hemorrhage are identified.

Impression: Severe, chronic small vessel ischemic white matter disease along with generalized cerebral atrophy. No acute intracranial process.

Cardiac MRI demonstrates a moderate-sized subendocardial perfusion defect and subsequent dense late gadolinium enhancement in the mid-to-apical anterior and anteroseptal walls, consistent with prior myocardial infarction in the left anterior descending artery distribution. Transmurality of the scar is estimated at 50-75% in the mid-anterior segment. Left ventricular ejection fraction is reduced at 42% with regional hypokinesis of the infarcted segments.

Impression: Prior subendocardial-to-transmural myocardial infarction in the LAD territory with associated wall motion abnormalities and moderately reduced left ventricular systolic function. Viability remains in the infarcted segments given less than 75% transmurality.

Fetal MRI at 27 weeks gestation demonstrates complete agenesis of the corpus callosum. There is a classic parallel configuration of the lateral ventricles (colpocephaly) with teardrop-shaped posterior horns, measuring 12.8 mm at the atrium. The third ventricle is elevated and slightly dilated, protruding superiorly. Interhemispheric sulci show a radial wheel-spoke pattern arising from the roof of the third ventricle. Radial migration and sulcation patterns otherwise match the gestational age of 27 weeks.

Impression: Complete agenesis of the corpus callosum with colpocephaly and mild-to-moderate ventriculomegaly.

The examination reveals a thinned, akinetic inferior wall of the left ventricle from base to apex. Left ventricular ejection fraction is severely reduced at 32%. Late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) imaging shows extensive, transmural enhancement of the entire inferior and inferolateral walls, consistent with a chronic, complete myocardial infarction. No residual viable myocardium is identified in these segments.

Impression: Severe chronic ischemic cardiomyopathy with a large, transmural, non-viable inferior myocardial infarction. Global left ventricular systolic dysfunction is severely depressed.

Multiplanar, multisequence MRI of the brain was performed. The ventricular system, cortical sulci, and basal cisterns are normal in size, shape, and configuration. No focal areas of abnormal signal intensity or restricted diffusion are identified within the brain parenchyma. Evaluation of the internal auditory canals reveals symmetric facial and vestibulocochlear nerves, with no evidence of cerebellopontine angle mass or abnormal enhancement.

Impression: Normal MR imaging of the brain and internal auditory canals. No structural abnormality, mass lesion, or demyelinating process is identified to account for the patient's dizziness.

Cardiac MRI shows a subendocardial late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) pattern involving approximately 25-50% of the wall thickness in the inferior and inferoseptal walls of the left ventricle, characteristic of a prior subendocardial myocardial infarction in the right coronary artery (RCA) territory. There is mild hypokinesia of these segments. Left ventricular ejection fraction is borderline reduced at 48%.

Impression: Prior subendocardial myocardial infarction in the RCA territory with mild regional wall motion abnormalities and borderline left ventricular systolic dysfunction.

Cardiac MRI was obtained for the evaluation of newly diagnosed congestive heart failure. Cine imaging reveals severe, diffuse dilation of the left ventricle (LVEDV 245 mL) and moderate dilation of the right ventricle. There is global, diffuse hypokinesis of the left ventricular myocardium, with a severely depressed ejection fraction calculated at 28%. The left atrium is also severely enlarged.

Late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) imaging demonstrates a thin, linear mid-myocardial stripe of enhancement along the basal-to-mid interventricular septum, characteristic of non-ischemic dilated cardiomyopathy. No subendocardial enhancement is noted. Impression: Severely dilated cardiomyopathy with severe global left ventricular dysfunction (EF 28%) and non-ischemic septal mid-wall fibrosis.

A bicuspid aortic valve (likely Sievers type 1) is visualized with severe calcification and restricted opening. Phase contrast velocity mapping indicates a peak systolic velocity of 4.3 m/s across the valve, consistent with severe stenosis. There is severe, concentric left ventricular hypertrophy with septal thickness of 18 mm. LV systolic function is preserved with an EF of 55%.

Impression: Severe bicuspid aortic valve stenosis with severe secondary concentric left ventricular hypertrophy. There is no evidence of coexisting aortic coarctation.

The thoracic aorta was evaluated. There is a discrete, focal narrowing of the proximal descending thoracic aorta, located just distal to the origin of the left subclavian artery. The minimum internal diameter at the coarctation site measures 8 mm, compared to a normal distal aortic diameter of 18 mm. Collateral vessels arising from the internal mammary and intercostal arteries are prominent. The left ventricle is concentric and mildly hypertrophic with an EF of 63%.

Impression: Classic post-ductal coarctation of the aorta in an adult patient, with significant focal stenosis and extensive collateralization. Associated mild left ventricular hypertrophy is present.

Cardiac MRI reveals symmetric thickening of the left ventricular walls (septal thickness 15 mm) with diffuse, subendocardial late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) sparing the apex, a pattern highly characteristic of cardiac amyloidosis. There is associated thickening of the interatrial septum and right ventricular free wall. Left ventricular systolic function is mildly reduced (LVEF 48%) with a restrictive filling pattern.

Impression: Findings are strongly indicative of cardiac amyloidosis, characterized by diffuse subendocardial LGE, bi-atrial enlargement, and concentric myocardial thickening.

Cardiac MRI demonstrates normal left and right ventricular chamber dimensions and wall thickness. Left ventricular end-diastolic volume is 142 mL, and end-systolic volume is 54 mL, yielding an ejection fraction of 62%. There is no evidence of regional wall motion abnormalities, myocardial edema on T2-weighted imaging, or abnormal late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) to suggest myocardial scarring or fibrosis.

Impression: Unremarkable cardiac MRI study. Both ventricles demonstrate normal size, global systolic function, and myocardial tissue characteristics with no focal scar or active inflammatory processes.

Brain MRI displays protrusion of the cerebellar tonsils approximately 6.5 mm below the plane of the foramen magnum. The third and fourth ventricles are normal in size. No supratentorial mass lesions are identified, and the cerebral hemispheres are normal. Fast imaging sequences of the spine show no signs of cervical syrinx formation.

Impression: Chiari I malformation with 6.5 mm tonsillar ectopia. No associated syringomyelia or hydrocephalus seen on the current examination.

MR imaging of the brain demonstrates an ill-defined, non-enhancing area of T2/FLAIR hyperintensity centered within the left frontal lobe white matter, measuring approximately 3.2 x 2.8 cm. The lesion does not show restricted diffusion or significant mass effect. No microhemorrhages are present on gradient echo sequences. Surrounding cerebral structures appear grossly normal.

Impression: Infiltrative, non-enhancing left frontal lobe white matter lesion, suspicious for a low-grade astrocytoma. Correlation with advanced perfusion or MR spectroscopy is recommended for further evaluation.

Fetal MRI at 32 weeks gestation reveals normal structural development. Reassuring brain development is seen with distinct superior temporal sulci and age-appropriate gyration. The lateral ventricles are symmetric with an atrial width of 5.9 mm. Normal fetal chest, cardiac position, and abdominal anatomy are confirmed.

Impression: Unremarkable fetal MRI showing appropriate structural development and healthy intracranial structures at 32 weeks gestation.

The study demonstrates marked dilation of the left ventricle with an end-diastolic volume index of 135 mL/m² and severe global hypokinesis. The left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) is severely reduced at 22%. Mid-wall linear late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) is observed in the mid-septal segment, preserving the subendocardium. The right ventricle is also mildly dilated with a depressed ejection fraction of 38%.

Impression: Severe dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM) with biventricular involvement. The mid-wall linear late gadolinium enhancement is characteristic of a non-ischemic etiology.

The study was conducted to evaluate atypical chest discomfort. The anatomy of the heart is unremarkable, with normal chamber dimensions and normal myocardial thickness. Left ventricular wall motion is symmetric throughout. There is no evidence of inducible ischemia, myocardial edema, or late gadolinium enhancement.

Impression: Completely normal cardiac MRI. There is excellent global biventricular systolic function with a left ventricular ejection fraction of 64%.

MR of the brain demonstrates a well-circumscribed, extra-axial, dural-based mass along the right parasagittal frontoparietal region measuring approximately 2.8 x 2.5 cm. The mass is isointense to gray matter on T1 and T2 sequences, demonstrates intense homogeneous enhancement post-contrast, and exhibits a classic dural tail sign. There is mild localized compression of the adjacent cortex.

Impression: Features are highly characteristic of a benign parasagittal meningioma. Mild compression of the adjacent cerebral cortex is noted without associated vasogenic edema.

Fetal MRI evaluated at 22 weeks gestation reveals normal fetal brain development. Opercularization of the sylvian fissure is progressing normally for this gestational age. The ventricular system is symmetric and normal in size, with atrial measurements of 5.4 mm on the left and 5.6 mm on the right. The corpus callosum and cerebellar structures are fully intact and show no signs of deformity.

The chest, abdominal cavity, and extremities are structurally normal. Impression: Normal fetal MRI study demonstrating age-appropriate neurodevelopment and somatic structures at 22 weeks gestation.

Brain MRI was performed using multiplanar, multisequence protocols. There is no evidence of acute infarction, intracranial hemorrhage, or abnormal mass lesion. The ventricles and sulci are symmetric and unremarkable for the patient's age. The basal ganglia and brainstem structures show normal signal characteristics, and the major cerebral vascular flow voids are preserved.

Impression: Normal magnetic resonance imaging of the brain. No structural or vascular abnormalities identified to account for the patient's clinical presentation of chronic tension-type headaches.

There is a crescent-shaped extra-axial fluid collection along the left frontoparietal hemisphere measuring up to 1.4 cm in maximal width. This collection displays mixed signal intensity, with T1 hyperintensity and T2 hypointensity, indicating a subacute-on-chronic subdural hematoma. There is resulting mass effect with compression of the left cerebral sulci and a 4 mm midline shift to the right.

Impression: Subacute-on-chronic left frontoparietal subdural hematoma with moderate mass effect and midline shift. Close clinical observation and neurosurgical consultation are recommended.

Multiplanar, multisequence brain MRI shows normal brain parenchyma without mass effect, abnormal signal, or hemorrhage. Ventricles and sulci are normal for age. Basal ganglia and brainstem are unremarkable.

Impression: Unremarkable MRI of the brain. No structural, inflammatory, or vascular abnormalities are identified.

Cardiac MRI demonstrates normal biventricular dimensions with a mildly reduced left ventricular ejection fraction of 51%. T2-weighted STIR sequences reveal patchy regions of high signal intensity in the subepicardial region of the lateral and basal-lateral walls, indicating localized myocardial edema. Myocardial T1 mapping values are elevated at 1280 ms.

Late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) imaging confirms patchy, non-ischemic subepicardial enhancement in the corresponding lateral wall segments, satisfying the revised Lake Louise criteria. Impression: Acute myocarditis with active myocardial edema and subepicardial necrosis/fibrosis in the lateral wall segments.

Cardiac MRI demonstrates prominent bileaflet mitral valve prolapse (MVP), with both leaflets displacing > 2 mm past the mitral annulus during systole. This is associated with a severe eccentric regurgitant jet that fills a significantly dilated left atrium (LAVi 54 mL/m²). Left ventricular volumes are dilated, with a compensatory elevated ejection fraction of 66%.

Impression: Severe mitral valve regurgitation secondary to bileaflet mitral valve prolapse, resulting in moderate left atrial and left ventricular dilation. Left ventricular function is hyperdynamic.

Cardiac MRI shows severe asymmetric septal hypertrophy, with the maximal septal wall thickness measuring 22 mm. There is systolic anterior motion (SAM) of the anterior mitral valve leaflet, resulting in a dynamic left ventricular outflow tract (LVOT) obstruction and moderate mitral regurgitation. Left ventricular ejection fraction is hyperdynamic at 75%. Late gadolinium enhancement imaging shows patchy mid-myocardial hyperenhancement at the RV-LV insertion points, typical for hypertrophic cardiomyopathy.

Impression: Findings strongly characteristic of hypertrophic obstructive cardiomyopathy (HOCM) with hyperdynamic LV function and patchy focal fibrosis.

MR brain imaging reveals a localized nidus of tightly packed, serpiginous vascular flow voids centered in the left parieto-occipital region, measuring 3.1 x 2.4 cm. Multiple prominent feeding arteries from the left middle and posterior cerebral arteries are noted, along with dilated draining veins extending into the superior sagittal sinus. No surrounding intraparenchymal hemorrhage or significant edema is demonstrated.

Impression: Intracranial arteriovenous malformation (AVM) in the left parieto-occipital lobe without evidence of acute rupture. Further evaluation with catheter angiography is recommended for definitive treatment planning.

Fetal MRI at 34 weeks gestation demonstrates bilaterally enlarged, T2-hypointense kidneys that fill the fetal abdomen, which is significantly distended. Numerous tiny microcysts are suspected, characteristic of autosomal recessive polycystic kidney disease (ARPKD). Severe oligohydramnios is present, causing compression of the fetal thorax.

The fetal brain demonstrates mature sulcation for 34 weeks. The lateral ventricles are normal, measuring 6.5 mm. Impression: Bilaterally enlarged kidneys with severe oligohydramnios, highly consistent with infantile polycystic kidney disease (ARPKD).

Brain MRI reveals multiple well-defined, ovoid T2/FLAIR hyperintense lesions distributed throughout the periventricular, juxtacortical, and infratentorial white matter. Several lesions are oriented perpendicular to the lateral ventricles, consistent with Dawson's fingers. Following gadolinium administration, two active lesions in the left parietal lobe show nodular contrast enhancement.

Impression: Demyelinating disease of the central nervous system, demonstrating dissemination in both space and time, highly indicative of active Multiple Sclerosis.

Cardiac MRI shows diffuse, symmetric thickening of the left ventricular myocardium (interventricular septum measuring 16 mm, lateral wall 15 mm). There is also diffuse thickening of the interatrial septum and the right ventricular free wall. Late gadolinium enhancement imaging demonstrates a characteristic pattern of diffuse, subendocardial enhancement involving both ventricles, accompanied by suboptimal myocardial nulling, strongly suggestive of an infiltrative process. Left ventricular ejection fraction is mildly reduced at 44%.

Impression: Findings are classic for cardiac amyloidosis, showing diffuse concentric biventricular thickening, abnormal myocardial nulling kinetics, and extensive subendocardial late gadolinium enhancement.

MR imaging of the brain demonstrates marked ventriculomegaly involving the lateral and third ventricles, which is disproportionate to the degree of cerebral cortical sulcal atrophy. Prominent narrowing of the sulci at the high convexities and parasagittal regions is visualized, along with enlargement of the sylvian fissures (DESH sign). There is also a prominent flow void in the aqueduct of Sylvius on T2-weighted sequences.

Impression: Ventriculomegaly out of proportion to sulcal enlargement, highly suggestive of normal pressure hydrocephalus (NPH) in the appropriate clinical context. Clinical correlation with the triad of gait disturbance, cognitive decline, and urinary incontinence is recommended.

Cardiac MRI reveals a moderate-to-large circumferential pericardial effusion, measuring up to 18 mm adjacent to the right atrium and 15 mm adjacent to the left ventricular apex. There is evidence of early diastolic collapse of the right atrium, suggesting elevated intrapericardial pressures and impending hemodynamic compromise. The pericardium itself appears mildly thickened and demonstrates intense late gadolinium enhancement, suggestive of active pericarditis. Biventricular chamber sizes and systolic function are otherwise preserved, with a left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) of 58%.

Impression: Moderate-to-large circumferential pericardial effusion with signs suggestive of early tamponade physiology (diastolic right atrial collapse). Features also suggest active pericarditis with thickened, enhancing pericardium.

Fetal MRI at 36 weeks gestation demonstrates completely normal anatomy. There is extensive, age-appropriate sulcation and gyral patterning across both cerebral hemispheres. The lateral ventricles are completely symmetric with a normal atrial measurement of 6.8 mm.

The posterior fossa structures, including the cerebellum and brainstem, are fully developed. The thoracic and abdominal structures are unremarkable. Impression: Unremarkable fetal MRI demonstrating completely normal structural development and age-appropriate brain maturation.

Cardiac MRI demonstrates marked, asymmetric hypertrophy of the left ventricle, predominantly involving the anterior and posterior interventricular septum. The maximal septal wall thickness measures 24 mm in the basal to mid-ventricular regions. There is dynamic left ventricular outflow tract (LVOT) obstruction during systole, associated with systolic anterior motion (SAM) of the anterior mitral valve leaflet. Late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) imaging reveals patchy, mid-wall hyperenhancement at the superior and inferior RV insertion points.

Impression: Phenotypic features highly consistent with obstructive Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy (HCM). Notable septal hypertrophy, systolic anterior motion of the mitral valve, and classic LGE at the RV insertion points.

Cardiac MRI shows a bicuspid aortic valve (fusion of the right and left coronary cusps) with calcification and severely restricted systolic excursion. Planimetric measurement of the aortic valve area is restricted at 0.9 cm². Post-stenotic dilation of the ascending aorta is present, measuring 4.4 cm. Mild concentric hypertrophy of the left ventricle is noted.

Left ventricular systolic function remains preserved with an ejection fraction of 55%. Impression: Severe aortic stenosis secondary to a bicuspid aortic valve, with mild compensatory left ventricular concentric hypertrophy and ascending aortic ectasia.

The intracranial brain structures are intact and demonstrate normal morphology. No focal lesions, abnormal enhancement, or restricted diffusion are observed. The ventricular system, basal cisterns, and major vascular flow voids are unremarkable.

Impression: Normal MR imaging of the brain. No structural, neoplastic, or inflammatory lesions identified to account for the patient's complaints of recurring tension headaches.

Evaluation of the interatrial septum demonstrates a large secundum-type atrial septal defect (ASD) measuring approximately 18 mm in diameter. Real-time phase-contrast velocity mapping demonstrates a significant left-to-right shunt with a Qp:Qs ratio calculated at 1.8. Moderate right ventricular dilation is present with flattening of the interventricular septum during diastole, indicating right ventricular volume overload.

The right ventricular ejection fraction remains preserved at 52%. Impression: Secundum atrial septal defect with a significant left-to-right shunt and signs of right ventricular volume overload. No pulmonary arterial hypertension is suspected on current imaging.

Fetal MRI at 33 weeks gestation shows Dandy-Walker variant (cerebellar vermian hypoplasia). There is mild hypoplasia of the inferior cerebellar vermis with a moderately enlarged keyhole-shaped fourth ventricle communicating with the cisterna magna. The posterior fossa size is normal, and there is no significant elevation of the torcula. Supratentorial brain anatomy shows normal ventricular sizes (atrium 6.8 mm) and normal sulcation.

Remaining fetal anatomy is normal. Impression: Cerebellar vermian hypoplasia (Dandy-Walker variant) with normal posterior fossa size and no supratentorial abnormalities.

The study demonstrates marked dilation of the right ventricle with regional wall motion abnormalities, including dyskinesis and aneurysm formation at the right ventricular outflow tract and inferior wall. The right ventricular ejection fraction is severely reduced at 31%, whereas left ventricular size and function are preserved (LVEF 59%). Late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) imaging demonstrates transmural-like hyperenhancement in the RV free wall, suggesting fibrofatty replacement.

Impression: Findings strongly meet the diagnostic criteria for Arrhythmogenic Right Ventricular Cardiomyopathy (ARVC), including severe RV dilation, regional dyskinesis, and RV free wall fibrosis.

MRI brain demonstrates a non-enhancing, ill-defined intra-axial lesion in the left frontal lobe. The lesion is hyperintense on T2 and FLAIR, and hypointense on T1-weighted images. There is minimal surrounding vasogenic edema and no restricted diffusion or hemorrhagic components. Ventricular size is normal.

Impression: Non-enhancing infiltrative left frontal lobe mass, highly suggestive of a low-grade astrocytoma. Recommend further evaluation with MR spectroscopy and neurosurgical biopsy.

Cardiac MRI reveals asymmetric septal hypertrophy, most pronounced at the basal and mid-ventricular levels, measuring up to 2.2 cm. There is associated systolic anterior motion (SAM) of the anterior mitral valve leaflet, resulting in dynamic left ventricular outflow tract (LVOT) obstruction and moderate mitral regurgitation. Late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) imaging demonstrates focal patchy areas of hyperenhancement at the right ventricular insertion points, typical of hypertrophic cardiomyopathy.

Impression: Hypertrophic obstructive cardiomyopathy (HOCM) with severe asymmetric septal hypertrophy, dynamic LVOT obstruction, and characteristic patchy insertion-point LGE. Left ventricular ejection fraction is hyperdynamic at 74%.

Cardiac MRI shows subendocardial to transmural late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) in the mid-to-apical anterior and anteroseptal walls of the left ventricle, conforming to a left anterior descending artery territory myocardial infarction. There is associated focal thinning and severe hypokinesia in these segments. Left ventricular ejection fraction is reduced at 38% with a dilated left ventricle (EDV of 210 mL).

Impression: Evidence of a prior transmural myocardial infarction in the LAD territory with associated severe regional wall motion abnormalities and moderately reduced left ventricular systolic function.

Brain MRI with susceptibility-weighted imaging (SWI) demonstrates curvilinear susceptibility artifacts within the basal cisterns, sylvian fissures, and cerebral sulci, consistent with acute subarachnoid hemorrhage. No focal mass is seen, but there is mild widening of the temporal horns of the lateral ventricles suggesting early hydrocephalus.

Impression: Acute subarachnoid hemorrhage within the basal cisterns and sylvian fissures. Urgent CT angiogram or MR angiogram of the head is recommended to evaluate for intracranial aneurysm rupture.

Cardiac MRI demonstrates normal cardiac chamber dimensions and preserved biventricular systolic function. Left ventricular end-diastolic volume is 125 mL and the left ventricular ejection fraction is 64% with normal global and regional wall motion. The right ventricle is also normal in size and function with an ejection fraction of 58%. Myocardial perfusion and late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) imaging show no focal enhancement or fibrosis.

Impression: Completely normal cardiac MRI. No evidence of myocardial ischemia, scarring, or cardiomyopathy. Normal chamber sizes and biventricular function.

Cardiac MRI shows normal cardiac chambers size, wall thickness, and function. The left ventricular end-diastolic volume (LVEDV) is 142 mL, and the left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) is calculated at 62%, indicating excellent systolic function. The right ventricle is also normal in size and function with an ejection fraction of 56%. There is no evidence of myocardial edema on T2-weighted imaging or late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) to suggest myocardial scarring or fibrosis.

Impression: Unremarkable cardiac MRI. Normal biventricular size and systolic function with no myocardial scarring, fibrosis, or perfusion defects.

Cardiac MRI demonstrates normal left and right ventricular chamber volumes with no regional wall motion abnormalities. Left ventricular ejection fraction is calculated at 58% and right ventricular ejection fraction is 53%, representing preserved systolic function. No late gadolinium enhancement is noted within the left or right ventricular walls, and there is no evidence of ischemic scarring, amyloidosis, or pericardial effusion.

Impression: Normal cardiac MRI study. Normal biventricular volumes and function for age, with no evidence of myocardial scar or active inflammatory process.

Sagittal and coronal T1-weighted images obtained through the sella turcica demonstrate a well-defined hypo-enhancing lesion within the right lateral aspect of the pituitary gland, measuring 8 x 6 mm. There is mild remodeling of the sellar floor on the right, but no significant deviation of the pituitary stalk or compression of the optic chiasm.

Impression: Microadenoma of the pituitary gland, measuring 8 mm. No extension into the suprasellar space or cavernous sinuses.

Cardiac MRI demonstrates normal anatomy. Left ventricular ejection fraction is calculated at 60% and right ventricular ejection fraction at 56%. There is no evidence of chamber enlargement, hypertrophy, or regional hypokinesis. Contrast-enhanced sequences show zero late gadolinium enhancement. Mitral, aortic, and tricuspid valve excursions are completely normal.

Impression: Normal cardiac MRI study. No structural or functional cardiac abnormalities identified.

Cardiac MRI demonstrates normal cardiac chambers without evidence of hypertrophy, dilation, or congenital anomalies. Left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) is calculated at 60%, and right ventricular ejection fraction (RVEF) is 57%. No regional wall motion abnormalities are observed, and flow quantification across the pulmonary and aortic valves is physiological. Multiplanar LGE imaging demonstrates no focal myocardial fibrosis or scarring.

Impression: Unremarkable cardiac MRI. Normal biventricular volume and function with no signs of cardiomyopathy, myocardial edema, or late gadolinium enhancement.

Magnetic resonance imaging of the brain was performed using multiplanar, multisequence protocols. No acute intracranial pathology is identified. The cerebral ventricles, sulci, and cisterns are normal in caliber and configuration. There is no evidence of intracranial hemorrhage, infarct, or suspicious parenchymal or extra-axial enhancement.

Impression: Normal MR of the brain. No objective structural etiology found to account for patient's complaints of vertigo or dizziness.

Cardiac magnetic resonance imaging was performed to evaluate for a suspected cardiac source of embolus. Standard multiplanar cine and tissue characterization sequences reveal normal cardiac chamber dimensions and wall thicknesses. The left ventricular ejection fraction is 62%, and the right ventricular ejection fraction is 58%, without regional wall motion abnormalities or intra-cavitary thrombi. Late gadolinium enhancement and perfusion sequences are entirely normal.

Impression: Normal cardiac MRI with no evidence of myocardial infarction, scar, or intracardiac thrombus to explain the patient's neurological symptoms.

Cardiac MRI demonstrates marked dilatation and dysfunction of the right ventricle, with an end-diastolic volume index of 115 mL/m² and a depressed right ventricular ejection fraction (RVEF) of 34%. Regional wall motion evaluation reveals localized aneurysmal outpouchings and dyskinesis within the right ventricular outflow tract (RVOT) and inferior wall. Highly localized fatty infiltration and mid-wall fibrosis are suspected on delayed enhancement images.

Impression: Features are highly characteristic of arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy (ARVC) based on regional RV dyskinesis, severe RV dilation, and systolic dysfunction. Left ventricular size and ejection fraction (60%) remain normal.

Cardiovascular magnetic resonance imaging shows normal left ventricular end-diastolic (112 mL) and end-systolic volumes. Myocardial wall thickness is uniform throughout, with no evidence of hypertrophy. Left ventricular ejection fraction is normal at 63%. Right ventricular volumes, wall motion, and systolic function (RVEF 57%) are preserved. Valves demonstrate normal excursions without flow acceleration.

Myocardial perfusion is uniform during stress, and no late gadolinium enhancement is noted. Impression: Normal cardiovascular MRI with normal biventricular size and function, and no evidence of myocardial scar or ischemia.

Fetal MRI at 29 weeks gestation. The left fetal kidney is enlarged and replaced by multiple, variable-sized, non-communicating cysts. No normal renal parenchyma is identified on the left. The right kidney appears structurally normal with normal signal intensity. The amniotic fluid volume is within normal limits.

The fetal brain anatomy, sulcation, and ventricular atria (6.3 mm) are normal. Impression: Left multicystic dysplastic kidney (MCDK) with a normal contralateral right kidney and normal amniotic fluid volume.

Cardiac MRI reveals patchy epicardial and mid-wall late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) localized to the lateral and inferolateral free wall. T2-weighted imaging and T2 mapping show corresponding elevated signal intensity in these regions, consistent with active myocardial edema. Left ventricular ejection fraction is preserved at 55%.

Impression: Findings satisfy the updated Lake Louise Criteria for acute myocarditis, demonstrating both active myocardial edema and non-ischemic pattern scar/injury in the lateral wall.

Fetal MRI at 33 weeks gestation shows a large right-sided congenital diaphragmatic hernia. There is herniation of the right lobe of the liver and small bowel loops into the right chest cavity, causing leftward mediastinal shift and compression of the cardiac chambers. The left lung is compressed but visible. Estimated fetal lung volume is below average for 33 weeks.

Impression: Large right-sided congenital diaphragmatic hernia with liver herniation. High risk of severe pulmonary hypoplasia requiring specialized neonatal critical care.

Fetal MRI at 20 weeks gestation shows completely normal maternal and fetal anatomy. The fetal brain exhibits symmetric lateral ventricles measuring 5.5 mm. Sulcation and migrational status are appropriate for 20 weeks gestation. The corpus callosum and cerebellar structures are completely intact. Fetal movement is well-demonstrated, and amniotic fluid volume is completely normal.

The fetal chest, abdominal organs, spine, and bladder are fully developed and normal in appearance. Impression: Normal fetal MRI study at 20 weeks gestation.

Fetal MRI at 22 weeks gestation demonstrates a mildly hypoplastic cerebellar vermis and an enlarged posterior fossa fluid collection communicating with the fourth ventricle, characteristic of a Dandy-Walker variant. Cortical sulcation is normal for gestational age. The lateral ventricles are at the upper limits of normal, with the atrium measuring 9.5 mm.

Impression: Dandy-Walker variant with mild ventriculomegaly, requiring careful prenatal genetic counseling and postnatal follow-up.

Fetal MRI at 25 weeks gestation. There is a large left-sided congenital diaphragmatic hernia (Bochdalek type). The stomach, small bowel loops, and a portion of the left lobe of the liver have herniated into the left hemithorax. This has resulted in a severe rightward mediastinal shift and compression of the developing lungs. The observed-to-expected total fetal lung volume is calculated at 38%, indicating severe pulmonary hypoplasia.

The fetal brain anatomy and sulcation are normal, and ventricular atrial widths measure 6.0 mm. Impression: Large left-sided congenital diaphragmatic hernia with significant mediastinal shift and severe pulmonary hypoplasia.

Fetal MRI at 33 weeks gestation reveals hypoplasia of the inferior cerebellar vermis with a small keyhole-like cleft in the posterior fossa. The overall size of the posterior fossa is not significantly enlarged, and the tentorium is normally positioned, findings consistent with a Dandy-Walker variant. The lateral ventricles are stable, with the atrium measuring 9.0 mm. Sulcation is mature and appropriate for 33 weeks.

No other intracranial or extracranial anomalies are identified. Impression: Hypoplasia of the inferior cerebellar vermis, consistent with a Dandy-Walker variant/isolated vermian hypoplasia.

MR of the brain shows a well-circumscribed, extra-axial, dural-based mass along the right frontal convexity. The mass measures approximately 2.8 x 2.4 x 2.2 cm and is isointense to gray matter on both T1- and T2-weighted sequences, with intense, homogeneous enhancement following contrast administration. A distinct 'dural tail' sign is visualized. There is mild localized mass effect on the adjacent frontal cortex, but no significant edema.

Impression: Findings are highly suggestive of a benign meningioma of the right frontal convexity. No acute mass effect or midline shift is observed; routine follow-up or neurosurgical consultation is recommended.

Fetal MRI at 23 weeks gestation reveals a mild form of posterior fossa anomaly, consistent with a Dandy-Walker variant. There is mild hypoplasia of the inferior cerebellar vermis, accompanied by an enlarged cisterna magna measuring 12.5 mm, which communicates with the posterior fossa. The lateral ventricles are normal, with atrial measurements of 6.5 mm bilaterally. No supratentorial abnormalities are present.

Impression: Dandy-Walker variant (megacisterna magna with mild inferior vermian hypoplasia). Supratentorial brain anatomy is normal.

MR imaging of the brain demonstrates a large, heterogeneous, ring-enhancing mass centered within the right temporal lobe. The lesion measures approximately 4.2 x 3.8 x 3.5 cm and is surrounded by extensive T2/FLAIR hyperintensity consistent with severe vasogenic edema. This complex elicits prominent mass effect, compressing the temporal horn of the right lateral ventricle and producing approximately 7 mm of leftward midline shift. Magnetic resonance spectroscopy reveals elevated choline-to-creatine and reduced NAA peaks within the solid components.

Impression: Aggressive, ring-enhancing right temporal lobe mass with significant mass effect and midline shift. The imaging features are highly characteristic of a high-grade glial neoplasm, such as glioblastoma, though a solitary metastatic lesion remains in the differential diagnosis. Urgent neurosurgical consultation is recommended.

Magnetic resonance evaluation of the heart reveals normal cardiac volumes and wall thicknesses. Left ventricular ejection fraction is 61% and right ventricular ejection fraction is 56%. No segmental wall motion abnormalities are present. Pre- and post-contrast sequences show no areas of delayed enhancement or signal abnormalities to suggest focal scar or inflammation.

Impression: Normal cardiac MRI with normal chamber dimensions, preserved biventricular systolic function, and no evidence of myocardial injury or scar.

Cardiac MRI shows normal chamber dimensions and preserved wall thickness. Left ventricular ejection fraction is 60%, and right ventricular ejection fraction is 55%. SSFP cine imaging shows no regional wall motion abnormalities. T2 mapping and late gadolinium enhancement are negative for inflammation, scar, or infiltrative process.

Impression: Unremarkable cardiac MRI with normal biventricular dimensions, preserved systolic function, and no evidence of myocardial scarring or acute inflammation.

MRI reveals significant thickening and prolapse of the posterior leaflet (P2 segment) of the mitral valve into the left atrium during systole. Phase-contrast flow imaging demonstrates a severe, eccentric, anteriorly-directed regurgitant jet. There is marked dilation of the left atrium with an indexed volume of 58 mL/m². Left ventricular size is mildly increased with a hyperdynamic ejection fraction of 64%.

Impression: Severe mitral regurgitation secondary to myxomatous mitral valve disease and posterior leaflet prolapse, resulting in significant left atrial dilation and mild left ventricular volume overload.

Fetal MRI at 30 weeks gestation demonstrates completely normal structural development. Sylvian fissure opercularization and parieto-occipital and calcarine sulcus patterns are completely appropriate for 30 weeks. The lateral ventricles are symmetric, with atrial measurements of 6.3 mm bilaterally.

The corpus callosum is fully formed. Visualized spinal, thoracic, and abdominal organs are within normal limits. Impression: Normal fetal brain MRI showing age-appropriate brain development and normal cranial biometry.

Fetal MRI at 25 weeks gestation demonstrates age-appropriate development. The brain shows emerging central and parieto-occipital sulci, which is normal for 25 weeks. The lateral ventricles are completely normal and measure 5.6 mm at the atrium. The thoracic and abdominal organs, as well as the extremities, are grossly normal within the limits of resolution.

Impression: Normal fetal MRI at 25 weeks gestation. No anomalies of the central nervous system or body are visualized.

This adult patient with a history of repaired Tetralogy of Fallot demonstrates significant dilatation of the right ventricular outflow tract (RVOT) and the main pulmonary artery. Severe pulmonary regurgitation is noted on phase-contrast sequences, with a regurgitant fraction calculated at 48%. There is severe dilation of the right ventricle, with an end-diastolic volume index of 160 mL/m2. Right ventricular ejection fraction is mildly reduced at 43%.

Impression: Status post remote surgical repair of Tetralogy of Fallot. Findings show severe pulmonary regurgitation causing significant right ventricular volume overload and progressive RV dysfunction.

Fetal MRI at 24 weeks gestation reveals bilateral, severely enlarged, multicystic kidneys. Both kidneys are replaced by numerous non-communicating cysts of varying sizes, with virtually no normal-appearing renal parenchyma visible. There is severe oligohydramnios, which limits optimal visualization of the fetal limbs, although the fetal spine appears intact. The urinary bladder is not visualized, indicating minimal to no fetal urine production.

Impression: Bilateral multicystic dysplastic kidney disease with severe oligohydramnios. This constellation of findings carries a poor prognosis due to associated pulmonary hypoplasia.

Brain MRI demonstrates marked enlargement of the lateral, third, and fourth ventricles. Crucially, this ventriculomegaly is disproportionate to the mild-to-moderate degree of cerebral cortical sulcal atrophy. Periventricular T2 hyperintensity is present, suggesting transependymal CSF migration. Temporal horns are notably dilated.

Impression: Ventriculomegaly disproportionate to atrophy, highly suggestive of normal pressure hydrocephalus (NPH) in this clinical context. Recommend correlation with clinical triad of gait instability, cognitive decline, and urinary urgency.

High-resolution 3D MR angiography demonstrates focal, severe narrowing of the proximal descending thoracic aorta, just distal to the origin of the left subclavian artery, with an internal lumen diameter of 7 mm. Marked post-stenotic dilation is observed, alongside prominent collateral pathways involving the internal mammary and intercostal arteries. The left ventricle demonstrates mild concentric hypertrophy.

Impression: Severe focal coarctation of the aorta with prominent collateral circulation and secondary mild concentric left ventricular hypertrophy. Left ventricular function is normal (LVEF 58%).

A large, crescent-shaped extra-axial fluid collection is demonstrated over the right cerebral hemisphere, measuring up to 1.8 cm in thickness. The collection exhibits heterogeneous signal intensity, indicating mixed chronic and subacute components. Mass effect is evident, with compression of the right lateral ventricle, effacement of adjacent sulci, and 8 mm of leftward midline shift.

Impression: Large, chronic-on-subacute right subdural hematoma causing significant mass effect and midline shift. Prompt neurosurgical evaluation is recommended.

Cardiac MRI shows marked thickening of the pericardium measuring up to 6 mm, with diffuse enhancement post-contrast injection. There is a moderate, simple circumferential pericardial effusion without evidence of loculation. Real-time cine imaging demonstrates respiratory-dependent ventricular septal bounce, suggestive of constrictive physiology.

Impression: Constrictive pericarditis with active pericardial inflammation and a moderate pericardial effusion. Right and left ventricular systolic function is preserved.

MR of the brain demonstrates normal ventricular size and sulcation for the patient's age. No acute infarct, hemorrhage, or mass lesion is identified. The major intracranial flow voids are preserved, and the paranasal sinuses are clear.

Impression: Normal MRI of the brain. No structural abnormality to explain the patient's headaches.

Fetal MRI at 32 weeks gestation shows excellent development of the fetal brain. The primary and secondary sulci, including the central, precentral, and postcentral sulci, are well-formed, demonstrating appropriate maturation for 32 weeks. The lateral ventricles are highly symmetric, with the atrial width measuring 5.9 mm. The corpus callosum is fully formed, showing normal thickness of the rostrum, genu, body, and splenium. No extra-axial fluid collections or facial clefts are visualized.

Impression: Normal fetal MRI at 32 weeks gestation, showcasing normal sulcation and age-appropriate brain development.

Fetal MRI at 36 weeks gestation shows excellent detail of late-gestation anatomy. The cerebral hemispheres demonstrate mature operculization and deep, complex sulcation patterns. The lateral ventricles are completely normal, with the atrium measuring 5.2 mm. The corpus callosum is thick and fully formed, and the posterior fossa demonstrates no abnormal fluid collections.

The fetal chest demonstrates well-inflated lungs with normal high-signal intensity. Abdominal organs are structurally normal with a fluid-filled stomach and bladder. Impression: Normal fetal MRI study at 36 weeks showing advanced fetal brain maturation and normal visceral anatomy.

There is a well-defined zone of restricted diffusion in the left middle cerebral artery territory, specifically involving the left insula and basal ganglia, consistent with acute ischemic stroke. High signal on DWI corresponds to low signal on ADC maps. No intracranial hemorrhage is demonstrated on susceptibility-weighted sequences.

Impression: Acute left MCA territory ischemic infarct with involvement of the basal ganglia and insula. No evidence of hemorrhagic transformation.

MRI dedicated to the sella turcica demonstrates a well-circumscribed, solid mass centered within the pituitary fossa measuring 2.1 x 1.8 x 1.7 cm. The mass extends superiorly out of the sella, causing displacement and compression of the optic chiasm. The lesion is relatively isointense on T1 and demonstrates heterogeneous contrast enhancement. The infundibulum is deviated to the left.

Impression: Pituitary macroadenoma with suprasellar extension and optic chiasm compression. Endocrinological and neurosurgical workups, as well as formal visual field testing, are highly recommended.

Brain MRI was performed utilizing multiplanar, multisequence protocols. The cerebral cortex, white matter, and deep grey matter nuclei are normal. There are no focal lesions, acute ischemia, hemorrhage, or abnormal enhancements. The ventricles and extra-axial fluid spaces are normal in caliber. Visualized orbits, paranasal sinuses, and mastoid air cells are unremarkable.

Impression: Unremarkable MRI of the brain. No structural, inflammatory, or vascular pathology identified.

Fetal MRI at 30 weeks gestation demonstrates a large multicystic dysplastic left kidney (MCDK) containing multiple non-communicating cysts of varying sizes. The right kidney is compensatory hypertrophied but morphologically normal. The amniotic fluid volume is within normal limits. The brain demonstrates normal, age-appropriate sulcation with a ventricular atrial width of 6.3 mm.

Impression: Left multicystic dysplastic kidney (MCDK) with a normal right kidney and normal amniotic fluid volume. Good prognosis given the presence of a healthy, functioning contralateral kidney.

MR imaging of the brain reveals no abnormal signal intensity in the cerebral hemispheres, brainstem, or cerebellum. The ventricles and cisterns are normal in caliber. No areas of restricted diffusion or abnormal contrast enhancement are seen. Visually, the major intracranial vessels are patent.

Impression: Normal brain MRI. No evidence of neoplasm, ischemic stroke, or other intracranial abnormalities.

MRI shows a non-enhancing, ill-defined T2/FLAIR hyperintense lesion within the left frontal lobe cortex and subcortical white matter, measuring approximately 3.1 x 2.7 cm. The lesion does not show restricted diffusion or significant mass effect. No associated hemorrhage or necrosis is identified.

Impression: Ill-defined, non-enhancing T2/FLAIR hyperintense lesion in the left frontal lobe, highly suspicious for a low-grade glioma (e.g., diffuse astrocytoma). Recommend follow-up or advanced imaging/biopsy.

Cardiac MRI demonstrates normal left ventricular chamber size and wall thickness. Left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) is calculated at 62%, and right ventricular ejection fraction (RVEF) is 58%, both well within normal limits. There is no evidence of regional wall motion abnormalities, myocardial edema on T2-weighted imaging, or focal myocardial scar/fibrosis on late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) imaging. Cardiac valves appear structurally normal with no hemodynamically significant stenosis or regurgitation.

Impression: Normal cardiac MRI study. No evidence of myocardial ischemia, infarction, cardiomyopathy, or active myocarditis.

Cardiac magnetic resonance imaging demonstrates normal anatomical and functional parameters of both ventricles. Left ventricular ejection fraction is computed at 61% and right ventricular ejection fraction is 54%. Myocardial perfusion imaging is uniform under rest conditions. Late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) imaging is negative, with no evidence of replacement fibrosis, inflammatory changes, or acute ischemic injury.

Impression: Normal cardiac MRI study showing no structural, regional kinetic, or delayed enhancement abnormalities. No evidence of myocardial dysfunction or structural disease.

MRI demonstrates severe asymmetric hypertrophy of the left ventricle, localized predominantly within the anterior interventricular septum where the maximum wall thickness measures 21 mm. Left ventricular systolic function is hyperdynamic with an ejection fraction (LVEF) of 72%. Late gadolinium enhancement imaging reveals patchy mid-myocardial enhancement localized at the right ventricular insertion points, consistent with interstitial fibrosis.

Impression: Classic morphological features of hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) with severe asymmetric septal hypertrophy. Hyperdynamic left ventricular systolic function with dynamic outflow tract narrowing noted during peak systole.

Fetal MRI at 32 weeks gestation demonstrates a mild keyhole-shaped fluid collection in the posterior fossa. The cerebellar vermis is present but exhibits partial hypoplasia of the inferior aspect, with mild elevation of the fourth ventricle and a slightly enlarged cisterna magna measuring 11.5 mm. The cerebellar hemispheres are symmetric and normal in size. The lateral ventricles are within normal limits, with the atria measuring 6.5 mm. Cortical sulcation is appropriate for 32 weeks.

Impression: Dandy-Walker variant (partial vermian hypoplasia with enlarged posterior fossa CSF space). Supratentorial brain anatomy is normal for gestational age.

Fetal MRI at 28 weeks gestation demonstrates a Dandy-Walker variant. There is moderate hypoplasia of the inferior cerebellar vermis with mild elevation of the tentorium. There is open communication of the fourth ventricle with an enlarged cisterna magna, which measures 12.5 mm in anteroposterior diameter. The cerebellar hemispheres are normal in volume. The supratentorial brain shows normal cortical sulcation for 28 weeks, and the ventricular atria measure 7.2 mm.

No other structural abnormalities of the fetus are identified. Impression: Dandy-Walker variant with inferior vermian hypoplasia and enlarged cisterna magna. Supratentorial brain is normal.

MR angiogram and cine imaging of the thoracic aorta reveal a focal narrowing in the proximal descending aorta, located immediately distal to the origin of the left subclavian artery. The narrowest segment measures 8 mm in diameter, compared to a pre-coarctation aortic diameter of 18 mm. Prominent internal mammary and intercostal collateral vascular networks are visualized. Systolic flow acceleration with a diastolic tail is noted across the obstruction on phase-contrast imaging.

Impression: Congenital coarctation of the aorta with significant narrowing distal to the left subclavian artery and extensive collateral circulation. Concentric left ventricular remodeling is present.

MRI demonstrates peg-like herniation of the cerebellar tonsils approximately 8 mm below the level of the foramen magnum. There is mild crowding of the craniocervical junction. However, no cervical syrinx or hydromyelia is visualized on the sagittal screening survey of the cervical spine.

Impression: Chiari I malformation with 8 mm tonsillar ectopia, resulting in mild crowding of the craniocervical junction. No signs of associated syringomyelia are present on current sequences.

MRI of the brain demonstrates a crescentic, extra-axial fluid collection over the right cerebral hemisphere measuring up to 1.4 cm in maximal thickness. The collection is hyperintense on both T1 and T2-weighted sequences, indicating a subacute-to-chronic subdural hematoma containing extracellular methemoglobin. There is moderate mass effect, resulting in effacement of the adjacent right-sided sulci and a 5 mm leftward midline shift.

Impression: Subacute-to-chronic right subdural hematoma with moderate mass effect and a 5 mm leftward midline shift. Urgent neurosurgical evaluation is recommended.

Fetal MRI at 28 weeks gestation demonstrates bilateral symmetric ventriculomegaly. The left lateral ventricle atrium measures 14.8 mm and the right lateral ventricle atrium measures 14.2 mm, indicating moderate ventriculomegaly. There is mild thinning of the corpus callosum with preservation of its overall anatomical segments. Sulcation and gyration patterns are normal for 28 weeks.

No intraventricular hemorrhage, periventricular nodular heterotopia, or other intracranial lesions are identified. Impression: Moderate bilateral fetal ventriculomegaly. Recommend close follow-up with serial ultrasound or fetal MRI and pediatric neurosurgical consultation.

MRI of the brain was performed utilizing multiplanar, multisequence protocols. There are no focal areas of signal abnormality in the cerebral hemispheres, brainstem, or cerebellum. No restriction of diffusion or abnormal enhancement is noted. The ventricles and sulci are normal in size and appearance for the patient's age.

Impression: Unremarkable MRI of the brain. No acute pathology, demyelinating disease, or space-occupying lesion is identified to explain the patient's sensory disturbances.

MRI of the brain reveals prominent, confluent T2/FLAIR hyperintensities in the periventricular and deep white matter of both cerebral hemispheres. These changes are symmetric and represent chronic microvascular ischemic changes. There are also several small lacunar infarcts in the bilateral basal ganglia, but no acute infarcts or hemorrhages.

Impression: Moderate to severe chronic microvascular ischemic white matter disease. Multiple chronic lacunar infarctions, without acute intracranial event.

Fetal MRI at 32 weeks gestation shows normal, age-appropriate intracranial development. The cerebral cortex demonstrates progressive, expected sulcation, including deep parieto-occipital, calcarine, and central sulci. The lateral ventricles are completely normal, with an atrial diameter of 5.8 mm. The corpus callosum is well-defined and structurally intact. Spine and posterior fossa anatomy, including the vermis and cisterna magna, are normal.

Impression: Normal fetal MRI at 32 weeks gestation, showing appropriate brain maturation and no structural abnormalities.

Cardiac MRI demonstrates a small, restrictive perimembranous ventricular septal defect (VSD) measuring approximately 4 mm in diameter. Phase-contrast velocity mapping across the defect shows a high-velocity jet with a peak systolic gradient of 78 mmHg, indicating a restrictive shunt. Left ventricular and right ventricular dimensions and systolic function are completely normal (LVEF 62%, RVEF 55%).

Impression: Small, restrictive perimembranous ventricular septal defect with a high-velocity left-to-right shunt. No evidence of ventricular volume overload or pulmonary hypertension.

Cardiac MRI demonstrating asymmetric septal hypertrophy, with the maximal diastolic wall thickness of the interventricular septum measuring 22 mm. There is systolic anterior motion (SAM) of the anterior mitral valve leaflet, resulting in eccentric mitral regurgitation and dynamic left ventricular outflow tract (LVOT) obstruction. Late gadolinium enhancement imaging reveals focal, patchy enhancement at the right ventricular insertion points.

Impression: Classic findings of hypertrophic obstructive cardiomyopathy (HOCM) with significant septal hypertrophy, SAM of the mitral valve, and associated focal myocardial fibrosis at insertion points.

High-resolution MRI of the brain, including dedicated views of the internal auditory canals, was performed. Brain parenchyma, cerebellar hemispheres, and brain stem are normal in appearance. No cerebellopontine angle or intracanalicular abnormalities are seen, and the cochleovestibular nerves appear intact.

Impression: Normal MR examination of the brain and internal auditory canals. No structural abnormality found to account for unilateral tinnitus.

MR imaging of the brain was performed utilizing multiplanar, multisequence protocols. The brain parenchyma demonstrates normal signal intensity throughout, with no evidence of acute infarction, hemorrhage, or mass effect. The ventricles and sulci are within normal limits for the patient's age. The major intracranial vascular flow voids are preserved.

Impression: Normal MR imaging of the brain. No acute intracranial pathology, demyelinating process, or structural lesions identified.

Fetal MRI at 21 weeks gestation demonstrates a right-sided congenital diaphragmatic hernia, which is a less common variant. The right lobe of the liver, gallbladder, and loops of bowel are displaced into the right chest cavity. This herniation causes a significant leftward shift of the mediastinum and heart, compressing the left lung. The total fetal lung volume is severely reduced (calculated at 35% of predicted value for 21 weeks).

Fetal brain anatomy and spinal structures appear completely normal, with lateral ventricles measuring 6.2 mm. Impression: Right-sided congenital diaphragmatic hernia with intrathoracic liver and significant secondary pulmonary hypoplasia.

Cine sequences show mild global left ventricular systolic dysfunction with an LVEF of 47%. There is localized T2 hyperintensity in the basal-to-lateral and inferolateral epicardial regions, indicative of myocardial edema. Late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) imaging demonstrates prominent, patchy mid-wall to subepicardial hyperenhancement involving the same lateral and inferolateral segments.

Impression: Acute myocarditis with active myocardial edema and subepicardial injury, fulfilling the Lake Louise MRI criteria.

MR imaging of the brain with high-resolution trigeminal nerve sequences (CISS/FIESTA) demonstrates normal course and caliber of both trigeminal nerves. There is no evidence of microvascular compression, tumor, or demyelinating plaque in the cisternal segments or brainstem nuclei. The rest of the brain parenchyma is unremarkable.

Impression: Unremarkable brain and cranial nerve MRI. No structural abnormality, vascular compression, or plaque seen along the trigeminal pathways to explain atypical facial pain.

Fetal MRI at 33 weeks gestation shows normal, age-appropriate intracranial structures. The lateral ventricles measure 6.0 mm bilaterally, indicating normal size. Brain sulcation and cortical folding are advanced and highly appropriate. Normal chest and abdominal anatomy are visualised.

Impression: Completely normal 33-week fetal MRI. Structurally unremarkable central nervous system development.

Cardiac MRI shows excellent biventricular systolic function with normal wall thickness and chamber sizes. No wall motion abnormalities are identified. No late gadolinium enhancement is present to suggest focal myocardial scar or fibrosis. Visualized portion of the great vessels and heart valves appear normal.

Impression: Normal cardiac MRI study. Left ventricular ejection fraction is 63%, and right ventricular ejection fraction is 59%.

Fetal MRI evaluated at 26 weeks gestation demonstrates complete agenesis of the corpus callosum. The lateral ventricles show a characteristic colpocephalic configuration (teardrop appearance), with prominent dilation of the occipital horns. The right lateral ventricular atrium measures 11.2 mm and the left measures 10.9 mm. A radial arrangement of the sulci (sunburst sign) is noted on sagittal and parasagittal views.

No other associated intracranial anomalies, such as interhemispheric cysts or migration defects, are identified. The fetal posterior fossa is normal. Impression: Complete agenesis of the corpus callosum with associated mild colpocephaly.

Cardiac MR evaluation demonstrates a small defect in the membranous interventricular septum, measuring approximately 5 mm, consistent with a perimembranous ventricular septal defect (VSD). Phase-contrast flow analysis demonstrates a left-to-right shunt with a Qp:Qs ratio of 1.3:1. The left ventricle is minimally dilated with normal systolic function (LVEF 63%), while the right ventricle is normal in size and function.

Impression: Small perimembranous ventricular septal defect with a modest left-to-right shunt (Qp:Qs 1.3:1) and minimal left ventricular volume overload. No pulmonary hypertension is suggested.

Fetal MRI at 28 weeks gestation demonstrates bilateral ventriculomegaly. The right lateral ventricular atrium measures 13.5 mm and the left lateral ventricular atrium measures 14.1 mm. There is mild dangling of the choroid plexuses within both ventricles. Mild delay in cortical sulcation is noted for the stated gestational age, with the parieto-occipital fissure being less prominent than expected. The corpus callosum is present and normal in appearance. No intraventricular hemorrhage or periventricular nodular heterotopia is identified.

Impression: Bilateral moderate fetal ventriculomegaly at 28 weeks gestation, with mild delay in cortical sulcation. Follow-up imaging is recommended to monitor ventricular progression.

Cardiac MRI reveals severe, transmural late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) involving the mid-to-apical anterior wall, apex, and apical septum, which is thin and dyskinetic, forming a small apical aneurysm. Thrombus is not visualized within the aneurysm. The left ventricle is moderately dilated, and global left ventricular systolic function is severely depressed with an LVEF of 28%.

Impression: Transmural myocardial infarction in the LAD distribution with apical aneurysm formation and severely depressed left ventricular systolic function. No intraventricular thrombus identified.

MR imaging of the brain reveals an acute area of restricted diffusion in the right middle cerebral artery (MCA) territory, specifically involving the posterior limb of the internal capsule and adjacent lentiform nucleus. This area is hyperintense on DWI and hypointense on ADC, consistent with cytotoxic edema. Mild mass effect on the right lateral ventricle is noted, without midline shift.

Impression: Acute ischemic stroke within the right MCA distribution, involving the internal capsule and basal ganglia. There is no evidence of hemorrhagic transformation on susceptibility-weighted imaging.

The study was performed using multiplanar, multisequence brain MRI protocols. Brain parenchyma demonstrates symmetric signal intensity and normal morphology throughout. There is no evidence of intracranial mass, localized edema, acute ischemia, or extra-axial fluid collections. The cerebrospinal fluid pathways and ventricular system are normal. Cranial nerves demonstrate normal course and caliber.

Impression: Normal MR imaging of the brain. No structural, inflammatory, or vascular pathological abnormalities detected.

Sagittal MRI sequences show herniation of the cerebellar tonsils approximately 7 mm below the level of the foramen magnum. The tonsils appear pointed and peg-like. There is narrowing of the CSF space at the craniocervical junction, but no cervical syrinx is visualized on spinal survey.

Impression: Chiari I malformation with 7 mm of tonsillar ectopia. No associated syringomyelia is identified.

Fetal MRI at 36 weeks gestation shows appropriate late-third-trimester anatomy. The cerebral cortex shows advanced gyration and deep sulcal development, including defined precentral, postcentral, and superior temporal sulci. The lateral ventricles are normal, with the atrium measuring 6.2 mm. Visualized abdominal organs, kidneys, bladder, and heart are structurally unremarkable.

Impression: Normal fetal MRI study demonstrating mature, age-appropriate brain development and normal systemic structures at 36 weeks gestation.

Cardiac MRI evaluation shows normal heart size and left ventricular wall thickness.
