Biventricular systolic function is well-preserved with a calculated left ventricular ejection fraction of 64% and right ventricular ejection fraction of 58%. Cine imaging confirms normal synchronous contraction of all segments. No myocardial scar or fibrosis is seen on late gadolinium enhancement images, and there is no evidence of pericardial effusion.

Impression: Normal cardiac MRI study. There is no structural or functional abnormality to account for atypical chest pain or non-specific symptoms.

Cardiac MRI demonstrates prominent, excessive trabeculations in the apical and inferolateral regions of the left ventricle. The ratio of non-compacted to compacted myocardium at end-diastole is measured at 2.6, which is diagnostic for non-compaction. The left ventricular volumes are slightly increased, and the global ejection fraction is mildly depressed at 48%. No late gadolinium enhancement is identified within the compacted or non-compacted segments.

Impression: Findings are consistent with Left Ventricular Non-Compaction (LVNC) cardiomyopathy with associated mild systolic dysfunction.

Cardiac magnetic resonance imaging demonstrates normal biventricular size, morphology, and systolic function. The left ventricular ejection fraction is calculated at 65% with symmetric wall thickening during systole. T2-weighted and T1-mapping parameters are entirely normal with no evidence of myocardial edema. No pathological late gadolinium enhancement is present within either the left or right ventricles.

Impression: Normal cardiac MRI study. There is no evidence of ischemic or non-ischemic cardiomyopathy, localized fibrosis, or inflammatory myocardial disease.

Fetal MRI at 31 weeks gestation reveals partial agenesis of the corpus callosum. The anterior body and genu are present, but the splenium and rostrum are absent. There is associated mild colpocephaly with dilated posterior horns of the lateral ventricles, measuring 11.2 mm on the left and 10.9 mm on the right. Cortical sulcation is appropriate for gestational age. No other intracranial abnormalities are visualized.

Impression: Partial agenesis of the corpus callosum and mild bilateral colpocephaly. Remaining fetal anatomy is within normal limits.

MRI of the brain demonstrates a localized region of cortical swelling and hyperintensity on DWI in the right temporal-occipital region. ADC mapping shows corresponding low signal, confirming restricted diffusion and acute cytotoxic edema. No large vessel occlusion is noted on the visualized intracranial flow voids.

Impression: Acute cortical ischemic stroke in the right temporal-occipital territory. No evidence of hemorrhage or mass effect.

Fetal MRI at 29 weeks gestation shows completely normal fetal brain development. The cortical sulcation matches expected landmarks for 29 weeks. The lateral ventricular atria are symmetric and measure 5.9 mm. Posterior fossa and brainstem morphology are unremarkable. Visualized thoracic and abdominal anatomy, including kidneys, urinary bladder, stomach, and bowel, demonstrate normal signal characteristics.

Impression: Completely normal fetal MRI study demonstrating age-appropriate brain development and unremarkable systemic anatomy.

Fetal MRI at 30 weeks gestation reveals findings classic for a Dandy-Walker malformation. There is severe hypoplasia and upward rotation of the cerebellar vermis. This is associated with a highly dilated, cystic posterior fossa that communicates widely with an enlarged fourth ventricle. The torcula and tentorium are abnormally elevated. The lateral ventricles are moderately dilated, with atrial measurements of 11.5 mm, suggesting mild secondary hydrocephalus.

Sulcation patterns within the cerebral hemispheres are slightly delayed but show no overt dysplasia. Impression: Dandy-Walker malformation characterized by cerebellar vermian hypoplasia, an enlarged posterior fossa cyst, and associated mild ventriculomegaly.

MRI of the brain and internal auditory canals (IAC) reveals a well-circumscribed, enhancing mass centered within the right cerebellopontine angle (CPA) measuring approximately 2.1 x 1.8 cm. The lesion extends into the porus acusticus of the right IAC, resulting in widening of the canal (the classic 'ice cream cone' sign). There is mild compression of the adjacent right cerebellar peduncle and brainstem, but no obstructive hydrocephalus.

Impression: Right cerebellopontine angle mass with extension into the internal auditory canal, highly characteristic of a vestibular schwannoma (acoustic neuroma). Otolaryngology and neurosurgical consultation are advised.

High-resolution MR imaging of the internal auditory canals and brain was performed. The bilateral vestibulocochlear and facial nerve complexes are intact, showing symmetric size and signal within the internal auditory canals. No cerebellopontine angle cistern masses or abnormal enhancement are visualized. Brain parenchyma is completely normal.

Impression: Normal MR of the brain and internal auditory canals, with no evidence of acoustic neuroma or other structural lesions to explain the patient's symptoms of unilateral tinnitus.

Fetal MRI evaluated at 28 weeks gestation reveals a left-sided congenital diaphragmatic hernia. The stomach and loops of the small bowel are herniated into the left hemithorax, causing moderate rightward mediastinal shift. The left kidney and spleen appear to remain in the abdomen.

The lateral ventricles are normal, with the atrium measuring 6.1 mm. The cerebral sulcation and gyral patterns are within normal limits for 28 weeks. Impression: Left-sided congenital diaphragmatic hernia with intrathoracic herniation of stomach and bowel, causing moderate mediastinal shift.

Magnetic resonance imaging of the brain was performed utilizing multiplanar, multisequence protocols. The cerebral hemispheres demonstrate normal signal intensity and morphological appearance. No intra- or extra-axial mass lesions, areas of restricted diffusion, or acute hemorrhagic focus are identified. The ventricular system, basal cisterns, and subarachnoid spaces are within normal limits for the patient's age.

Impression: Unremarkable MRI of the brain without acute intracranial pathology. Visualized paranasal sinuses and mastoid air cells are clear.

MR of the brain reveals normal brain morphology. There are no localized areas of abnormal signal intensity or enhancement within the cerebral hemispheres, brainstem, or cerebellum. The ventricles are normal in size, and the meninges show no abnormal thickening or enhancement.

Impression: Normal brain MRI. No structural abnormality or pathological enhancement seen.

Fetal MRI at 27 weeks gestation reveals mild asymmetric ventriculomegaly. The right lateral ventricular atrium measures 10.8 mm, while the left lateral ventricular atrium measures 10.2 mm. No associated anomalies such as periventricular nodular heterotopia or subependymal cysts are visualized. The corpus callosum is intact, and the posterior fossa structures are normal in appearance and size. Fetal spine, chest, and abdomen are unremarkable.

Impression: Isolated mild bilateral ventriculomegaly at 27 weeks gestation. Follow-up imaging is recommended to monitor the ventricular dimensions.

Fetal MRI at 20 weeks gestation demonstrates completely normal early anatomical development. Symmetric, normal ventricles measuring 5.2 mm are seen. Midline brain structures, early primary sulcation, the cerebellar hemispheres, and the posterior fossa are normal and unremarkable. The fetal chest, abdominal organs, and spinal column are structurally normal.

Impression: Normal fetal MRI at 20 weeks gestation, demonstrating age-appropriate structural brain and systemic development.

MR imaging of the brain was performed using multiplanar, multisequence protocols. Brain structures demonstrate completely normal anatomical appearance. There are no signs of intracranial hemorrhage, infarcts, or extra-axial masses. Ventricular dimensions and CSF flow patterns are entirely preserved. Visualized vascular structures demonstrate normal flow voids.

Impression: Completely normal brain MRI. No evidence of organic brain disease or acute pathology to explain clinical balance concerns.

Fetal MRI at 30 weeks gestation demonstrates bilateral ventriculomegaly. The lateral ventricular atria measure 15.8 mm on the left and 15.1 mm on the right. There is thinning of the overlying cerebral mantle. The cortical sulcation and opercularization patterns are delayed by approximately 2-3 weeks for the stated gestational age.

Impression: Severe bilateral fetal ventriculomegaly. Recommend prenatal genetic counseling and postnatal neurosurgical evaluation.

Fetal MRI at 29 weeks gestation demonstrates a right-sided congenital diaphragmatic hernia (CDH). A portion of the fetal liver (the left lobe) and gallbladder are herniated into the right hemithorax, causing a leftward mediastinal shift and compression of the heart. The right lung is nearly completely compressed, and the left lung shows reduced T2-weighted signal and volume.

The cerebral ventricles are normal in size, with atrial measurements of 6.3 mm. Brain sulcation matches expectations for 29 weeks. Impression: Right-sided congenital diaphragmatic hernia with liver-up herniation and secondary pulmonary hypoplasia.

Fetal MRI at 28 weeks gestation demonstrates features consistent with a Dandy-Walker variant. There is mild hypoplasia of the inferior cerebellar vermis, and the cisterna magna is moderately dilated, measuring 11.5 mm. The fourth ventricle communicates with the posterior fossa space. The lateral ventricles are within normal limits with an atrial width of 8.8 mm. Cerebral sulcation is normal.

Impression: Dandy-Walker variant characterized by mild inferior vermian hypoplasia and moderate cisterna magna enlargement. Reassuring supratentorial brain development.

Fetal MRI performed at 24 weeks gestation for further evaluation of family history of CNS anomalies. There is normal development of the fetal cerebral hemispheres with symmetric lateral ventricles, the left measuring 5.8 mm and the right measuring 6.0 mm. Cortical folding and sulcation are entirely appropriate for 24 weeks gestation. The corpus callosum, cerebellar hemispheres, and brainstem are well-defined and structurally normal.

Impression: Normal fetal brain MRI. No evidence of ventriculomegaly or developmental brain anomalies at 24 weeks gestation.

Evaluation of the thoracic aorta demonstrates a focal, high-grade narrowing of the proximal descending aorta just distal to the origin of the left subclavian artery. The narrow segment measures approximately 8 mm in diameter, with a significant post-coarctation dilation distal to the obstruction. Flow analysis reveals a peak systolic velocity of 3.8 m/s across the stenosis, corresponding to a peak pressure gradient of approximately 58 mmHg. Collateral vessels are visualized along the chest wall.

Impression: Classic severe focal coarctation of the thoracic aorta with significant hemodynamic obstruction and extensive collateral vessel development. Left ventricular mass is increased, reflecting chronic pressure overload.

Brain MRI demonstrates generalized parenchymal volume loss, characterized by prominent cortical sulci and enlargement of the ventricular system. There is disproportionate thinning and atrophy of the hippocampus bilaterally, left greater than right, along with enlargement of the temporal horns of the lateral ventricles. Chronic microvascular white matter changes are mild.

Impression: Significant generalized cerebral atrophy, with disproportionate bilateral hippocampal atrophy. These structural findings support a clinical diagnosis of neurodegenerative disease, such as Alzheimer's disease.

Magnetic resonance imaging of the brain was performed utilizing multiplanar, multisequence protocols. The brain parenchyma is normal in appearance, with no signs of acute focal ischemia, hemorrhage, or mass effect. Ventricles and sulci are well within normal limits for the patient's age. Cranial nerves VII and VIII appear normal bilaterally.

Impression: Unremarkable MRI of the brain. No structural anomalies, intracranial masses, or evidence of acute ischemia are identified to account for the patient's clinical symptoms of tension headaches.

MRI of the brain demonstrates normal gray-white matter differentiation. There are no areas of abnormal enhancement, restricted diffusion, or susceptibility artifact to suggest active ischemia, mass lesions, or hemorrhage. The ventricles, sulci, and cisterns are normal in size and configuration.

Impression: Completely normal brain MRI. No structural abnormality is identified to explain the clinical history of acute-onset subjective tinnitus.

Fetal MRI at 22 weeks gestation reveals a mild malformation of the posterior fossa. The inferior cerebellar vermis is hypoplastic, with a keyhole communication between the fourth ventricle and an enlarged posterior fossa fluid space. The cerebellar hemispheres are normal in size. The lateral ventricles measure 7.1 mm and are within normal limits, and the corpus callosum appears intact.

Impression: Dandy-Walker variant (isolated inferior cerebellar vermian hypoplasia) with keyhole communication to the cisterna magna. Lateral ventricles are normal.

The study demonstrates normal intracranial anatomical structures. Brain parenchyma shows no signal abnormalities on T1, T2, or FLAIR sequences. There is no evidence of restricted diffusion, intracranial bleeding, or abnormal pathological enhancement. The ventricles and extra-axial fluid spaces are normal for age.

Impression: Negative MR study of the brain. No structural, inflammatory, or vascular changes are detected to explain the patient's recent episode of syncope.

Cardiac MRI shows normal left ventricular volumes with preserved systolic function (LVEF 65%). High-resolution cine imaging of the mitral valve demonstrates posterior systolic displacement of the posterior mitral valve leaflet (P2 segment) by approximately 4 mm past the mitral annular plane. Phase-contrast flow quantification demonstrates a significant regurgitant volume of 38 mL, consistent with moderate mitral regurgitation. No myocardial scar or enhancement is noted on LGE sequences.

Impression: Posterior mitral valve leaflet prolapse (P2 segment) with moderate mitral regurgitation. Left ventricular size and systolic function are currently preserved.

Multiplanar, multisequence brain MRI was performed. The brain parenchyma is normal in appearance with appropriate white matter and gray matter differentiation. No areas of abnormal signal intensity are noted on T2/FLAIR or DWI sequences. The optic chiasm, pituitary gland, and brainstem are unremarkable. The paranasal sinuses and mastoid air cells are well-aerated.

Impression: Normal MR imaging of the brain. No structural abnormality, parenchymal lesion, or evidence of acute intracranial pathology.

The study demonstrates concentric thickening of the left ventricular myocardium (septal thickness 17 mm) and biatrial enlargement. Late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) imaging reveals diffuse, subendocardial, and transmural LGE of non-coronary distribution across both ventricles. There is also marked enhancement of the atrial walls and a classic failure to properly null the myocardium during the TI scout sequence.

Impression: Diffuse biventricular and atrial late gadolinium enhancement is highly characteristic of cardiac amyloidosis. Clinical and biochemical correlation with serum free light chains or pyrophosphate scintigraphy is recommended.

Fetal MRI at 36 weeks gestation demonstrates a right-sided congenital diaphragmatic hernia (CDH). A significant portion of the right lobe of the liver and small intestinal loops are herniated into the right hemithorax. This causes severe leftward shift of the mediastinum and compression of the left lung. The observed-to-expected total lung volume is estimated at 35%. Intracranial structures are normal with a mature sulcation pattern. The ventricular system is normal, measuring 6.8 mm.

Amniotic fluid is moderately increased. Impression: Right-sided CDH with liver herniation and severe secondary pulmonary hypoplasia.

MR evaluation of the brain reveals a large crescentic extra-axial fluid collection over the left cerebral hemisphere, measuring up to 1.8 cm in maximal thickness. The collection is heterogeneous on T1 and T2 sequences, demonstrating internal septations and signs of multi-staged hemorrhage. It exerts significant mass effect on the underlying brain parenchyma, resulting in effacement of the left lateral ventricle and a 7 mm midline shift to the right.

Impression: Large, chronic-to-subacute subdural hematoma over the left cerebral hemisphere with prominent mass effect and midline shift. Neurosurgical evaluation is indicated.

Fetal MRI at 29 weeks gestation shows significant abnormalities of the renal parenchyma. The left kidney is severely enlarged and replaced by multiple, non-communicating cysts of varying sizes up to 1.8 cm, consistent with multicystic dysplastic kidney (MCDK). The contralateral right kidney appears normal in size and parenchymal signal, and the fetal bladder is normally filled with urine. Amniotic fluid volume is subjective normal.

Impression: Left multicystic dysplastic kidney with a normal, functioning right kidney. Amniotic fluid volume remains adequate.

Brain MRI demonstrates a well-demarcated area of restricted diffusion in the left middle cerebral artery (MCA) territory, specifically involving the posterior limb of the internal capsule and adjacent lentiform nucleus. This area is hyperintense on DWI and hypointense on ADC mapping, consistent with acute cytotoxic edema. Corresponding T2/FLAIR hyperintensity is subtle, suggesting relatively early onset within the therapeutic window.

Impression: Acute ischemic infarction of the left basal ganglia/internal capsule region in the left MCA distribution. Immediate clinical correlation and stroke team evaluation are indicated.

Fetal MRI at 35 weeks gestation demonstrates partial agenesis of the corpus callosum, with absence of the posterior body and splenium. There is mild colpocephaly, with the posterior horns of the lateral ventricles measuring 11.5 mm on the left and 11.1 mm on the right. The anterior horns and third ventricle are mildly elevated. Sulcation is mature and appropriate for 35 weeks, with well-defined primary and secondary gyri.

The posterior fossa structures, including the brainstem and cerebellar vermis, are normal. Impression: Partial agenesis of the corpus callosum with mild colpocephaly. Normal cortical maturation and no other structural anomalies identified.

Fetal MRI at 23 weeks gestation demonstrates severe shortening of all fetal long bones (micromelia). There is also marked narrowing of the fetal thorax with a 'bell-shaped' appearance and short ribs. The skull shows a slightly prominent forehead (frontal bossing) but normal mineralization. The brain parenchyma is structurally normal for 23 weeks, with an atrial ventricular width of 6.2 mm and age-appropriate sulcation patterns.

No internal organs show gross structural malformations. Impression: Severe skeletal dysplasia, most consistent with a lethal form such as thanatophoric dysplasia, characterized by severe micromelia, narrow chest, and frontal bossing.

Fetal MRI at 28 weeks gestation demonstrates complete agenesis of the corpus callosum. There is characteristic colpocephaly, with prominence of the posterior occipital horns measuring 14.2 mm bilaterally and a tear-drop appearance of the lateral ventricles. The third ventricle is superiorly displaced and dilated, while the cingulate gyrus exhibits a radial, sunburst sulcation pattern.

Impression: Complete agenesis of the corpus callosum with associated colpocephaly. No other associated midline structural anomalies are detected in the posterior fossa.

Fetal MRI at 32 weeks gestation reveals mild bilateral ventriculomegaly. The right lateral ventricular atrium measures 11.2 mm and the left measures 10.8 mm. Cortical folding is appropriate for 32 weeks, with prominent central and superior frontal sulci. The corpus callosum and posterior fossa are structurally within normal limits. No evidence of hemorrhage or ischemic damage is noted.

Impression: Mild, isolated bilateral ventriculomegaly. Sulcation is age-appropriate; follow-up ultrasound is recommended to monitor ventricular caliber.

Cardiac MRI reveals a large secundum-type atrial septal defect (ASD) measuring approximately 2.4 cm in diameter. There is a significant left-to-right shunt with a calculated pulmonary-to-systemic flow ratio (Qp/Qs) of 1.8. Moderate right ventricular dilation is present (RVEDVI 124 mL/m²), but right ventricular systolic function remains preserved.

Impression: Secundum atrial septal defect with significant left-to-right shunt and consequent right ventricular volume overload. Left ventricular dimensions and function are within normal limits.

MR imaging of the brain demonstrates a large, heterogeneous, ring-enhancing mass centered within the right temporal lobe, measuring approximately 4.2 x 3.8 x 3.5 cm. The lesion is surrounded by an extensive zone of T2/FLAIR hyperintense vasogenic edema, which causes significant mass effect, including partial compression of the right lateral ventricle and a 6 mm leftward midline shift. Foci of internal microhemorrhage and central necrosis are prominent.

Impression: Highly aggressive intra-axial mass in the right temporal lobe, highly characteristic of a high-grade glioma such as glioblastoma. There is associated severe mass effect, vasogenic edema, and subfalcine herniation.

Fetal MRI at 22 weeks gestation reveals a severe malformation of the posterior fossa structures. There is complete agenesis of the cerebellar vermis associated with marked enlargement of the posterior fossa and cystic dilation of the fourth ventricle. The cerebellar hemispheres are hypoplastic and displaced anterolaterally. The tentorium cerebelli is elevated. The supratentorial brain shows normal migration with ventricular atria measuring 8.5 mm.

Fetal spine appears intact. Visceral anatomy is unremarkable. Impression: Dandy-Walker malformation. There is severe cerebellar vermis agenesis with posterior fossa expansion. Genetic and neurosurgical consultation is recommended.

Dedicated MRI evaluation of the sella turcica demonstrates a large, well-circumscribed, hypo-enhancing mass centered within the adenohypophysis, measuring 1.5 x 1.2 x 1.3 cm. The mass expands the sella and abuts the optic chiasm, with mild upward displacement of the chiasm structure. No cavernous sinus invasion is observed.

Impression: Pituitary macroadenoma with mild mass effect and superior extension touching the optic chiasm. Visual field testing and endocrinological workup are indicated.

Fetal MRI at 28 weeks gestation demonstrates complete agenesis of the corpus callosum. The normal comma-shaped ventricles are absent; instead, there is parallel alignment of the lateral ventricles (colpocephaly) with dilation of the occipital horns measuring 12.5 mm on the left and 12.1 mm on the right. Steer-horn configuration of the frontal horns is noted on coronal views. The third ventricle is superiorly displaced. Sulcation patterns are slightly delayed but within acceptable parameters for gestational age.

Impression: Complete agenesis of the fetal corpus callosum with associated mild bilateral colpocephaly. No other major intracranial anomalies or extracranial findings are detected.

Fetal MRI at 27 weeks gestation demonstrates complete agenesis of the corpus callosum. There is associated moderate colpocephaly, with the left lateral ventricle atrium measuring 12.0 mm and the right lateral ventricle atrium measuring 11.8 mm. The third ventricle is elevated and mildly dilated.

The sulcal pattern shows the classic radial orientation of gyri along the medial hemispheric wall. There are no additional parenchymal anomalies or posterior fossa cysts. Impression: Complete agenesis of the corpus callosum with associated moderate colpocephaly and characteristic radial sulcation pattern.

MR imaging of the brain with and without gadolinium contrast reveals a large, heterogeneously enhancing, thick-walled necrotic mass centered in the right temporal lobe measuring approximately 4.8 x 4.2 x 3.9 cm. There is a vast surrounding territory of vasogenic edema displaying high T2/FLAIR signal, causing significant mass effect with a 7 mm leftward midline shift and partial compression of the right lateral ventricle and temporal horn. Perfusion-weighted imaging shows elevated relative cerebral blood volume (rCBV) in the peripheral enhancing nodular components, suggestive of neovascularization.

Impression: Large, heterogeneously enhancing, necrotic intra-axial right temporal lobe mass with significant surrounding mass effect and midline shift. The imaging features and perfusion characteristics are highly suspicious for a high-grade primary glial neoplasm, such as glioblastoma multiforme (GBM).

Fetal MRI at 34 weeks gestation demonstrates beautifully mature cerebral anatomy. The deep sulcation is well-developed, with deep sylvian fissures and prominent central and superior temporal sulci, entirely age-appropriate. The lateral ventricles are normal and symmetric, with the atrial width measuring 6.1 mm. The fetal organs in the chest and abdomen are morphologically normal.

Impression: Normal fetal MRI at 34 weeks gestation, confirming excellent and symmetrical cerebral development with appropriate cortical maturation.

Fetal MRI at 25 weeks gestation reveals a large left-sided congenital diaphragmatic hernia (CDH). The stomach, several loops of small bowel, and a portion of the left hepatic lobe have herniated into the left hemithorax. This has resulted in a severe mediastinal shift to the right, compression of the fetal heart, and severe hypoplasia of the left lung. The right lung volume is also mildly reduced.

The fetal brain shows normal structure and sulcation for 25 weeks, with an atrial width of 6.2 mm. Impression: Left-sided congenital diaphragmatic hernia with significant herniation of abdominal organs, mediastinal shift, and secondary pulmonary hypoplasia.

Cardiac MRI shows a small-to-moderate perimembranous ventricular septal defect (VSD) measuring approximately 8 mm in diameter. Phase-contrast imaging demonstrates a left-to-right shunt with a Qp/Qs ratio of 1.35. The left ventricle is minimally dilated with an end-diastolic volume of 152 mL, and global systolic function is preserved with an ejection fraction of 61%. Right ventricular size and function are within normal limits.

Impression: Small-to-moderate perimembranous ventricular septal defect with a mild left-to-right shunt. Preserved biventricular systolic function and mild left-sided volume load.

The right ventricle is severely dilated and demonstrates regional wall motion abnormalities, including microaneurysms and dyskinesis of the right ventricular outflow tract (RVOT) and inferior free wall. The right ventricular ejection fraction is reduced at 35%. The left ventricle appears normal in size and function with an ejection fraction of 59%. Delayed contrast imaging reveals patchy late gadolinium enhancement along the right ventricular free wall.

Impression: Right ventricular dilation and dyskinesis with reduced right ventricular ejection fraction, highly suggestive of Arrhythmogenic Right Ventricular Cardiomyopathy (ARVC) meeting Task Force diagnostic criteria.

Fetal MRI at 22 weeks gestation evaluated for severe oligohydramnios. There is complete absence of amniotic fluid, causing severe compression of the fetus and limiting image quality. No renal parenchymal tissue or renal arteries can be identified within either fetal flank or the pelvis. The fetal bladder is not visualized. The fetal lungs are small, indicating pulmonary hypoplasia secondary to prolonged anhydramnios.

Impression: Bilateral renal agenesis associated with severe anhydramnios and early pulmonary hypoplasia (Potter sequence).

Cardiac MRI was requested for assessment of coronary anatomy and anomalous origin. Multiplanar cine and angiography sequences demonstrate normal origin and course of the main coronary arteries. Both ventricles and atria demonstrate normal volumes, mass indices, and morphology. The left ventricular ejection fraction is 62%, and there is no late gadolinium enhancement or edema.

Impression: Normal cardiac MRI with normal coronary origins. No structural, tissue, or functional myocardial pathologies are identified.

Brain MR evaluation shows multiple, well-circumscribed, ovoid T2/FLAIR hyperintense demyelinating plaques oriented perpendicular to the ventricles along the corpus callosum (Dawson's fingers) and within the periventricular white matter. Three of these lesions, localized to the left parietal lobe, demonstrate nodular ring enhancement following gadolinium administration, indicating active disease.

Impression: Findings are highly characteristic of active demyelinating disease, consistent with multiple sclerosis. Presence of both enhancing and non-enhancing lesions fulfills McDonald criteria for dissemination in time and space.

Fetal MRI performed at 26 weeks gestation reveals a complete absence of the corpus callosum. There is characteristic colpocephaly with dilation and teardrop shaping of the occipital horns; the atrial width of the left lateral ventricle measures 12.1 mm and the right measures 11.8 mm. The cerebral gyri display a radial 'sunburst' pattern extending from the margin of the third ventricle, which is slightly elevated.

Impression: Agenesis of the corpus callosum with associated mild colpocephaly. No other intracranial anomalies are visualized.

Cardiac MRI demonstrates normal left and right ventricular chamber dimensions. The left ventricular end-diastolic volume is 135 mL and end-systolic volume is 51 mL, yielding a calculated left ventricular ejection fraction of 62%. There is no focal wall motion abnormality or evidence of myocardial edema on T2-weighted sequences. Late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) imaging shows no hyperenhancement to suggest focal myocardial scar or fibrosis.

Impression: Unremarkable cardiac MRI study. Normal biventricular size and systolic function with no evidence of myocardial scar, inflammation, or infiltration.

Brain MRI shows multiple bilateral focal areas of T2 and FLAIR hyperintensity within the deep and periventricular white matter, sparing the subcortical U-fibers. These findings are stable compared to prior imaging and do not show signs of restricted diffusion or abnormal contrast enhancement. The ventricles and cortical sulci are mildly prominent, consistent with mild age-related involutional changes.

Impression: Moderate chronic microvascular ischemic white matter disease. Mild generalized parenchymal volume loss appropriate for the patient's age.

Fetal MRI at 24 weeks gestation shows findings consistent with a Dandy-Walker variant. There is partial hypoplasia of the inferior cerebellar vermis, with mild dilation of the posterior fossa CSF space and prominent communication with the fourth ventricle. The cerebellar hemispheres appear structurally normal. The lateral ventricles are within normal limits (7.2 mm atria) and the corpus callosum is intact.

No other major systemic anomalies are identified. Amniotic fluid volume is normal. Impression: Fetal Dandy-Walker variant characterized by partial inferior vermian hypoplasia, with no evidence of significant ventriculomegaly or hydrocephalus.

Fetal MRI performed at 33 weeks gestation reveals normal fetal development. The cerebral hemispheres demonstrate normal symmetric architecture, and the sulcation pattern is well-developed for 33 weeks, showing secondary sulci. The lateral ventricles are completely symmetric with an atrial diameter of 5.9 mm.

The corpus callosum and brainstem are completely intact, and no posterior fossa abnormalities are noted. Amniotic fluid and placenta are normal. Impression: Completely normal fetal MRI study demonstrating appropriate structural development.

Fetal MRI at 25 weeks gestation reveals a large occipital encephalocele. A defect in the occipital bone measures approximately 1.5 cm, through which a cerebrospinal fluid-filled hernial sac containing herniated, dysplastic occipital brain tissue and meninges protrudes. This defect is associated with microcephaly and distortion of the posterior fossa structures. The lateral ventricles are dilated, with atrial measurements of 11.2 mm on the right and 11.5 mm on the left.

Impression: Posterior occipital encephalocele with cerebral herniation, microcephaly, and moderate ventriculomegaly. Pediatric neurosurgical consultation is recommended to discuss prognosis and delivery options.

Fetal MRI at 30 weeks gestation reveals normal structural development. The cerebral cortex shows expected gyration, and the lateral ventricles are completely normal, with the atrium measuring 6.1 mm. The corpus callosum is intact, and posterior fossa structures show normal development.

No abnormalities of the fetal spine, face, chest, or abdomen are detected. Impression: Normal fetal MRI study demonstrating age-appropriate brain development and normal visceral anatomy.

MRI of the brain demonstrates normal anatomical findings. The cerebral cortex, white matter, and deep gray nuclei are within normal limits. There are no signs of demyelination, mass effect, or prior ischemia. Basal cisterns and CSF spaces are entirely unremarkable.

Impression: Unremarkable and normal brain MRI. No intracranial findings to explain atypical migrainous presentation.

Brain MRI demonstrates multiple focus-like T2/FLAIR hyperintense lesions within the periventricular, juxtacortical, and infratentorial white matter. Several of these lesions demonstrate active contrast enhancement following gadolinium administration, indicative of blood-brain barrier disruption. Moderate cerebral atrophy is observed, out of proportion to the patient's age.

Impression: Active neuroinflammatory demyelinating process consistent with a relapsing-remitting multiple sclerosis (RRMS) flare-up. Multiple active enhancing lesions are visualized.

Fetal MRI at 23 weeks gestation performed for borderline ventriculomegaly on prior ultrasound. Current MR imaging demonstrates symmetric lateral ventricles measuring 7.1 mm on the left and 6.9 mm on the right, which are well within normal limits. Cortical sulcation is appropriate for 23 weeks, displaying a normal sylvian fissure pattern. The corpus callosum and posterior fossa are normal.

Impression: Normal fetal MRI. Resolving or normal-variant borderline ventriculomegaly with no structural anomalies detected.

Magnetic resonance imaging of the brain with and without gadolinium demonstrates a large, heterogeneously enhancing mass centered within the right temporal lobe, measuring 4.5 x 3.8 x 4.1 cm. The lesion exhibits extensive central non-enhancing areas consistent with necrosis, surrounded by a prominent rim of vasogenic edema. There is moderate mass effect on the right lateral ventricle, resulting in a 6 mm leftward midline shift.

Impression: High-grade primary glial neoplasm, highly suggestive of glioblastoma multiforme. Secondary mass effect with early subfalcine herniation is noted. Urgent neurosurgical consultation is recommended.

Fetal MRI at 33 weeks gestation shows normal structural anatomy. Cerebral cortical maturation is progressing normally, with expected secondary sulci visible. The lateral ventricles are completely symmetric with an atrial diameter of 6.1 mm. The midline structures, including the corpus callosum and pituitary gland, are unremarkable.

All extracranial structures, including the chest, abdomen, spine, and bladder, are normal. Impression: Completely normal fetal MRI study demonstrating age-appropriate structural and central nervous system development.

Fetal MRI at 23 weeks gestation demonstrates multiple, bilateral non-communicating cysts of varying sizes throughout both kidneys. There is no normal renal parenchyma visible on either side, consistent with bilateral multicystic dysplastic kidney (MCDK) disease. The bladder is not filled and cannot be identified. Marked oligohydramnios is present. The fetal brain and spine appear normal for 23 weeks, with ventricular atria measuring 6.1 mm.

Sulcation is appropriate for gestational age. Impression: Bilateral multicystic dysplastic kidney disease and severe oligohydramnios.

MR imaging of the brain demonstrates an irregular, peripherally enhancing thick-walled cystic mass within the right temporal lobe, measuring approximately 4.2 x 3.8 x 3.5 cm. This lesion is surrounded by an extensive zone of T2/FLAIR hyperintensity, consistent with vasogenic edema, causing significant compression of the temporal horn of the right lateral ventricle and a 6 mm leftward midline shift. No evidence of hemorrhage is noted, but restricted diffusion along the rim is suggestive of high hypercellularity.

Impression: Enhancing right temporal lobe intra-axial mass with extensive surrounding edema and mass effect, highly suspicious for a high-grade glioma (such as glioblastoma multiforme). Urgent neurosurgical consultation is recommended.

MR imaging of the brain demonstrates herniation of the cerebellar tonsils approximately 7 mm below the level of the foramen magnum. The tonsils are pointed in configuration. There is crowding of the craniocervical junction, but no evidence of syringomyelia in the cervical cord covered on this exam. The supratentorial brain is unremarkable.

Impression: Chiari I malformation, indicated by 7 mm tonsillar ectopia and crowding of the craniocervical junction. No associated cervical syrinx visualized on these sagittal sequences.

Brain MRI shows multiple discrete, ovoid T2/FLAIR hyperintense lesions within the periventricular, juxtacortical, and infratentorial white matter. Several periventricular lesions are oriented perpendicular to the lateral ventricles, suggestive of Dawson's fingers. Following contrast administration, two active lesions in the right frontal lobe demonstrate nodular and incomplete ring enhancement, indicative of active demyelination.

Impression: Multiple demyelinating-type white matter lesions demonstrating dissemination in space and time. Findings are highly characteristic of active relapsing-remitting multiple sclerosis (MS).

Fetal MRI at 35 weeks gestation demonstrates a single live fetus in breech presentation. The fetal brain demonstrates normal parenchymal signal intensity and excellent sulcation matching 35 weeks development. The lateral ventricular atria measure 5.5 mm bilaterally, which is well within normal limits. The corpus callosum is intact and the brainstem is normal.

Visualized fetal chest and abdomen reveal normal lungs, symmetric kidneys, and a normal urinary bladder. Spine is intact. Impression: Normal fetal MRI at 35 weeks gestation. No structural, cranial, or somatic anomalies.

Cardiac MRI demonstrates normal ventricular volumes, wall thickness, and systolic function of both the left and right ventricles. Left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) is 63%, and right ventricular ejection fraction (RVEF) is 61%. First-pass perfusion and late gadolinium enhancement sequences are completely normal, with no evidence of myocardial scar, ischemia, or active inflammation.

Impression: Normal cardiac MRI. Unremarkable ventricular anatomy, preserved biventricular systolic function, and no evidence of scar or fibrosis.

Anatomical and functional cardiac MRI sequences show normal chamber sizes and preserved wall thickness. Left and right ventricular ejection fractions are normal at 60% and 53% respectively. No regional dyskinesia, akinesia, or hypokinesia are demonstrated. Real-time rest perfusion and late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) imaging show no evidence of microvascular ischemia, focal myocardial scar, or structural abnormality.

Impression: Unremarkable cardiac MRI. Normal ventricular morphology, volumes, and systolic function without signs of ischemic heart disease or infiltrative cardiomyopathy.

Cardiac MRI is performed for evaluation of unexplained palpitations. Both ventricles demonstrate normal internal dimensions and mass. The left ventricular ejection fraction is 61%, and the right ventricular ejection fraction is 56%. No segmental wall motion abnormalities, regional thinning, or myocardial edema is identified. Delayed post-contrast sequences show no evidence of late gadolinium enhancement (LGE).

Impression: Unremarkable cardiac MRI. Preserved biventricular systolic function with no structural heart anomalies, scar, or perfusion defects identified.

Multiplanar MR angiography of the thoracic aorta demonstrates a discrete, focal narrowing of the distal aortic arch, just distal to the origin of the left subclavian artery. The minimum luminal diameter at the coarctation site is 8 mm, compared to 20 mm at the mid-ascending aorta. Prominent collateral intercostal and internal mammary arteries are visualized bypassing the obstruction. Mild left ventricular hypertrophy is present.

Impression: Classic post-ductal coarctation of the aorta with significant narrowing and well-developed collateral circulation. Left ventricular hypertrophic remodeling is present with a normal ejection fraction of 60%.

Fetal MRI at 24 weeks gestation reveals normal intracranial and extracranial anatomy. The lateral ventricular atria measure 6.0 mm bilaterally, and the cerebrospinal fluid spaces are entirely normal. The corpus callosum is fully formed, and the cerebellar vermis displays normal morphology. Cerebral sulcation and migration are normal for 24 weeks.

The spine is intact without dysraphism. Thoracic, abdominal, and pelvic structures are normal, with appropriate amniotic fluid volume. Impression: Completely normal fetal MRI study demonstrating age-appropriate structural development.

Fetal MRI at 29 weeks gestation demonstrates a right-sided congenital diaphragmatic hernia (CDH). The right hepatic lobe and a segment of the gallbladder are herniated into the right hemithorax. This causes leftward mediastinal shift and compression of the heart and left lung. The total fetal lung volume is calculated at 42% of expected, indicating moderate pulmonary hypoplasia.

The fetal brain shows normal age-appropriate sulcation and normal lateral ventricles with an atrial width of 5.6 mm. Impression: Right-sided congenital diaphragmatic hernia with liver herniation and moderate fetal pulmonary hypoplasia.

Cardiac MRI demonstrates severe mitral regurgitation arising from posterior leaflet prolapse (P2 segment) with associated chordal rupture. The left atrium is severely dilated (volume index of 65 mL/m²), and the left ventricle is moderately dilated (LVEDV 210 mL) with compensatory hyperkinesis (LVEF 68%). Mitral regurgitant volume is calculated at 55 mL per beat, corresponding to a regurgitant fraction of 48%.

Impression: Severe mitral valve regurgitation secondary to posterior mitral leaflet prolapse and flail. Significant left atrial and ventricular dilatation are seen, reflecting chronic volume overload.

Fetal MRI at 34 weeks gestation demonstrates mild bilateral lateral ventriculomegaly. The left atrium measures 11.2 mm and the right atrium measures 10.9 mm. There is no evidence of intracranial mass, subependymal nodules, or intraventricular hemorrhage. The corpus callosum is fully formed and normal in length. Sulcation is mature and fully appropriate for 34 weeks.

Fetal body, limbs, and abdominal organs are unremarkable. Impression: Mild, isolated bilateral ventriculomegaly with normal underlying brain parenchyma. Recommend serial sonographic monitoring.

High-resolution imaging of the sella turcica demonstrates a hypoenhancing, well-circumscribed lesion in the right lateral aspect of the anterior pituitary gland, measuring 8 x 6 mm. There is mild deviation of the pituitary stalk to the left, but the optic chiasm is free and unimpeded.

Impression: Pituitary microadenoma in the right lateral adenohypophysis, without optic chiasm compression.

Fetal MRI at 22 weeks gestation demonstrates bilateral renal agenesis. No renal tissue or renal arteries can be identified in either renal fossa, and the adrenal glands show the characteristic 'lying down' sign. Severe anhydramnios (complete absence of amniotic fluid) is noted, leading to significant crowding of the fetus. There is secondary mild pulmonary hypoplasia.

The fetal brain shows normal morphology and sulcation for 22 weeks, with a ventricular atrium measuring 5.4 mm. Impression: Bilateral renal agenesis associated with severe anhydramnios and secondary pulmonary hypoplasia.

Adult follow-up MRI in a patient with a history of repaired Tetralogy of Fallot. The study reveals severe pulmonary valve regurgitation with a calculated regurgitant fraction of 46%. There is severe dilation of the right ventricle (end-diastolic volume index of 172 ml/m²) and mild right ventricular dysfunction with an RVEF of 40%. The left ventricle remains normal in size with a preserved EF of 58%.

Impression: Repaired Tetralogy of Fallot showing severe pulmonary valve regurgitation and significant right ventricular dilation. These findings meet typical criteria for consideration of pulmonary valve replacement.

Multiplanar brain MRI was performed to evaluate chronic migraine symptoms. The ventricular system, basal cisterns, and major sulci are all within normal limits. No space-occupying lesions, foci of restricted diffusion, or abnormal enhancement patterns are observed in the cerebral hemispheres, cerebellum, or brainstem. The major vascular flow voids are intact.

Impression: Completely normal MR examination of the brain. No structural, neoplastic, or vascular etiology is present to account for the patient's migraine clinical profile.

MRI of the brain demonstrates normal anatomical configuration of the cerebral hemispheres, brainstem, and cerebellum. There is no restriction of diffusion on DWI sequence to suggest acute infarction. The ventricular system and subarachnoid spaces show age-appropriate mild prominence, without signs of hydrocephalus. The dural venous sinuses show normal flow voids.

Impression: Normal MRI of the brain. No acute territorial ischemia, mass lesion, or abnormal intracranial enhancement identified to explain the patient's neurological symptoms.

MRI brain demonstrates multiple callososeptal, periventricular, and juxtacortical hyperintense lesions on FLAIR and T2-weighted sequences. Several lesions are oriented perpendicular to the ventricles (Dawson's fingers). After contrast administration, two active periventricular lesions show nodular enhancement, suggesting lesions of varying ages.

Impression: Multiple demyelinating lesions demonstrating dissemination in time and space, highly indicative of active multiple sclerosis. Neurology follow-up is recommended.

Cardiac and thoracic MR angiography shows a discrete narrowing of the proximal descending thoracic aorta, located immediately distal to the origin of the left subclavian artery. The luminal diameter at the coarctation site is 6 mm with post-stenotic dilation of 22 mm. Significant collateral vessels are noted arising from the internal mammary and intercostal arteries.

Left ventricular volumes are normal, but there is mild concentric hypertrophy of the left ventricle with preserved ejection fraction of 60%. Impression: Discrete coarctation of the descending thoracic aorta with secondary left ventricular hypertrophy and prominent collateral vessel recruitment.

MRI of the brain demonstrates a crescentic, extra-axial fluid collection over the right frontoparietal hemisphere measuring 1.1 cm in maximum thickness. The collection exhibits heterogeneous hyperintensity on T1 and T2 weighted imaging, representing subacute hemorrhage of varying age. There is compression of the underlying sulci and minor mass effect on the right lateral ventricle.

Impression: Subacute right subdural hematoma with minor mass effect. Close imaging and clinical follow-up is recommended to ensure stability.

Fetal MRI at 36 weeks gestation. The fetal brain exhibits advanced, age-appropriate gyration and sulcation, with deep tertiary branches. The lateral ventricles are small and symmetric, measuring 5.2 mm at the atria. The corpus callosum is thick and well-formed. The posterior fossa demonstrates normal cerebellar hemispheres and a normal vermis.

The fetal chest shows fully expanded lungs, and the abdomen, skeletal system, and spine are completely normal. Impression: Normal fetal MRI at 36 weeks gestation, showing advanced cerebral maturation and unremarkable fetal anatomy.

High-resolution brain MRI utilizing epilepsy-specific protocol (including 3D FLAIR and T1 sequences) demonstrates symmetric and morphologically normal hippocampal formations bilaterally. There is no evidence of cortical dysplasia, migration anomalies, or focal mass lesions. Ventricles and extra-axial spaces are normal.

Impression: Unremarkable brain MRI. No structural abnormality or epileptogenic focus identified on this high-resolution study.

Cardiac MRI demonstrates a distinct two-layered structure of the left ventricular myocardium, most prominent in the apical and lateral segments. There is marked hypertrabeculation with deep intratrabecular recesses; the ratio of non-compacted to compacted myocardium at end-diastole is measured at 2.5:1. Left ventricular systolic function is mildly reduced with an ejection fraction of 48%. No late gadolinium enhancement is identified within the compacted or non-compacted layers.

Impression: Findings are diagnostic of Left Ventricular Non-Compaction (LVNC) based on Jenni criteria, with a non-compacted to compacted ratio of 2.5:1 and associated mild left ventricular systolic dysfunction.

Fetal MRI at 21 weeks gestation demonstrates normal fetal anatomy. The cerebral cortex shows initial sylvian fissure formation, which is appropriate for this early gestational age. The lateral ventricles are symmetric, with atrial widths of 5.5 mm on the left and 5.2 mm on the right. The cerebellum and cisterna magna are normal in size and morphology. Visualized thoracic and abdominal viscera are structurally normal.

Impression: Unremarkable fetal MRI at 21 weeks gestation. Normal intracranial structures and age-appropriate early cortical sulcation.

MR of the brain shows normal signal intensity of the brain parenchyma. No acute infarctions, hemorrhages, or intracranial masses are identified. The ventricles and cortical sulci are unremarkable for the patient's age. Visualized paranasal sinuses are clear.

Impression: Unremarkable MRI of the brain. No acute pathology or structural lesions identified.

The ventricles and sulci are within normal limits for the patient's age. There is no evidence of intra-axial or extra-axial mass, acute ischemia, or hemorrhage. Visualized cranial nerves VII and VIII are unremarkable, with normal appearance of the internal auditory canals bilaterally.

Impression: Normal MR brain. No acute pathology, posterior fossa abnormalities, or cerebellopontine angle lesions to explain the patient's transient vertigo/dizziness.

Brain MRI shows abnormal high signal intensity on FLAIR sequences within the subarachnoid spaces of the basal cisterns, anterior interhemispheric fissure, and bilateral Sylvian fissures, which correlates with acute subarachnoid hemorrhage. Magnetic resonance angiography (MRA) of the circle of Willis demonstrates a 5 mm saccular aneurysm arising from the anterior communicating artery.

Impression: Acute subarachnoid hemorrhage localized predominantly in the basal cisterns, with an associated anterior communicating artery aneurysm. Urgent neurosurgical intervention is indicated.

Fetal MRI at 28 weeks gestation demonstrates normal intracranial and visceral development. The lateral ventricular atria measure 6.2 mm and are symmetric. The corpus callosum and septum pellucidum are fully visualized and normal. Cerebral sulcation is appropriate for 28 weeks gestation, with normal sylvian and parieto-occipital fissures.

The fetal spine is intact, and the chest, abdomen, and limbs demonstrate normal signal and development. Normal amniotic fluid is present. Impression: Unremarkable fetal MRI at 28 weeks gestation, demonstrating completely normal fetal anatomy.

Cardiac MRI reveals marked, diffuse, concentric biventricular wall thickening (LV septal wall 19 mm) associated with biatrial enlargement. Late gadolinium enhancement imaging demonstrates diffuse, subendocardial, non-coronary LGE involving both ventricles and the atria, accompanied by abnormal myocardial and blood pool gadolinium kinetics. Left ventricular ejection fraction is moderately reduced at 40%.

Impression: Findings are classic for cardiac amyloidosis with advanced restrictive physiology and diffuse myocardial infiltration.

Fetal MRI at 28 weeks gestation demonstrates herniation of the stomach, multiple small bowel loops, and a portion of the left hepatic lobe into the left hemithorax. This causes a significant mediastinal shift to the right, compressing the heart against the right thoracic wall. The left lung volume is severely reduced. Intracranial anatomy is unremarkable, with an atrial width of 6.0 mm and age-appropriate sulcation.

Impression: Left-sided congenital diaphragmatic hernia with significant herniation of abdominal viscera and associated mediastinal shift, suggesting high risk for pulmonary hypoplasia.

Cardiac MRI shows diffuse, symmetric thickening of the left ventricular myocardium (19 mm) and interatrial septum, along with a thickened right ventricular free wall. Late gadolinium enhancement imaging demonstrates classic diffuse, subendocardial hyperenhancement with difficulty nulling the myocardium, typical of cardiac amyloid deposition. Elevated T1 relaxation times are also noted.

Impression: Severe concentric biventricular hypertrophy with classic delayed enhancement patterns of cardiac amyloidosis. Left ventricular ejection fraction is moderately reduced at 40%.

Cardiac MRI demonstrates asymmetric, severe septal hypertrophy with a maximal wall thickness of 22 mm at the mid-ventricular level. There is systolic anterior motion (SAM) of the mitral valve associated with dynamic left ventricular outflow tract (LVOT) obstruction and moderate mitral regurgitation. Late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) imaging shows significant, patchy mid-wall enhancement localized to the hypertrophied septal segments and at the right ventricular insertion points.

Impression: Features are highly characteristic of hypertrophic obstructive cardiomyopathy (HOCM) with septal predominance. The presence of focal late gadolinium enhancement suggests replacement fibrosis, which is a key marker for risk stratification.

Cardiac MRI demonstrates marked dilatation and dysfunction of the right ventricle, with a right ventricular end-diastolic volume index of 135 mL/m2 and an RVEF of 34%. Regional wall motion abnormalities are noted, specifically dyskinesis and aneurysm formation within the right ventricular outflow tract and inferior wall (the triangle of dysplasia). Late gadolinium enhancement imaging reveals patchy, transmural hyperenhancement within the RV free wall, suggesting fibrofatty replacement.

Impression: Right ventricular structural and functional abnormalities highly diagnostic of Arrhythmogenic Right Ventricular Cardiomyopathy (ARVC) based on current Task Force criteria. Left ventricular function is preserved (LVEF 55%).

Cardiac MRI demonstrates severe dilation of the right ventricle with an elevated RV end-diastolic volume index. There is global RV hypokinesis with focal microaneurysms and dyskinesis visualized in the RV free wall and outflow tract (the 'triangle of dysplasia'). The right ventricular ejection fraction is depressed at 34%, while left ventricular size and function are preserved (LVEF 58%). T1-weighted sequences demonstrate fatty infiltration of the RV free wall.

Impression: Features highly suggestive of Arrhythmogenic Right Ventricular Cardiomyopathy (ARVC), meeting major structural task force criteria.

Fetal MR imaging evaluated at 36 weeks gestation reveals excellent development of the fetal brain. Mature tertiary sulcation patterns are visualized, corresponding perfectly to the advanced gestational age. The ventricular system is small and symmetric, with the lateral ventricles measuring 6.1 mm at the atria. Normal anatomical positioning of the thoracic and abdominal organs is confirmed, and the fetal spine is intact.

Impression: Normal late-third-trimester fetal MRI. Structural brain maturation is appropriate for 36 weeks without evidence of congenital anomaly.

Brain MR imaging reveals multiple foci of high T2/FLAIR signal intensity scattered throughout the periventricular, juxtacortical, and infratentorial white matter. Several lesions demonstrate a perpendicular orientation to the lateral ventricles, consistent with Dawson's fingers. Post-contrast imaging reveals active enhancement of two periventricular lesions.

Impression: Demyelinating disease pattern consistent with active Multiple Sclerosis (MS), showing evidence of dissemination in both time and space.

MR of the brain demonstrates a crescentic, extra-axial fluid collection along the right frontoparietal convexity measuring up to 1.4 cm in maximal thickness. The collection is hyperintense on both T1 and T2 weighted imaging, consistent with a subacute subdural hematoma. There is associated compression of the right cerebral hemisphere, sulcal effacement, and a 5 mm leftward midline shift.

Impression: Subacute right frontoparietal subdural hematoma causing moderate mass effect and midline shift. Clinical correlation is recommended.

Fetal MRI at 30 weeks gestation demonstrates complete absence of the corpus callosum. The lateral ventricles display a parallel configuration with widening of the posterior horns (colpocephaly), a classic 'steer-horn' or teardrop appearance on coronal sequences. The left lateral ventricle atrium measures 11.2 mm and the right measures 11.0 mm. Sulcation patterns on the medial aspect of the hemispheres are abnormal, radiating outward in a radial pattern from the third ventricle roof.

No other intracranial masses, hemorrhage, or extracranial anomalies are identified. Impression: Complete agenesis of the corpus callosum (ACC) with associated colpocephaly and mild ventriculomegaly.

MR imaging of the brain reveals an infiltrative, heterogeneously enhancing mass in the left parietal lobe, measuring 4.5 x 3.9 cm, which extends across the splenium of the corpus callosum. Extensive surrounding vasogenic edema is present. There is moderate mass effect on the atrium of the left lateral ventricle, and minor midline shift to the right.

Impression: Infiltrative, heterogeneously enhancing mass in the left parietal lobe with corpus callosum extension, highly suggestive of a high-grade glioma (glioblastoma). Significant surrounding vasogenic edema is present.

Fetal MRI at 25 weeks gestation demonstrates severe, symmetric bilateral ventriculomegaly. The lateral ventricular atria measure 18.2 mm on the left and 17.9 mm on the right. There is prominent dangling of the choroid plexuses and thinning of the surrounding cerebral cortex. The third ventricle is also dilated, whereas the fourth ventricle is normal, strongly suggesting congenital aqueductal stenosis. Sulcation pattern is appropriate for 25 weeks.

Impression: Severe bilateral ventriculomegaly, likely secondary to aqueductal stenosis. Early prenatal neurosurgical and genetic consultation is recommended.

MR imaging of the brain reveals multiple oval, hyperintense lesions on T2 and FLAIR sequences within the periventricular and juxtacortical white matter. Several of these lesions are oriented perpendicular to the lateral ventricles, demonstrating a classic 'Dawson's fingers' configuration. On post-contrast T1-weighted sequences, two of the periventricular lesions show active ring-like enhancement, indicating active demyelination.

Impression: Multiple demyelinating lesions demonstrating spatial and temporal dissemination, highly consistent with active relapsing-remitting multiple sclerosis (MS). Neurological follow-up is recommended to correlate with CSF findings and clinical criteria.

MRI demonstrates severe dilation of the left ventricle with an end-diastolic volume index of 145 mL/m2. Diffuse global hypokinesis of the left ventricular myocardium is present. Late gadolinium enhancement imaging demonstrates a thin, linear band of mid-wall hyperenhancement in the mid-septal segment, suggesting a non-ischemic pattern of myocardial fibrosis.

Impression: Severe non-ischemic dilated cardiomyopathy. Left ventricular systolic function is severely depressed with a calculated ejection fraction of 28%.

MRI of the brain demonstrates a large, heterogeneously enhancing, infiltrative intra-axial mass in the left temporal lobe measuring approximately 4.8 x 4.2 x 4.0 cm. The mass exhibits prominent central necrotic or cystic areas with thick, irregular peripheral ring enhancement. There is extensive surrounding vasogenic edema causing significant mass effect, with subfalcine herniation to the right by 8 mm and compression of the left lateral ventricle.

Impression: Infiltrative left temporal lobe mass with necrosis and significant surrounding vasogenic edema. Findings are highly suggestive of high-grade glioma, such as glioblastoma multiforme (GBM).

Fetal MRI at 25 weeks gestation shows marked skeletal anomalies. There is severe rhizomelic shortening of the long bones, with curved femurs displaying a 'telephone-receiver' morphology. The thoracic cavity is severely narrowed and bell-shaped, with significant platyspondyly of the spine. Intracranial structures appear normal, though there is mild ventriculomegaly with atrial width at 9.5 mm.

Impression: Severe skeletal dysplasia, most consistent with Thanatophoric Dysplasia Type I, given the combination of telephone-receiver femurs, narrow thorax, and platyspondyly. Prognosis is lethal; pediatric genetics counseling is advised.

Fetal MRI at 29 weeks gestation demonstrates a massively dilated urinary bladder (megacystis) occupying a large portion of the fetal abdomen and pelvis. Severe bilateral hydroureteronephrosis is visualized, with cortical thinning of both kidneys. There is moderate oligohydramnios present. The fetal bowel loops appear small and microcolon is suspected.

Fetal brain anatomy and cortical sulcation are entirely appropriate for 29 weeks, with lateral ventricles measuring 6.8 mm. Impression: Severe megacystis with bilateral hydroureteronephrosis, highly suggestive of Megacystis-Microcolon-Intestinal Hypoperistalsis Syndrome (MMIHS) or posterior urethral valves.

Fetal MRI performed at 32 weeks gestation shows completely normal fetal brain morphology. The cortical sulcation and gyration patterns are well-developed and highly appropriate for 32 weeks, with visible secondary and tertiary sulci. Midline structures, including the corpus callosum and septum pellucidum, are intact. The ventricular system is normal, with the right atrium measuring 6.1 mm and the left measuring 6.3 mm.

Impression: Normal fetal MRI study showing expected, age-appropriate structural development and sulcation of the brain.

Magnetic resonance imaging of the brain was performed utilizing multiplanar, multisequence protocols. No intra-axial or extra-axial mass lesions, abnormal enhancement, acute ischemia, or hemorrhagic foci are identified. The ventricles and sulci are within normal limits for the patient's age. Paranasal sinuses and mastoid air cells are well-aerated.

Impression: Unremarkable MRI of the brain. No structural, inflammatory, or vascular abnormalities are identified.

Cardiac MRI shows normal heart size and left ventricular wall thickness. Biventricular systolic function is well-preserved with a calculated left ventricular ejection fraction of 64% and right ventricular ejection fraction of 58%. Cine imaging confirms normal synchronous contraction of all segments. No myocardial scar or fibrosis is seen on late gadolinium enhancement images, and there is no evidence of pericardial effusion.

Impression: Unremarkable cardiac MRI. Normal biventricular function and size without diagnostic criteria for ischemic, infiltrative, or inflammatory cardiac disease.

Fetal MRI at 34 weeks gestation demonstrates a normal third-trimester fetus. The sulcation and gyration are appropriate for 34 weeks, with clear visualization of the superior temporal and calcarine sulci. The lateral ventricles are symmetric and measure 5.8 mm at the atrium. The callosal morphology is entirely normal. Fetal lungs show normal T2 hyperintensity and volume, and the diaphragm is intact.

Impression: Normal fetal MRI at 34 weeks gestation, with no evidence of intracranial or somatic abnormalities.

Brain MRI was performed using high-resolution structural sequences. No acute cortical infarcts, intracranial hemorrhages, or mass lesions are observed. The ventricles and subarachnoid spaces are symmetric and age-appropriate. The brainstem and cerebellum are normal in appearance.

Impression: Unremarkable MRI of the brain. No pathological intracranial findings.

Fetal MRI performed at 27 weeks gestation demonstrates a left-sided congenital diaphragmatic hernia. Multiple fluid-filled bowel loops and the stomach are herniated into the left hemithorax, resulting in a prominent shift of the mediastinum and heart to the right. The contralateral right lung is compressed but visible. Fetal brain evaluation shows normal ventricular size (atrial width 5.8 mm) and normal sulcation for 27 weeks.

Impression: Left-sided congenital diaphragmatic hernia with significant mediastinal shift and secondary lung compression. Brain development appears completely normal for gestational age.

High-resolution T2 and contrast-enhanced T1 images of the internal auditory canals reveal a well-circumscribed, enhancing mass centered within the right internal auditory canal and extending into the cerebellopontine angle, measuring 1.4 x 1.1 x 1.0 cm. The mass exhibits a characteristic 'ice cream cone' appearance and causes mild displacement of the adjacent brainstem.

Impression: Right vestibular schwannoma (acoustic neuroma) with intracanalicular and cisternal components. Stable to progressive findings requiring neurotology/neurosurgical follow-up.

Fetal MRI at 29 weeks gestation demonstrates mild bilateral ventriculomegaly. The left lateral ventricular atrium measures 11.2 mm and the right measures 10.8 mm. There is no evidence of intraventricular hemorrhage, periventricular nodular heterotopia, or other developmental anomalies of the forebrain. The corpus callosum is present and normal in size. Fetal brain sulcation (including the central and cingulate sulci) is age-appropriate.

The posterior fossa, spine, lungs, and abdominal organs are within normal limits for 29 weeks. Impression: Mild, bilateral fetal ventriculomegaly without associated structural abnormalities. Routine serial follow-up by ultrasound is recommended.

Cardiac MRI demonstrates marked, asymmetric hypertrophy of the left ventricular myocardium, most prominent in the basal anterior and anteroseptal walls. The maximal wall thickness measures 24 mm in the septum. Dynamic imaging reveals systolic anterior motion (SAM) of the mitral valve, resulting in late-systolic left ventricular outflow tract (LVOT) obstruction with an estimated peak instantaneous gradient of 48 mmHg. Late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) imaging shows focal, patchy enhancement at the right ventricular insertion points.

Impression: Morphological features are highly characteristic of hypertrophic obstructive cardiomyopathy (HOCM) with significant LVOT obstruction. Left ventricular ejection fraction is preserved at 68%.

MR imaging of the brain reveals a large, crescent-shaped, extra-axial fluid collection over the right cerebral hemisphere, measuring up to 1.8 cm in maximum thickness. The collection is hyperintense on both T1 and T2-weighted sequences, indicating a subacute-to-chronic subdural hematoma. There is significant mass effect with compression of the underlying right cerebral cortex, effacement of the right lateral ventricle, and a 7 mm leftward midline shift.

Impression: Large, right-sided subacute-to-chronic subdural hematoma causing significant mass effect and a 7 mm midline shift. Urgent neurosurgical evaluation is indicated.

Fetal MRI at 20 weeks gestation demonstrates early, age-appropriate anatomy. The cerebral hemispheres are relatively smooth, showing expected primary sulcation with initial formation of the sylvian fissures, which is normal for 20 weeks. The lateral ventricles are prominent but within normal range, with the atrium measuring 5.2 mm. Midline structures, including the early corpus callosum, are present.

The fetal heart, lungs, and abdominal organs are in their normal anatomical positions. Spine is intact. Impression: Normal early fetal MRI at 20 weeks gestation with no detectable structural anomalies.

Cardiac magnetic resonance imaging demonstrates normal biventricular volumes and mass. The left ventricular ejection fraction is 63% and the right ventricular ejection fraction is 59%, with symmetric contraction and no regional wall motion abnormalities. Valvular structures are morphologically normal with trace, physiologic regurgitation only. No myocardial edema, delayed enhancement, or perfusion abnormalities are observed.

Impression: Normal cardiac MRI with normal chamber dimensions, biventricular function, and no evidence of myocardial injury, scarring, or infiltration.

Fetal MRI at 23 weeks gestation demonstrates complete absence of both kidneys in the renal fossae. Consistent with bilateral renal agenesis, there is severe anhydramnios resulting in crowding of the fetus. The urinary bladder is not visualized, confirming lack of urine production. The fetal lungs are severely compressed, with volumes significantly below expected values, suggesting early pulmonary hypoplasia. The fetal brain shows normal midline structure and lateral ventricles measuring 5.4 mm.

Impression: Bilateral fetal renal agenesis with severe oligohydramnios/anhydramnios and secondary pulmonary hypoplasia (Potter's sequence) at 23 weeks gestation. Prognosis is extremely poor; prompt multidisciplinary maternal-fetal medicine consultation is indicated.

Cardiac MRI performed for atypical chest pain. Left and right ventricular chambers are normal in size, with normal wall thickness. Left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) is calculated at 62%, and right ventricular ejection fraction (RVEF) is 58%. No regional wall motion abnormalities are identified, and there is no evidence of delayed gadolinium enhancement or acute myocardial edema.

Impression: Unremarkable cardiac MRI study. No evidence of myocardial infarction, scar, active myocarditis, or structural heart disease.

Cardiac MRI demonstrates a focal narrowing of the descending thoracic aorta just distal to the origin of the left subclavian artery, with a minimal luminal diameter of 6.5 mm. Flow quantification reveals a significant peak systolic gradient across the coarctation site estimated at 35 mmHg, with persistent diastolic flow forward. Moderate concentric left ventricular hypertrophy is present (LV mass index 95 g/m²), and there is prominent collateralization via the internal mammary and intercostal arteries.

Impression: Congenital coarctation of the aorta with significant narrowing, significant peak systolic gradient, collateral vascular development, and associated secondary left ventricular hypertrophy.

MRI of the brain demonstrates a crescent-shaped extra-axial fluid collection along the right cerebral hemisphere, measuring up to 1.1 cm in maximum thickness. The collection is hyperintense on both T1 and T2-weighted sequences, indicating a subacute subdural hematoma. There is compression of the underlying cerebral sulci and mild compression of the right lateral ventricle, with a 3 mm leftward midline shift.

Impression: Subacute right-sided subdural hematoma with mild mass effect on the underlying cerebral hemisphere and minor leftward midline shift.

Cardiac MRI reveals significant dilation and dysfunction of the right ventricle (RVEDVI 135 mL/m², ejection fraction 35%). Cine sequences demonstrate regional dyskinesia and microaneurysms within the right ventricular outflow tract and inferior wall. Focal areas of delayed enhancement are observed within the right ventricular free wall.

Impression: Right ventricular structural and functional abnormalities highly suggestive of Arrhythmogenic Right Ventricular Cardiomyopathy (ARVC) based on current diagnostic criteria. Left ventricular size and function are preserved.

Fetal MRI performed at 20 weeks gestation demonstrates normal anatomy. The fetal brain shows appropriate early operculization with smooth cerebral cortex, typical for 20 weeks. The lateral ventricles are symmetric, with the atrium measuring 7.1 mm. The corpus callosum and cerebellar vermis are visible and developmentally normal.

The fetal spine is intact without dorsal defect. The kidneys, stomach, and urinary bladder are visualized and normal. Impression: Normal fetal MRI at 20 weeks gestational age, demonstrating normal early neurodevelopment.

MRI brain reveals a poorly circumscribed, non-enhancing mass in the left frontal lobe white matter, measuring 3.1 x 2.8 cm. The lesion is hyperintense on T2/FLAIR sequences and hypointense on T1-weighted images. There is minimal mass effect with no significant midline shift or surrounding vasogenic edema, and no areas of restricted diffusion are identified on DWI sequences.

Impression: Findings are highly consistent with a low-grade diffuse glioma (such as astrocytoma or oligodendroglioma). Recommend MR spectroscopy and surgical/neurosurgical evaluation for biopsy or resection planning.

Cardiac MRI was performed to evaluate acute onset dyspnea and troponin elevation. T2-weighted and T2-mapping sequences show evidence of elevated signal intensity (myocardial edema) in the mid-to-epicardial segments of the lateral and inferolateral left ventricular wall. Corresponding late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) is observed in a subepicardial, non-coronary distribution within these same lateral wall regions. The LVEF is preserved at 52% with mild localized lateral wall hypokinesia.

Impression: Clinical and imaging findings are highly consistent with acute myocarditis according to updated Lake Louise Criteria. No signs of coronary ischemia are present.

Fetal MRI at 29 weeks gestation demonstrates mild vermian hypoplasia with a prominent, keyhole-shaped fluid space in the posterior fossa, representing a Dandy-Walker variant. The lateral ventricles are at the upper limits of normal, with the atrium measuring 9.5 mm. The cortical sulcation and gyral patterns are within normal limits for 29 weeks.

Impression: Dandy-Walker variant with mild vermian hypoplasia and borderline ventricular dilation. No major supratentorial anomalies.

Cardiac MR study demonstrates normal cardiac chamber dimensions and myocardial thickness. Cine imaging shows normal left ventricular contracting with an ejection fraction of 60% and normal right ventricular contractility with an ejection fraction of 55%. There are no focal regional wall motion abnormalities, valvular dysfunction, or evidence of intra-cavitary thrombi. Myocardial tissue characterization reveals normal native T1 and T2 relaxation times and no late gadolinium enhancement.

Impression: Unremarkable cardiac MRI with normal biventricular volumes and function. No evidence of myocardial inflammation, infiltration, or focal fibrosis.

Cardiac MRI shows normal left ventricular (LV) and right ventricular (RV) volumes, mass, and systolic function. The LVEF is 63% and RVEF is 58% with no localized thinning or wall motion abnormalities. T1 and T2 mapping parameters of the myocardium are within established normal ranges. Multiplanar late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) imaging shows no areas of focal fibrosis, infarction, or scarring.

Impression: Normal cardiac MRI study. There is no evidence of structural myocardial disease, edema, or late gadolinium enhancement.

Brain MRI demonstrates no signal abnormalities in the cerebrum, cerebellum, or brainstem. The ventricular system is normally configured and size-appropriate. No extra-axial fluid collections or signs of intracranial mass effect are present.

Impression: Normal MR study of the brain. No structural or vascular abnormalities visualized.

Fetal MRI at 29 weeks gestation demonstrates bilateral lateral ventriculomegaly. The left atrium measures 11.2 mm and the right measures 10.8 mm, representing mild ventriculomegaly. There is no thinning of the cerebral mantle, and the sulcation is appropriate for 29 weeks, demonstrating early development of the secondary sulci. The third and fourth ventricles are normal in size.

The cerebellum and corpus callosum are fully intact. No other fetal anomalies are identified. Impression: Mild, bilateral, symmetric fetal ventriculomegaly. Recommendation includes follow-up imaging to monitor ventricular size and exclude progressive dilation.

Fetal MRI at 24 weeks gestation reveals severe skeletal dysplasia. There are multiple fractures involving the ribs and long bones, with significant shortening and wrinkling of the femurs. The skull vault is compressible and thin, and the chest is extremely narrow. Intracranial sulcation is normal for gestational age, but skull compression is evident.

Impression: Severe skeletal dysplasia, highly characteristic of Osteogenesis Imperfecta Type II. Given the narrow thorax and severe osseous fragility, the prognosis is extremely poor.

Fetal MRI at 32 weeks gestation shows completely normal fetal brain and somatic anatomy. The cerebral hemispheres display appropriate and well-defined sulcation and operculization patterns for 32 weeks, with prominent central and parieto-occipital sulci. The lateral ventricles are symmetric, with the atrium measuring 6.1 mm on the left and 5.9 mm on the right. Visceral organ situs is normal, and amniotic fluid volume is within normal limits.

Impression: Normal fetal MRI study at 32 weeks gestation, showing appropriate neurodevelopmental landmarks and no structural anomalies.

Cardiac MRI reveals severe, bi-ventricular dilation with global hypokinesis. The left ventricular end-diastolic volume is significantly increased, and the left ventricular ejection fraction is severely reduced at 22%. Right ventricular ejection fraction is also depressed at 31%. Late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) sequences demonstrate a thin, linear band of mid-wall enhancement within the interventricular septum, characteristic of non-ischemic dilated cardiomyopathy.

Impression: Dilated cardiomyopathy with severe biventricular systolic dysfunction and non-ischemic mid-wall fibrosis.

Cardiac MRI demonstrates asymmetric septal hypertrophy of the left ventricle, with a maximum diastolic septal wall thickness of 22 mm at the basal and mid-ventricular levels. There is associated systolic anterior motion (SAM) of the mitral valve leading to moderate mitral regurgitation and a dynamic left ventricular outflow tract (LVOT) obstruction. Late gadolinium enhancement imaging reveals patchy, focal hyperenhancement at the RV-LV insertion points.

Impression: Classic findings of hypertrophic obstructive cardiomyopathy (HOCM) with severe asymmetric septal hypertrophy and dynamic LVOT obstruction. Left ventricular ejection fraction is hyperdynamic at 75%.
