Fetal magnetic resonance imaging at 26 weeks gestation reveals completely normal fetal development. Both cerebral hemispheres show symmetric opercularization of the Sylvian fissures and normal early cortical sulcation. The lateral ventricles are normal, with the left atrium measuring 6.1 mm and the right measuring 6.3 mm.

The posterior fossa, spine, heart, and abdominal organs are completely intact without any detectable morphological anomalies. Impression: Completely unremarkable fetal MRI study demonstrating normal anatomical development for 26 weeks gestation.

The study demonstrates a moderate pericardial effusion measuring up to 18 mm posterior to the left ventricle, without clear features of tamponade such as diastolic right-sided collapse. The pericardial layers appear thickened (measuring 4 mm) and demonstrate late gadolinium hyperenhancement, consistent with active inflammation. Biventricular volumes and systolic function are preserved, with an LVEF of 58%.

Impression: Moderate pericardial effusion with thickened, enhancing pericardial membranes, highly suggestive of acute-on-chronic pericarditis. No overt MRI signs of hemodynamic tamponade.

Fetal MRI at 26 weeks gestation reveals a left-sided congenital diaphragmatic hernia (CDH). The stomach, multiple loops of small bowel, and a portion of the left hepatic lobe are herniated into the left hemithorax. This has resulted in a severe rightward mediastinal shift and compression of the right lung. The observed-to-expected total lung volume is calculated at 32%, indicating severe pulmonary hypoplasia.

Intracranial anatomy is unremarkable, with the lateral ventricles measuring 6.1 mm. Impression: Left-sided congenital diaphragmatic hernia with visceral herniation and severe secondary lung hypoplasia.

The ventricular system is ventriculomegalic out of proportion to the degree of cerebral cortical sulcal widening, particularly involving the lateral and third ventricles. There is narrowing of the sulci along the high parietal convexity and widening of the Sylvian fissures (DESH sign). No aqueductal stenosis is visible.

Impression: Key imaging features characteristic of normal pressure hydrocephalus (NPH). Clinical correlation with gait and cognitive status is suggested.

Fetal MRI at 33 weeks gestation reveals a large right-sided congenital diaphragmatic hernia (CDH). The liver is partially herniated into the right hemithorax along with the gallbladder and loops of the colon. This causes severe leftward mediastinal shift and compression of the left lung. The total fetal lung volume is calculated to be severely reduced. Fetal brain maturation is normal, with complex sulcation for 33 weeks and a normal atrial width of 6.3 mm.

The skeletal system and urinary tract are unremarkable. Impression: Severe right-sided congenital diaphragmatic hernia with liver herniation ('liver-up' CDH) and secondary severe pulmonary hypoplasia. Brain development is age-appropriate.

MRI of the brain demonstrates a well-defined zone of restricted diffusion in the right middle cerebral artery (MCA) territory, specifically involving the right insular cortex and temporal-parietal region. This area shows corresponding low values on the ADC map and hyperintensity on T2/FLAIR sequences, consistent with acute to subacute infarction. There is minimal mass effect and no evidence of hemorrhagic transformation on susceptibility-weighted imaging.

Impression: Acute to subacute ischemic infarction in the right MCA distribution. No evidence of hemorrhage or major mass effect.

MR imaging of the brain is performed using multiplanar, multisequence techniques. Parenchymal signal intensity is normal throughout the brain. No areas of restricted diffusion, intracranial hemorrhage, or abnormal tissue enhancement are observed. The ventricular system, basal cisterns, and cortical sulci are unremarkable for the patient's age.

Impression: Normal MRI of the brain. No acute ischemic stroke, intracranial mass, or significant structural abnormality identified.

Cine MR imaging reveals akinesis of the basal and mid-inferior walls of the left ventricle. Left ventricular systolic function is moderately reduced with an ejection fraction of 39%. Late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) demonstrates a transmural pattern of hyperenhancement involving >75% of the wall thickness in the inferior wall, consistent with a non-viable scar in the posterior descending artery (PDA) territory.

Impression: Non-viable myocardial infarction involving the basal and mid-inferior walls, consistent with a chronic RCA/PDA territory occlusion.

Brain MRI was acquired using multiplanar, multi-echo protocols. Visualized cerebral hemispheres, brainstem, and cerebellum display normal signal characteristics without evidence of acute ischemia, hemorrhage, or mass lesions. The ventricles, cortical sulci, and basal cisterns are within normal anatomical limits for the patient's age. Major vascular flow voids at the skull base are preserved and symmetric.

Visualized orbits, paranasal sinuses, and mastoid air cells are unremarkable. Impression: Unremarkable MRI of the brain with no evidence of structural, infectious, or vascular pathology to explain the patient's chronic headaches.

Fetal MRI at 28 weeks gestation. The fetal brain demonstrates normal development, with appropriate secondary sulcation and opercular development. The ventricles are normal, with symmetric atrial measurements of 6.1 mm. The midline structures, cerebellum, and brainstem are unremarkable.

The fetal spine is intact, and the chest and abdominal organs are within normal limits. Impression: Normal fetal MRI at 28 weeks gestation with no structural abnormalities.

Cardiac MR imaging demonstrates normal biventricular volumes and myocardial mass. The left ventricular ejection fraction is 61%, and the right ventricular ejection fraction is 56%. There is normal segmental wall motion throughout both ventricles. First-pass perfusion and late gadolinium enhancement imaging reveal no perfusion abnormalities or areas of myocardial scarring. Heart valves are structurally normal with physiological flow patterns.

Impression: Normal cardiac MRI study. No diagnostic features of cardiomyopathy, myocardial ischemia, or prior infarct are identified.

Cardiac MRI shows chronic myocardial scarring in the inferior and inferoseptal walls of the left ventricle. Late gadolinium enhancement imaging reveals a trans-mural scar (approaching 85% thickness) extending from the basal to the apical inferior segments, with severe thinning and akinesis of the affected myocardium. Left ventricular ejection fraction is severely reduced at 33%, with an elevated end-diastolic volume index of 115 mL/m2.

Impression: Chronic transmural myocardial infarction in the right coronary artery distribution with associated wall thinning, severe akinesis, and severely reduced left ventricular systolic function (EF 33%).

MR brain imaging reveals a focal area of restricted diffusion in the right middle cerebral artery (MCA) territory, specifically within the right basal ganglia and adjacent posterior limb of the internal capsule. This region exhibits hyperintensity on DWI and corresponding ADC hypointensity, indicating acute cytotoxic edema. Minimal mass effect is exerted on the right lateral ventricle, with no midline shift.

Impression: Acute ischemic infarction within the right MCA territory involving the basal ganglia and internal capsule. No evidence of hemorrhagic transformation on susceptibility-weighted imaging.

MR imaging of the brain was performed following a recent concussive injury. No intra- or extra-axial fluid collections, hematomas, or areas of restricted diffusion are seen. The ventricular system, cortical sulci, and basal cisterns are within normal limits. Susceptibility-weighted sequences (SWI) show no microhemorrhages or evidence of diffuse axonal injury.

Impression: Normal MR imaging of the brain. No structural, traumatic, or hemorrhagic sequelae of head trauma visualized.

MR imaging of the brain reveals a wedge-shaped area of restricted diffusion with corresponding ADC hypointensity involving the cortex and subcortical white matter of the left parietal lobe, consistent with the distribution of the posterior division of the left middle cerebral artery. Faint high signal is visible on T2/FLAIR sequences within this region, representing early gyral edema. No acute intracranial hemorrhage or mass effect is identified.

Impression: Acute ischemic infarction of the left parietal lobe in the left MCA territory. No associated hemorrhagic transformation is visualized.

Fetal brain MRI at 31 weeks gestation demonstrates unilateral ventriculomegaly. The atrium of the left lateral ventricle measures 11.5 mm, representing mild-to-moderate ventriculomegaly, whereas the right lateral ventricle is normal at 6.8 mm. Sulcation and gyration patterns are normal for 31 weeks, showing secondary sulcation in the frontal and parietal lobes. The corpus callosum is intact. No hemorrhage or parenchymal lesions are visualized.

Impression: Mild isolated left-sided fetal ventriculomegaly at 31 weeks gestation. No other structural CNS abnormalities are identified.

Brain MRI demonstrates a crescentic extra-axial fluid collection along the left frontoparietal convexity measuring 1.2 cm in maximal depth. The collection is heterogeneous in signal, displaying high T1 and T2 signals, indicating subacute subdural hematoma. There is resultant effacement of the adjacent cerebral sulci and a 4 mm midline shift to the right. No skull fractures or intra-axial lesions are identified.

Impression: Subacute left frontoparietal subdural hematoma causing mild mass effect and minor midline shift. Close clinical monitoring is advised.

Fetal MRI performed at 28 weeks gestation for parental anxiety. Intracranial structures are normal. The lateral ventricles are symmetric with an atrial width of 6.1 mm. The corpus callosum is intact and fully formed. Cortical sulcation pattern is entirely consistent with a 28-week gestation, showing early development of the secondary sulci. Fetal lungs, liver, and kidneys are unremarkable.

Impression: Structurally normal fetal brain and body at 28 weeks gestation. No anomalies identified.

Cardiac MRI was performed to evaluate a patient with a history of surgical repair for Tetralogy of Fallot in childhood. Cine sequences demonstrate severe right ventricular dilation (RVEDVi 164 mL/m²) with a depressed right ventricular ejection fraction of 38%. The left ventricle is normal in size with a preserved ejection fraction of 55%. High-velocity, turbulent flow is noted across the pulmonary valve.

Phase-contrast flow quantification in the main pulmonary artery demonstrates severe pulmonary regurgitation, with a regurgitant fraction calculated at 46%. There is focal late gadolinium enhancement in the right ventricular outflow tract (RVOT) patch region and at the ventricular septal defect patch margin. Impression: Severe pulmonary regurgitation and right ventricular dilation/dysfunction, typical of late post-repair Tetralogy of Fallot physiology; findings support consideration for pulmonary valve replacement.

Brain MRI demonstrates diffuse, nodular, and linear leptomeningeal enhancement along the basal cisterns, sylvian fissures, and cerebellar folia. There are also several small, non-specific T2/FLAIR hyperintense lesions in the subcortical and deep white matter. Evaluation of the orbits shows mild bilateral enlargement and enhancement of the lacrimal glands.

Impression: Extensive basilar leptomeningeal enhancement, highly suggestive of neurosarcoidosis given the clinical history, though infectious etiologies (such as tuberculous meningitis) must be excluded. Lacrimal gland changes also support a systemic granulomatous process.

Brain MRI demonstrates normal gray-white matter differentiation throughout the cerebral hemispheres. There is no evidence of intra- or extra-axial mass lesions, acute territorial infarctions, or intracranial hemorrhage. The ventricles, sulci, and basal cisterns are within normal limits for the patient's age. The major intracranial arterial flow voids are completely intact and symmetric.

Visualized paranasal sinuses and orbit structures are clear. Impression: Normal brain MRI with no acute structural or vascular abnormalities to explain the patient's symptoms of chronic daily headaches.

MRI of the brain reveals a focus of acute intraparenchymal hemorrhage centered in the left basal ganglia, measuring 2.4 x 2.1 cm. The lesion exhibits characteristic susceptibility artifact on SWI sequences and is surrounded by a narrow rim of vasogenic edema. There is minor compression of the left lateral ventricle but no midline shift.

Impression: Acute left basal ganglia intraparenchymal hemorrhage, most commonly associated with hypertensive microangiopathy. No underlying vascular malformation or tumor is definitively identified.

Brain MRI shows prominent patchy and confluent FLAIR/T2 hyperintensities within the bilateral periventricular and subcortical white matter, sparing the subcortical U-fibers. There is moderate generalized parenchymal volume loss with compensatory dilation of ventricles and sulci, consistent with age. No acute infarct or mass is noted.

Impression: Moderate to severe chronic microvascular ischemic white matter disease. Age-appropriate generalized cerebral atrophy.

Cardiac MRI shows normal ventricular volumes and preserved global systolic function with a left ventricular ejection fraction of 56%. However, there is localized hypokinesis along the mid-lateral wall. Myocardial T2-weighted imaging demonstrates regional hyperintensity in the mid-lateral wall, indicating active myocardial edema. Post-contrast late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) imaging reveals patchy, subepicardial and mid-myocardial enhancement in the same territory.

Impression: Findings are highly characteristic of acute myocarditis involving the mid-lateral wall, meeting the updated Lake Louise criteria with evidence of regional myocardial edema and non-ischemic myocardial injury.

Cardiac MRI demonstrates normal biventricular chamber sizes and wall thicknesses. Left ventricular systolic function is preserved with an ejection fraction of 58%. Right ventricular volume and ejection fraction (55%) are normal for the patient's age. The major cardiac valves demonstrate physiological competence and normal motion. No pericardial effusion is seen.

Myocardial perfusion and late gadolinium enhancement sequences are normal, showing no signs of focal ischemia or scar. Impression: Normal cardiac MRI study. No evidence of myocardial infarction, hypertrophy, or non-ischemic cardiomyopathy.

Magnetic resonance imaging of the brain reveals normal brain parenchyma with preserved gray-white matter differentiation. There is no evidence of acute infarction, hemorrhage, or space-occupying lesions. The ventricles and extra-axial fluid spaces are normal for age. The major intracranial arteries demonstrate normal flow voids without sign of stenosis or aneurysm.

Impression: Unremarkable MRI of the brain. No structural, neoplastic, or vascular intracranial lesion is detected to account for the patient's syncopal episode.

Cardiac MRI shows severe dilation of both the left atrium (volume 120 mL) and the left ventricle (LVEDV 210 mL). Cine sequences demonstrate a flail posterior mitral valve leaflet (P2 segment) with severe prolapse into the left atrium during systole, generating a large, eccentric, retrograde regurgitant jet. Regurgitant volume is calculated at 55 mL, representing severe mitral regurgitation.

The left ventricular ejection fraction remains hyperdynamic at 65%, though this overestimates true forward systemic flow. No LGE is visualized within the myocardium. Impression: Severe degenerative mitral regurgitation secondary to posterior mitral leaflet prolapse/flail, causing marked left atrial and ventricular enlargement.

MRI of the brain was performed under general headache protocol. Structural analysis of both grey and white matter reveals no parenchymal lesions, focal edema, infarcts, or vascular abnormalities. Ventricles are symmetric and typical in size for age. Paranasal sinuses and mastoids are clear.

Impression: Normal MR study of the brain. No evidence of intracranial mass, chronic demyelination, or acute ischemia.

Evaluation of the thoracic aorta demonstrates a focal, severe narrowing of the aortic lumen in the proximal descending aorta, just distal to the origin of the left subclavian artery. The minimum internal diameter at the site of coarctation is 6 mm, with prominent collateral vessels originating from the internal mammary and intercostal arteries. Moderate concentric left ventricular hypertrophy is present (EF 68%).

Impression: Severe focal coarctation of the descending thoracic aorta with significant collateralization and secondary concentric left ventricular hypertrophy.

Fetal MRI at 32 weeks gestation demonstrates that the left kidney is enlarged and replaced by multiple, non-communicating, thin-walled cysts of varying sizes, consistent with a multicystic dysplastic kidney. The contralateral right kidney appears normal in size and position, and there is a normal volume of amniotic fluid. Fetal brain evaluation is normal, with an atrial width of 6.2 mm and normal sulcation.

Impression: Left multicystic dysplastic kidney with a normal, functioning right kidney and normal amniotic fluid volume. Fetal intracranial structures are normal.

Cardiac MRI shows normal heart anatomy with biventricular volumes and mass indexing well within the reference ranges for age and sex. The left ventricular ejection fraction is 64%, and the right ventricular ejection fraction is 59%. There is no focal or regional myocardial thinning, wall motion abnormality, or myocardial edema. Late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) is negative throughout the ventricles.

Impression: Completely normal cardiac MRI. No evidence of structural heart disease, ischemia, infarction, or non-ischemic myocardial scarring.

MRI of the brain demonstrates a crescentic, extra-axial fluid collection overlying the right cerebral hemisphere, measuring up to 1.8 cm in maximal thickness. The collection is heterogeneously hyperintense on T1 and T2 sequences, indicating a subacute to chronic subdural hematoma with areas of rebleeding. There is significant mass effect with effacement of the right hemispheric sulci, partial collapse of the right lateral ventricle, and an 8 mm leftward midline shift.

Impression: Large subacute-on-chronic right subdural hematoma causing significant mass effect and an 8 mm midline shift. Urgent neurosurgical evaluation is recommended.

Brain MRI demonstrates a large crescentic extra-axial fluid collection over the right cerebral hemisphere, measuring 1.6 cm in maximum width. The collection is T1 and T2 hyperintense, consistent with a chronic subdural hematoma with areas of internal septation and potential subacute rebleeding. There is associated mass effect, with effacement of the right hemispheric sulci and a 5 mm leftward midline shift.

Impression: Large chronic to subacute subdural hematoma over the right cerebral hemisphere, causing moderate mass effect and a 5 mm midline shift. Neurosurgical evaluation is recommended.

MR imaging of the brain demonstrates caudal herniation of the cerebellar tonsils through the foramen magnum by 8 mm, showing a peg-like configuration. There is partial effacement of the cisterna magna. The visualized cervical cord shows a small, non-expansile, fluid-filled cavity (syrinx) extending from C2 to C4. The ventricles are normal in size and position.

Impression: Chiari I malformation with cerebellar tonsillar ectopia of 8 mm, accompanied by a small cervical syrinx. Neurovascular follow-up is recommended.

The mitral valve leaflets are thickened with evidence of myxomatous degeneration. There is a flail of the posterior mitral valve leaflet (P2 segment) into the left atrium during systole, resulting in a large, eccentric regurgitant jet. The left atrium is severely dilated (volume index 65 mL/m²). The left ventricle is also dilated with an LVEDVI of 118 mL/m² and hyperdynamic systolic function (LVEF 68%).

Impression: Severe mitral regurgitation secondary to posterior leaflet flail, with associated severe left atrial dilation and left ventricular volume overload remodeling.

Fetal MRI at 28 weeks gestation demonstrates completely normal fetal intracranial anatomy. The cerebral hemispheres are symmetric, with appropriate parieto-occipital, calcarine, and cingulate sulcation for gestational age. The ventricular system is normal, with the atrial width of the lateral ventricles measuring 5.9 mm on the left and 6.0 mm on the right.

The corpus callosum is intact and normal in thickness. The posterior fossa structures, including the cerebellar vermis and brainstem, are unremarkable. Impression: Normal fetal brain MRI at 28 weeks gestation showing age-appropriate structural and cortical development.

Fetal MRI at 33 weeks gestation demonstrates a left-sided congenital diaphragmatic hernia (CDH). The stomach, left lobe of the liver, and multiple loops of bowel are herniated into the left hemithorax, causing severe rightward mediastinal shift. The left lung is severely compressed and hypoplastic. The right lung is moderately hypoplastic. Total lung volume calculation indicates significant reduction below predicted values for 33 weeks.

No intracranial anomalies are identified. Impression: Left-sided congenital diaphragmatic hernia with severe pulmonary hypoplasia. Liver-up herniation noted. Recommend immediate referral to a high-risk delivery and neonatal surgery center.

Fetal MRI at 30 weeks gestation reveals a large left-sided congenital diaphragmatic hernia (CDH). The stomach bubble and multiple loops of small bowel have herniated into the left hemithorax, resulting in a severe mass effect that shifts the mediastinum to the right. The left lung is compressed and severely hypoplastic, showing minimal T2-weighted signal, while the right lung is moderately compressed.

The fetal brain is structurally intact with appropriate opercular development and sulcation for 30 weeks. The lateral ventricles measure 6.0 mm. Impression: Left-sided congenital diaphragmatic hernia with significant mediastinal shift and severe left-sided lung hypoplasia.

Cardiac MRI demonstrates a congenitally bicuspid aortic valve with fusion of the left and right coronary cusps and calcified margins. There is severe restriction of valve opening during systole, with a planimetered aortic valve area of 0.8 cm². Phase-contrast imaging across the aortic valve demonstrates a peak systolic velocity of 4.2 m/s, consistent with severe aortic stenosis.

Secondary concentric left ventricular hypertrophy is noted, with a septal thickness of 15 mm, but global systolic function remains preserved (EF 59%). There is mild post-stenotic dilation of the ascending aorta, measuring 4.2 cm. Impression: Bicuspid aortic valve with severe aortic stenosis, post-stenotic ascending aortic dilation, and secondary concentric left ventricular hypertrophy.

Cardiac MRI shows normal ventricular volumes with preserved left ventricular ejection fraction at 55%. There is evidence of localized subepicardial and mid-wall late gadolinium enhancement within the basal to mid-lateral left ventricular wall. T2-weighted imaging demonstrates matching areas of high signal intensity in the same regions, indicating active myocardial edema.

Impression: Findings are highly consistent with acute myocarditis, characterized by subepicardial/mid-wall fibrosis and active myocardial edema in the lateral wall.

MR brain imaging reveals multiple punctate foci of susceptibility blooming on SWI sequences scattered throughout the lobar cerebral cortex and subcortical white matter, particularly in the parietal and occipital lobes. There is relative sparing of the basal ganglia, thalamus, and brainstem. Moderate periventricular white matter hyperintensity of presumed microvascular ischemic origin is also present.

Impression: Multiple lobar microbleeds, highly characteristic of cerebral amyloid angiopathy (CAA) in an elderly patient. Concurrent moderate chronic small vessel ischemic changes are noted.

Brain MRI performed for evaluation of chronic migraines. Multiplanar, multisequence brain imaging demonstrates symmetric brain parenchyma with no areas of restricted diffusion, abnormal susceptibility artifact, or pathological enhancement. Ventricles, sulci, and cisterns are within normal limits for patient age. Major intracranial arterial structures show intact flow voids.

Impression: Unremarkable MRI of the brain. No structural abnormality, acute ischemic change, or abnormal enhancement to explain the patient's migraine symptoms.

Fetal MRI at 25 weeks gestation demonstrates age-appropriate intracranial and extracranial structures. The cerebral cortex shows normal early sulcation, with the development of the cingulate and calcarine sulci visible and appropriate for 25 weeks. The lateral ventricles are symmetric, with the atrium measuring 5.5 mm. The posterior fossa, brainstem, and corpus callosum are normal.

Fetal organs within the chest and abdomen are well-visualized and show no abnormalities. Impression: Unremarkable fetal MRI study at 25 weeks gestation, showing completely normal structural development.

Fetal MRI at 28 weeks gestation demonstrates normal intracranial and systemic anatomy. Brain biometry is appropriate, and lateral ventricles measure 5.8 mm. Cerebral sulcation and gyration patterns show normal progression with visible sylvian, parieto-occipital, and cingulate sulci. The corpus callosum and posterior fossa structures are normal.

No chest, abdominal, or skeletal abnormalities are identified. Amniotic fluid volume and placental appearance are unremarkable. Impression: Unremarkable fetal MRI at 28 weeks gestation showing normal development.

Fetal MRI at 25 weeks gestation demonstrates posterior fossa anomalies. There is severe hypoplasia of the cerebellar vermis with rotation of the vermian remnant. The posterior fossa is enlarged, with a dilated CSF space representing a giant retrocerebellar fluid collection communicating directly with the fourth ventricle. Lateral ventricles are mildly dilated at 10.2 mm bilaterally.

No supratentorial anomalies or migration defects are detected. Impression: Findings are highly characteristic of Dandy-Walker malformation with secondary mild ventriculomegaly. Recommend prenatal pediatric neurology consultation.

Fetal MRI at 28 weeks gestation demonstrates a Dandy-Walker variant. The inferior cerebellar vermis is mildly hypoplastic, resulting in a visible communication between the fourth ventricle and the retrocerebellar fluid space, creating a characteristic keyhole appearance. The posterior fossa is not significantly enlarged. The lateral ventricular atria measure 10.2 mm, indicating borderline/mild ventriculomegaly. Cortical sulcation is appropriate for 28 weeks.

Impression: Cerebellar vermian hypoplasia consistent with Dandy-Walker variant, accompanied by borderline/mild ventriculomegaly.

Fetal MRI at 29 weeks gestation demonstrates a large left-sided congenital diaphragmatic hernia. Multiple loops of herniated fetal small bowel and the fetal stomach are located within the left hemithorax, causing a significant rightward mediastinal shift. The left lung is severely compressed and hypoplastic, with the measured lung volume significantly below the 5th percentile for gestational age. The right lung appears mildly compressed but otherwise intact.

Impression: Left-sided congenital diaphragmatic hernia (CDH) with intrathoracic stomach, severe left lung hypoplasia, and prominent mediastinal shift.

MRI demonstrates an ill-defined, non-enhancing, T2/FLAIR hyperintense infiltrative lesion centered within the left frontal lobe, measuring approximately 3.2 x 2.8 cm. The lesion shows minimal mass effect, with slight effacement of the surrounding cortical sulci but no significant compression of the lateral ventricle or midline shift. No necrotic areas or pathologically restricted diffusion are observed.

Impression: Non-enhancing low-grade infiltrative glial neoplasm, most consistent with an astrocytoma. Biopsy or interval MRI monitoring is recommended to determine histopathological type.

Cardiac MRI demonstrates a normal-sized left ventricle with mild global systolic dysfunction and a calculated ejection fraction of 52%. Elevated myocardial T2 relaxation times and increased signal intensity on T2-weighted imaging are noted in the subepicardial regions of the basal and mid-ventricular inferolateral walls. Late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) imaging confirms patchy epicardial-to-midwall hyperenhancement in these same segments, confirming active inflammatory change.

Impression: Features of acute post-viral myocarditis with active myocardial edema and subepicardial fibrosis of the inferolateral wall, associated with mild global LV dysfunction.

Cardiac MRI demonstrates diffuse, symmetric thickening of the left ventricular myocardium (interventricular septum measures 18 mm) and moderate thickening of the right ventricular free wall and interatrial septum. The left ventricular ejection fraction is mildly reduced at 45%. Post-contrast imaging demonstrates a highly characteristic pattern of diffuse, subendocardial late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) that does not conform to a coronary territory.

Impression: Morphological and contrast kinetics findings are highly characteristic of cardiac amyloidosis.

Fetal MRI at 22 weeks gestation demonstrates a classic Dandy-Walker malformation. There is severe hypoplasia of the cerebellar vermis with a markedly enlarged posterior fossa and high tentorial insertion. The fourth ventricle communicates freely with the retrocerebellar cerebrospinal fluid space. The lateral ventricles are within normal limits with an atrial width of 8.5 mm. Sulcation is appropriate for early gestational age.

Impression: Fetal Dandy-Walker malformation. The cerebral cortex and supratentorial structures show normal developmental progress, but severe cerebellar vermian dysgenesis is noted.

MRI of the brain demonstrates normal anatomical structure. The cerebral ventricles and sulci are slightly prominent, consistent with mild age-related brain atrophy, but are symmetric. There is no evidence of focal parenchymal lesions, acute ischemia, hemorrhage, or abnormal enhancement. Cranial nerve pathways are preserved, and the internal auditory canals are symmetric and normal.

Impression: Mild age-related cerebral atrophy. No acute brain pathology or structural lesions to explain the patient's dizziness or balance issues.

Fetal MRI at 31 weeks gestation demonstrates bilateral, symmetric ventriculomegaly. The lateral ventricular atria measure 12.8 mm on the left and 12.5 mm on the right, classifying this as moderate ventriculomegaly. The third ventricle is minimally prominent, but the aqueduct of Sylvius is poorly visualized. The cerebral cortex demonstrates age-appropriate sulcation patterns, and the corpus callosum is intact.

No other intracranial masses, hemorrhages, or destructive lesions are identified. The fetal body demonstrates normal morphology. Impression: Moderate, symmetric bilateral fetal ventriculomegaly without associated structural anomalies. Suggest clinical follow-up and TORCH screening.

Fetal MRI at 22 weeks gestation shows hypoplasia of the cerebellar vermis with a moderately enlarged posterior fossa CSF space, suggestive of a Dandy-Walker variant. The tentorium cerebelli and torcular are elevated. The lateral ventricles are within normal limits, measuring 8.5 mm. Sulcation and early migration patterns are consistent with 22 weeks.

Impression: Posterior fossa malformation consistent with a Dandy-Walker variant. Follow-up imaging is recommended to monitor for progressive ventriculomegaly.

Magnetic resonance imaging of the brain shows a well-defined area of restricted diffusion in the left middle cerebral artery (MCA) territory, characterized by bright signal on diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI) and corresponding low signal on the apparent diffusion coefficient (ADC) map. This region spans the left insula, adjacent frontal operculum, and deep basal ganglia, accompanied by subtle localized gyral swelling and loss of sulcal definition on T2-FLAIR sequences. Magnetic resonance angiography (MRA) demonstrates abrupt occlusion of the M2 segment of the left MCA.

Impression: Acute ischemic infarction in the left middle cerebral artery distribution. Intracranial MRA reveals occlusion of the left M2 branch, requiring immediate clinical correlation and stroke management.

MR imaging of the brain reveals an incidental, well-circumscribed extra-axial fluid collection in the left anterior temporal fossa, measuring 3.5 x 2.2 cm. The fluid completely follows cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) signal on all pulse sequences and shows no enhancement or restricted diffusion. There is mild remodeling of the adjacent sphenoid bone wing but no mass effect on the temporal lobe.

Impression: Left anterior temporal fossa arachnoid cyst (Galassi Type I). This is a benign, incidental finding requiring no acute intervention.

Cardiac MRI demonstrates subendocardial late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) in the basal to mid-inferior wall, extending to approximately 25-50% wall thickness, consistent with a prior non-transmural myocardial infarction in the right coronary artery (RCA) territory. There is mild hypokinesis of the corresponding segments. The left ventricular ejection fraction is mildly reduced at 48%, with an end-diastolic volume of 155 mL.

Impression: Subendocardial myocardial infarction in the RCA territory with viable myocardium remaining in the epicardial portion of the affected inferior wall. Mildly reduced global LV systolic function.

Cardiac MRI performed to rule out structural anomalies or ischemia. The left ventricular end-diastolic volume index is 74 mL/m2, within normal limits. Normal cardiac chambers, valvular apparatus, and great vessel morphology are visualized. No areas of myocardial edema, hyperenhancement on late gadolinium sequences, or abnormal perfusion are noted.

Impression: Normal cardiac MRI study. Normal biventricular volumes and systolic performance with a calculated left ventricular ejection fraction of 60%.

Fetal MRI at 25 weeks gestation reveals severe skeletal dysplasia. There is marked micromelia involving all extremities, associated with bowing of the long bones. The thoracic cage is highly constricted and narrow, displaying a classic 'bell-shaped' configuration consistent with thanatophoric dysplasia.

The skull demonstrates a slightly trilobed ('cloverleaf') appearance. The intracranial ventricles are normal, with the atrium measuring 6.0 mm, and the sulcation is appropriate. Impression: Severe micromelic skeletal dysplasia with thoracic constriction, highly suggestive of thanatophoric dysplasia.

MR brain imaging reveals a well-demarcated, extra-axial mass arising from the left parietal dural convexity, measuring approximately 3.2 x 3.0 x 2.8 cm. The lesion is homogeneously hyperintense to gray matter on T2-weighted images and demonstrates intense, uniform enhancement following contrast administration, with a prominent 'dural tail' sign. There is mild localized compression of the adjacent cerebral cortex and minimal surrounding parenchymal edema.

Impression: Left parietal extra-axial dural-based mass, characteristic of a benign meningioma. There is mild mass effect on the underlying brain parenchyma without significant edema or midline shift.

The study reveals normal chamber sizes with a mildly reduced left ventricular ejection fraction of 52%. T2-weighted STIR sequences demonstrate patchy hyperintensity in the subepicardium of the lateral and inferolateral walls, consistent with active myocardial edema. Post-contrast late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) confirms matching subepicardial and mid-myocardial enhancement in the same regions without subendocardial involvement.

Impression: Findings are highly consistent with acute myocarditis, demonstrating edema and myocardial injury following a classic non-ischemic pattern. Clinical correlation with electrocardiographic changes and inflammatory markers is recommended.

Multiplanar, multisequence cardiac MRI demonstrates normal biventricular dimensions, wall thickness, and contractile function. The left ventricular ejection fraction is 61% and the right ventricular ejection fraction is 59%. There is no evidence of regional wall motion abnormality, focal myocardial edema, or pathological tissue T1/T2 elongation.

Post-contrast sequences show no late gadolinium enhancement in either the ventricles or atria, confirming absence of focal myocardial fibrosis. Impression: Normal cardiac MRI study. No structural or functional cardiac abnormalities identified.

High-resolution MRI of the internal auditory canals (IACs) and brain was performed. The brain parenchyma is normal. Bilateral vestibulocochlear and facial nerves are well-visualized within the IACs, without asymmetry, thickening, or abnormal enhancement. The cerebellopontine angle cisterns are clear.

Impression: Normal MRI of the brain and internal auditory canals. No evidence of vestibular schwannoma or other mass lesions in the cerebellopontine angle to account for unilateral hearing loss.

Fetal MRI at 24 weeks gestation shows a large left-sided congenital diaphragmatic hernia. There is herniation of the stomach, multiple loops of small bowel, and a portion of the left lobe of the liver into the left hemithorax. This causes significant rightward mediastinal shift and compression of the heart and the contralateral lung. The total fetal lung volume is severely reduced, measured at 0.45 observed-to-expected ratio.

Impression: Left-sided congenital diaphragmatic hernia with liver herniation and significant mass effect on mediastinal structures. Findings carry high risk for severe postnatal pulmonary hypoplasia.

Fetal MRI at 27 weeks gestation demonstrates severe shortening of all visualized long bones, particularly the humeri and femora, indicative of micromelia. The thoracic cavity is severely narrowed and bell-shaped, with compressed lungs. The fetal skull is mildly enlarged with a prominent frontal bone. The lateral ventricles and brain anatomy are within normal limits for 27 weeks, with the ventricles measuring 6.0 mm at the atrium.

Impression: Fetal skeletal dysplasia, most consistent with a lethal form such as thanatophoric dysplasia, given the severe micromelia and bell-shaped chest. Genetic counseling is advised.

Fetal MRI at 27 weeks gestation demonstrates a single fetus in transverse lie. The cerebral cortex shows normal early sulcation, with well-formed parieto-occipital and cingulate sulci for gestational age. The lateral ventricles are completely normal and symmetric, with the atrium measuring 6.3 mm. The posterior fossa and brainstem are unremarkable.

Thoracic and abdominal anatomy is normal, with normal lung signal intensity and symmetric renal anatomy. Impression: Unremarkable fetal MRI at 27 weeks gestation, showing completely normal fetal development.

Fetal MRI at 30 weeks gestation demonstrates partial agenesis of the corpus callosum. The anterior body and genu are present, but the posterior body and splenium are absent. There is mild dilatation of the posterior horns of the lateral ventricles (atrial measurement 10.1 mm), typical of colpocephaly. The parenchymal migration and gyral structures are otherwise normal.

Impression: Partial agenesis of the corpus callosum with associated mild colpocephaly. No other congenital anomalies visualized.

All cardiac chambers show normal size and volume measurements. Ventricular contractility is symmetric and globally preserved with a left ventricular ejection fraction of 62% and a right ventricular ejection fraction of 55%. Myocardial perfusion imaging is symmetric and homogeneous, and late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) is negative throughout all segments of the myocardium.

Impression: Unremarkable cardiac MRI showing normal chamber volumes, intact global/regional contractility, and no evidence of focal myocardial scar or active inflammation.

Images demonstrate a large secundum-type atrial septal defect (ASD) in the mid-atrial septum, measuring 2.4 cm in diameter. Phase-contrast flow quantification indicates a significant left-to-right shunt with a Qp:Qs ratio of 2.1:1. The right atrium and right ventricle are severely dilated, demonstrating right ventricular volume overload. Right ventricular ejection fraction is 50%.

Impression: Large secundum atrial septal defect with a hemodynamically significant left-to-right shunt and resulting right heart volume overload. Surgical or percutaneous closure is indicated based on current guidelines.

Cardiac MRI reveals normal left and right ventricular chamber volumes and preserved systolic function. The left ventricular ejection fraction is 64%, and the right ventricular ejection fraction is 58%, without regional wall motion abnormalities. Valve structure and motion are unremarkable, with normal flow dynamics across the mitral, aortic, tricuspid, and pulmonary valves. No late gadolinium enhancement or abnormal T1/T2 myocardial signal is detected.

Impression: Completely normal cardiac MRI study. There is no evidence of cardiomyopathy, myocardial scar, inflammation, or structural heart disease.

Fetal MRI evaluated at 29 weeks gestation demonstrates marked asymmetry and dilation of the fetal ventricular system. The left lateral ventricle atrium is dilated and measures approximately 13.5 mm, consistent with moderate ventriculomegaly, whereas the right lateral ventricle atrium measures 10.2 mm. Cerebral sulcation and gyral migration patterns are otherwise appropriate for 29 weeks, and the midline corpus callosum appears intact.

No other intracranial masses, hemorrhages, or destructive lesions are visualized. Impression: Moderate asymmetric fetal ventriculomegaly, predominantly affecting the left lateral ventricle. Follow-up imaging and postnatal clinical correlation are recommended.

Brain MRI shows normal cranial anatomy. Ventricular and sulcal patterns are preserved. There is no evidence of intracranial hemorrhage, ischemic stroke, mass effect, or abnormal enhancement. The extra-axial CSF spaces are within normal limits and the pituitary gland is unremarkable.

Impression: Unremarkable MRI of the brain. No structural, inflammatory, or demyelinating pathology observed.

MR examination of the brain and craniocervical junction shows caudal herniation of the cerebellar tonsils through the foramen magnum by approximately 8 mm. The tonsils appear pointed and peg-like. There is associated crowding of the craniocervical junction with partial effacement of the surrounding CSF spaces. Visualized upper cervical spinal cord is normal in signal, and no syrinx is identified on the sagittal sequences. Cerebral parenchyma is otherwise unremarkable.

Impression: Chiari I malformation with 8 mm tonsillar descent and local cisternal crowding. No evidence of cervical syringomyelia.

MRI of the brain was performed to evaluate persistent non-specific dizziness. Imaging demonstrates normal intracranial architecture. The ventricular system, basal cisterns, and subarachnoid spaces are normal. There is no evidence of acute ischemia, hemorrhage, demyelinating disease, or mass lesions. The internal auditory canals are symmetric and clear.

Impression: Unremarkable MRI of the brain. No structural anomalies or internal auditory canal pathologies detected.

Cardiac MRI demonstrates diffuse, symmetrical concentric thickening of the left ventricular myocardium (wall thickness up to 1.8 cm) and biatrial enlargement. T1 mapping reveals significantly elevated native T1 values, and extracellular volume (ECV) fraction is calculated at 48% (normal <28%). There is diffuse, subendocardial late gadolinium enhancement across the entire left ventricle, along with difficulties achieving optimal myocardial nulling on scout sequences.

Impression: Classical features of cardiac amyloidosis with severe concentric hypertrophy, diffuse subendocardial LGE, and significantly increased extracellular volume. Mildly reduced LVEF at 45% with restrictive physiology.

Study was performed to rule out infiltrative myocardial disease in a patient presenting with conduction blocks. Ventricular wall thicknesses, chamber volumes, and biventricular systolic functions are completely normal (LVEF 62%, RVEF 59%). Myocardial T1 and T2 mapping parameters are within normal reference ranges. Late gadolinium enhancement imaging is entirely negative for any focal or diffuse myocardial enhancement.

Impression: Unremarkable cardiac MRI. No evidence of infiltrative myocardial disease, myocardial scar, or structural cardiac pathology to explain the patient's conduction block.

Cardiac MRI evaluated a 32-year-old female presenting with progressive dyspnea. There is a large defect in the mid-interatrial septum measuring approximately 2.2 cm, consistent with a secundum-type atrial septal defect (ASD). Phase-contrast flow quantification reveals a significant left-to-right shunt with a Qp/Qs ratio calculated at 2.1. Right ventricular and right atrial dilation are noted (RVEDV index of 115 mL/m²), indicating right-sided volume overload.

Impression: Large secundum atrial septal defect (ASD) with a hemodynamically significant left-to-right shunt (Qp/Qs = 2.1). Consequent dilation of the right atrium and right ventricle is present, though biventricular systolic function remains preserved.

Fetal MRI at 26 weeks gestation demonstrates a large multicystic dysplastic left kidney (MCDK). The left kidney is markedly enlarged and replaced by multiple, non-communicating, varying-sized cysts with no recognizable normal renal parenchyma. The contralateral right kidney appears normal in size and signal with normal corticomedullary differentiation. Amniotic fluid volume is within the normal range.

The fetal brain demonstrates normal sulcul pattern and ventricles (atrial measurement 6.0 mm). Impression: Left multicystic dysplastic kidney. The right kidney is normal, and amniotic fluid volume is preserved, suggesting adequate overall renal function at this stage.

MR brain imaging reveals a non-enhancing, well-defined mass within the left frontal lobe cortex and subcortical white matter, measuring approximately 2.8 x 2.4 x 2.1 cm. The lesion is hyperintense on T2/FLAIR and hypointense on T1-weighted sequences, with no restriction on diffusion imaging and no surrounding vasogenic edema.

Impression: Non-enhancing cortical and subcortical left frontal lobe mass, highly suggestive of a low-grade glioma (e.g., astrocytoma or oligodendroglioma). No secondary mass effect is seen.

Fetal MRI at 28 weeks gestation demonstrates significant dilation of the lateral ventricles. The left lateral ventricular atrium measures 14.8 mm and the right lateral ventricular atrium measures 15.2 mm, indicating bilateral severe ventriculomegaly. There is associated thinning of the surrounding white matter. The sulcation and gyration patterns are mildly delayed for 28 weeks, but the major lobar clefts and sylvian fissure are visible. The corpus callosum is present but thinned and stretched superiorly.

The posterior fossa and remainder of the fetal intracranial structures appear stable. Impression: Bilateral severe fetal ventriculomegaly with mild delay in age-appropriate cortical sulcation. No overt intracranial hemorrhage or posterior fossa malformation is identified.

Cardiac MRI demonstrates a small, restrictive ventricular septal defect located in the muscular portion of the mid-septum, measuring 4 mm in diameter. Shunt flow quantification indicates a minor left-to-right shunt with a Qp:Qs of 1.15. The left and right ventricular volumes, wall thicknesses, and global systolic functions are completely normal (LVEF 63%).

Impression: Small, hemodynamically insignificant muscular ventricular septal defect with a trivial left-to-right shunt and normal chamber dimensions.

MRI of the brain was performed with attention to the internal auditory canals (IACs). Brain parenchyma demonstrates normal signal intensity and architecture throughout. No CPA cistern masses, vascular compression of cranial nerves, or IAC abnormalities are identified. Ventricles and sulci are entirely normal for age.

Impression: Unremarkable brain and internal auditory canal MRI. No structural abnormality, mass, or demyelinating process identified to account for the patient's acute vertigo.

Fetal MRI at 22 weeks gestation reveals complete absence of the corpus callosum. The lateral ventricles show classic colpocephaly, with tear-drop configuration and prominent enlargement of the posterior horns. The left ventricular atrium measures 11.2 mm and the right measures 11.5 mm. Radial arrangement of the sulci (radiating from the third ventricle roof) is observed along the medial hemispheric walls, typical for callosal agenesis at this gestational phase. Third ventricle is moderately dilated and displaced superiorly.

All other fetal anatomical structures, including the spine, abdomen, and thorax, demonstrate no major anomalies. Impression: Complete agenesis of the corpus callosum with associated mild colpocephaly. No other midline defects are visualized.

Fetal MRI at 22 weeks gestation demonstrates a midline defect in the occipital bone. There is a herniated sac measuring approximately 2.1 x 1.8 cm containing cerebral spinal fluid and dysplastic cerebellar tissue, consistent with an occipital encephalocele. The remaining intracranial structures show distortion, with a mildly pulled and elongated brainstem. The lateral ventricles are within normal limits (7.0 mm).

Impression: Occipital encephalocele containing dysplastic neural and meningeal elements, with associated posterior brain stem distortion.

Fetal MRI at 26 weeks gestation reveals a hypoplastic cerebellar vermis and mildly reduced size of the cerebellar hemispheres. There is a prominent fluid collection in the posterior fossa that does not cause mass effect or elevation of the tentorium, suggesting a Dandy-Walker variant or mega cisterna magna. The lateral ventricular atria measure 8.8 mm.

Cerebral sulcation is appropriate for a 26-week fetus. Fetal spine and viscera are normal. Impression: Cerebellar vermian hypoplasia/Dandy-Walker variant. Genetic counseling and follow-up MRI are recommended.

Fetal MRI at 28 weeks gestation demonstrates a large cystic fluid collection in the posterior fossa that communicates with an enlarged fourth ventricle. The cerebellar vermis is hypoplastic and rotated superiorly. There is elevation of the torcula and tentorium, resulting in an overall enlarged posterior fossa. The lateral ventricles are moderately dilated, with the right atrium measuring 12.2 mm and the left measuring 11.8 mm.

Cortical sulcation matches the expected pattern for 28 weeks. The fetal chest and abdomen are unremarkable. Impression: Dandy-Walker malformation with secondary ventriculomegaly. Pediatric neurosurgery and genetic counseling are recommended.

Cardiac MR shows marked, symmetric thickening of the left ventricular walls (18 mm) and the interatrial septum, accompanied by a small circumferential pericardial effusion. Late gadolinium enhancement imaging demonstrates diffuse, subendocardial hyperenhancement of both the left and right ventricles, along with a highly characteristic abnormal myocardial nulling pattern on look-locker scout sequences, where the blood pool and myocardium null simultaneously. Left ventricular ejection fraction is moderately reduced at 42%.

Impression: Findings are classic and highly suggestive of cardiac amyloidosis, characterized by severe concentric hypertrophy, diffuse subendocardial LGE, abnormal nulling patterns, and moderate systolic dysfunction.
